Bounding the Smallest Singular Value of a Random Matrix Without Concentration
abstract: Given a random vector <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex>, set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_1,\ldots ,X_N$</tex> to be independent copies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ={1 \over \sqrt {N}}\sum _{i=1}^N \langle X_i,\cdot \rangle e_i$</tex> be the matrix whose rows are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${X_1 \over \sqrt {N}},\ldots , {X_N \over \sqrt {N}}$</tex>. We obtain new probabilistic lower bounds on the smallest singular value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{\min }(\Gamma )$</tex> in a rather general situation, and in particular, under the assumption that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is an isotropic random vector for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sup _{t\in S^{n-1}}{\BBP}\{|\langle t,X \rangle | \geq u\} \leq L/u^{2+\eta }$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L,\eta \gt 0$</tex>. Our results imply that a Bai–Yin-type lower bound holds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta \gt 2$</tex>, and, up to a log-factor, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta =2$</tex> as well. The bounds hold without any additional assumptions on the Euclidean norm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|X\|_{\ell _2^n}$</tex>. Moreover, we establish a nontrivial lower bound even without any higher moment assumptions (corresponding to the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta =0$</tex>), if the linear forms satisfy a weak “small-ball” property. These estimates follow from general lower bounds on the infimum of the quadratic empirical process <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \to N^{-1}\sum _{i=1}^N f^2(X_i)$</tex> which are of independent interest.

articleTitle: Small Ball Probabilities for Linear Images of High-Dimensional Distributions
abstract: We study concentration properties of random vectors of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AX$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X = (X_1,\ldots , X_n)$</tex> has independent coordinates and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is a given matrix. We show that the distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AX$</tex> is well spread in space whenever the distributions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_i$</tex> are well spread on the line. Specifically, assume that the probability that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_i$</tex> falls in any given interval of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. Then the probability that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AX$</tex> falls in any given ball of radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \|A\|_{\rm {HS}}$</tex> is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Cp)^{0.9 r(A)}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r(A)$</tex> denotes the stable rank of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> is an absolute constant.

articleTitle: Operator-Valued Free Multiplicative Convolution: Analytic Subordination Theory and Applications to Random Matrix Theory
abstract: We give an explicit description, via analytic subordination, of free multiplicative convolution of operator-valued distributions. In particular, the subordination function is obtained from an iteration process. This algorithm is easily numerically implementable. We present two concrete applications of our method: the product of two free operator-valued semicircular elements and the calculation of the distribution of dcd+d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>cd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for scalar-valued c and d, which are free. Comparison between the solution obtained by our methods and simulations of random matrices shows excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Local Universality of Zeroes of Random Polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we establish some local universality results concerning the correlation functions of the zeroes of random polynomials with independent coefficients. More precisely, consider two random polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f =\sum _{i=1}^n c_i \xi _i z^i$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {f} =\sum _{i=1}^n c_i \tilde {\xi }_i z^i$</tex>, where the ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {\xi }_i$</tex> are iid random variables that match moments to second order, the coefficients c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> are deterministic, and the degree parameter n is large. Our results show, under some light conditions on the coefficients c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and the tails of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi _i, \tilde {\xi }_i$</tex>, that the correlation functions of the zeroes of f and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {f}$</tex> are approximately the same. As an application, we give some answers to the classical question How many zeroes of a random polynomials are real? for several classes of random polynomial models. Our analysis relies on a general replacement principle, motivated by some recent work in random matrix theory. This principle enables one to compare the correlation functions of two random functions f and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {f}$</tex> if their log magnitudes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log |f|, \log |\tilde {f}|$</tex> are close in distribution, and if some nonconcentration bounds are obeyed.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Behavior of Least Energy Solutions for a Critical Elliptic System
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of positive least energy solutions to a two coupled elliptic system with Sobolev critical exponents. This system is related to coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations with critical exponents for Bose–Einstein condensates, and can be also seen as a counterpart of the classical Brézis–Nirenberg problem. There are three kinds of asymptotic behaviors for positive solutions of two coupled systems: (i) both two components converge; (ii) one component converges while the other one blows up; (iii) both two components blow up at some points and can be controlled by global bubbling solutions. In this paper, we prove that any of these three types happens under different circumstances for least energy solutions.

articleTitle: A New Characterization of the Mappings of Bounded Length Distortion
abstract: In this paper, we present a new characterization of the mappings of bounded length distortion (BLD for short). In the original geometric definition, it is assumed that a BLD mapping is open, discrete, and sense-preserving. We prove that the first two of the three conditions are redundant and the sense-preserving condition can be replaced by a weaker assumption that the Jacobian is nonnegative.

articleTitle: Tau Functions and the Limit of Block Toeplitz Determinants
abstract: A classical way to introduce tau functions for integrable hierarchies of solitonic equations is by means of the Sato–Segal–Wilson infinite-dimensional Grassmannian. Every point in the Grassmannian is naturally related to a Riemann–Hilbert problem on the unit circle, for which Bertola proposed a tau function that generalizes the Jimbo–Miwa–Ueno tau function for isomonodromic deformation problems. In this paper, we prove that the Sato–Segal–Wilson tau function and the (generalized) Jimbo–Miwa–Ueno iso- monodromic tau function coincide under a very general setting, by identifying each of them to the large-size limit of a block Toeplitz determinant. As an application, we give a new definition of tau function for Drinfeld–Sokolov hierarchies (and their generalizations) by means of infinite-dimensional Grassmannians, and clarify their relation with other tau functions given in the literature.

articleTitle: A Recursive Construction of Joint Eigenfunctions for the Hyperbolic Nonrelativistic Calogero-Moser Hamiltonians
abstract: We obtain symmetric joint eigenfunctions for the commuting partial differential operators associated to the hyperbolic Calogero-Moser <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-particle system. The eigenfunctions are constructed via a recursion scheme, which leads to representations by multidimensional integrals whose integrands are elementary functions. We also tie in these eigenfunctions with the Heckman–Opdam hypergeometric function for the root system <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{N-1}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Low Energy Resolvent for the Hodge Laplacian: Applications to Riesz Transform, Sobolev Estimates, and Analytic Torsion
abstract: On an asymptotically conic manifold (M,g), we analyze the asymptotics of the integral kernel of the resolvent R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>(k):=(Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>+k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> of the Hodge Laplacian Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> on q-forms as the spectral parameter k approaches zero, assuming that 0 is not a resonance. The first application we give is an L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> Sobolev estimate for d+δ and Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>. Then we obtain a complete characterization of the range of p>1 for which the Riesz transform for q-forms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_q=(d+\delta)\Delta _q^{-1/2}$</tex> is bounded on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>. Finally, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the analytic torsion of a family of smooth compact Riemannian manifolds (Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ϵ</inf>,g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ϵ</inf>) degenerating to a compact manifold (Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>,g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) with a conic singularity as ϵ→0.

articleTitle: On Uniqueness for Supercritical Nonlinear Wave and Schrödinger Equations
abstract: In a recent paper [39], Struwe considered the Cauchy problem for a class of nonlinear wave and Schrödinger equations. Under some assumptions on the nonlinearities, it was shown that uniqueness of classical solutions can be obtained in the much larger class of distribution solutions satisfying the energy inequality. As pointed out in [39], the conditions on the nonlinearities are satisfied for any polynomial growth but they fail to hold for higher growth (for example e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u2</sup>). Our aim here is to improve Struwe's result by showing that uniqueness holds for more general nonlinearities including higher growth or oscillations.

articleTitle: A Remark on a Uniqueness Property of High Multiplicity Tangent Flows in Dimension 3
abstract: In this note, we combine the work of Ilmanen [11] and of Colding et al. [3] to observe a uniqueness property for tangent flows at the first singular time of a smooth mean curvature flow of a closed surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^3$</tex>. Specifically, if, at a fixed singular point, one tangent flow is a positive integer multiple of a shrinking <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^2, {\BBS}^1\times {\BBR}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBS}^2$</tex>, then, modulo rotations, all tangent flows at the point are the same.

articleTitle: Orbit Closures of Source-Sink Dynkin Quivers
abstract: We use the Kempf–Lascoux–Weyman geometric technique to calculate the resolution of orbit closures of representations of Dynkin quivers with every vertex being source or sink. We use this resolution to derive the normality of such orbit closures. As a consequence, we obtain the normality of certain orbit closures of type E.

articleTitle: On Bi-exactness of Discrete Quantum Groups
abstract: We define Ozawa's notion of bi-exactness to discrete quantum groups, and then prove some structural properties of associated von Neumann algebras. In particular, we prove that any nonamenable subfactor of free quantum group von Neumann algebras, which is an image of a faithful normal conditional expectation, has no Cartan subalgebras.

articleTitle: Lagrangian Fibrations in Duality on Moduli Spaces of Rank 2 Logarithmic Connections Over the Projective Line
abstract: We study the moduli space of logarithmic connections of rank 2 on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1_\mathbb C$</tex> minus n points with fixed spectral data. There are two natural Lagrangian maps: one toward apparent singularities of the associated Fuchsian scalar equation and another one toward moduli of parabolic bundles. We show that these are transversal and dual to each other. In case n=5, we recover the beautiful geometry of Del Pezzo surfaces of degree 4.

articleTitle: The q-Hahn Boson Process and q-Hahn TASEP
abstract: We prove an intertwining relation (or Markov duality) between the q-Hahn Boson process and q-Hahn TASEP, two discrete time Markov chains introduced by Povolotsky [17], depending on three real parameters q,μ,ν. Using this and a variant of the coordinate Bethe ansatz, we compute nested contour integral formulas for expectations of a family of observables of the q-Hahn TASEP when started from step initial data. We then utilize these to prove a Fredholm determinant formula for distribution of the location of any given particle.

articleTitle: Rohlin Flows on Amalgamated Free Product Factors
abstract: We construct flows on an amalgamated free product factor and characterize the Rohlin property for them by faithfulness of R×Z actions on a measured space. As a corollary, we find Rohlin flows on this factor. This is the first example of Rohlin flows on non-McDuff factors. We also apply Masuda–Tomatsu’s theorem to our Rohlin flows, and obtain a classification up to strong cocycle conjugacy. However, it also turns out that usual cocycle conjugacy is different from strong cocycle conjugacy for our flows. Consequently, even though Masuda–Tomatsu’s analysis is applicable for flows on non-McDuff factors, the effect of their analysis on classification up to cocycle conjugacy is limited.

articleTitle: Birational Geometry of the Space of Complete Quadrics
abstract: We study the birational geometry of the moduli space of complete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-quadrics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We exhibit generators for Eff<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X)$</tex> and Nef<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X)$</tex>, the cone of effective divisors and the cone of nef divisors, respectively. As a corollary, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is a Fano variety. Furthermore, we run the Minimal Model Program on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and find a moduli interpretation for the models induced by the generators of the nef cone. In the case of complete quadric surfaces, we describe all the birational models of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> induced by the movable cone and find a moduli interpretation for some of these models.

articleTitle: Multifractal Analysis for Quotients of Birkhoff Sums for Countable Markov Maps
abstract: This paper is devoted to study multifractal analysis of quotients of Birkhoff averages for countable Markov maps. We prove a variational principle for the Hausdorff dimension of the level sets. Under certain assumptions we are able to show that the spectrum varies analytically in parts of its domain. We apply our results to show that the Birkhoff spectrum for the Manneville–Pomeau map can be discontinuous, showing the remarkable differences with the uniformly hyperbolic setting. We also obtain results describing the Birkhoff spectrum of suspension flows. Examples involving continued fractions are also given.

articleTitle: Deformations of Constant Scalar Curvature Sasakian Metrics and K-Stability
abstract: Extending the work of G. Székelyhidi and T. Brönnle to Sasakian manifolds, we prove that a small deformation of the complex structure of the cone of a constant scalar curvature Sasakian (cscS) manifold admits a constant scalar curvature structure if it is K-polystable. This also implies that a small deformation of the complex structure of the cone of a constant scalar curvature structure is K-semistable. As applications, we give examples of cscS manifolds which are deformations of toric examples, and we also show that if a 3-Sasakian manifold admits a nontrivial transversal complex deformation, then it admits a nontrivial Sasaki–Einstein deformation.

articleTitle: Hessian Continuity at Degenerate Points in Nonvariational Elliptic Problems
abstract: Established in the 1930s, Schauder a priori estimates are among the most classical and powerful tools in the analysis of problems ruled by second-order elliptic partial differential equations. Since then, a central problem in regularity theory has been to understand Schauder-type estimates fashioning particular borderline scenarios. In such context, it has been a common accepted aphorism that the continuity of the Hessian of a solution could never be superior than the continuity of the medium. Notwithstanding, in this article, we show that solutions to uniformly elliptic, linear equations with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{0,\bar {\epsilon }}$</tex> coefficients are of class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{2,\alpha }$</tex>, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt \bar {\epsilon } \ll \alpha \lt 1$</tex>, at Hessian degenerate points, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {H}(u):={\{ }X \,|\, D^2u(X) = 0{\} }$</tex>. In fact, we develop a more general regularity result at such Hessian degenerate points, featuring into the theory of fully nonlinear equations. The key, innovative idea in the proof is to interpret Hessian degenerate sets as abstract (nonphysical) free boundary points. This novel insight has a number of further applications.

articleTitle: Restrictions of SL3 Maass Forms to Maximal Flat Subspaces
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi$</tex> be a Hecke–Maass cusp form on a cubic central simple algebra over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>. We apply arithmetic amplification to improve the local bound for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-norm of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi$</tex> restricted to maximal flat subspaces.

articleTitle: Scaling Limits of Correlations of Characteristic Polynomials for the Gaussian β-Ensemble with External Source
abstract: We study the averaged product of characteristic polynomials of large random matrices in the Gaussian β-ensemble perturbed by an external source of finite rank. We prove that at the edge of the spectrum, the limiting correlations involve two families of multivariate functions of Airy and Gaussian types. The precise form of the limiting correlations depends on the strength of the nonzero eigenvalues of the external source. A critical value for the latter is obtained and a phase transition phenomenon similar to that of [2] is established. The derivation of our results relies mainly on previous articles by the authors, which deal with duality formulas [18] and asymptotics for Selberg-type integrals [22].

articleTitle: Locally Unsplit Families of Rational Curves of Large Anticanonical Degree on Fano Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we address Fano manifolds of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 3$</tex> with a locally unsplit dominating family of rational curves of anticanonical degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. We first observe that their Picard number is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>, and then we provide a classification of all cases with maximal Picard number. We also give examples of locally unsplit dominating families of rational curves whose varieties of minimal tangents at a general point are singular.

Infinite Reduced Words and the Tits Boundary of a Coxeter Group
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(W,S)$</tex> be a finite rank Coxeter system with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> infinite. We prove that the limit weak order on the blocks of infinite reduced words of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> is encoded by the topology of the Tits boundary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial _T X$</tex> of the Davis complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>. We consider many special cases, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> word hyperbolic and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> with isolated flats. We establish that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> is word hyperbolic, the limit weak order is the disjoint union of weak orders of finite Coxeter groups. We also establish, for each boundary point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi$</tex>, a natural order-preserving correspondence between infinite reduced words which “point towards” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi$</tex>, and elements of the reflection subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> which fixes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi$</tex>.

articleTitle: W-Algebras, False Theta Functions and Quantum Modular Forms, I
abstract: In this paper, we study certain partial and false theta functions in connection to vertex operator algebras and conformal field theory. We prove a variety of results concerning the asymptotics of modified characters of irreducible modules of certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}$</tex>-algebras of singlet type, which allows us in particular to determine their (analytic) quantum dimensions. Our results are fully consistent with the previous conjectures on fusion rings for these vertex algebras. More importantly, we prove quantum modularity (à la Zagier) of the numerator part of irreducible characters of singlet algebra modules, thus demonstrating that quantum modular forms naturally appear in many “sufficiently nice” irrational vertex algebras. It is interesting that quantum modularity persists on the whole set of rationals as in the original Zagier's example coming from Kontsevich's “strange series”. In the last part, slightly independent of all this, we also discuss Nahm-type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-hypergometric series in connection to tails of colored Jones polynomials of certain torus knots and characters of modules for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,p)$</tex>-singlet algebra.

articleTitle: Homotopy Categories, Leavitt Path Algebras, and Gorenstein Projective Modules
abstract: For a finite quiver without sources or sinks, we prove that the homotopy category of acyclic complexes of injective modules over the corresponding finite-dimensional algebra with radical square zero is triangle equivalent to the derived category of the Leavitt path algebra viewed as a differential graded algebra with trivial differential, which is further triangle equivalent to the stable category of Gorenstein projective modules over the trivial extension algebra of a von Neumann regular algebra by an invertible bimodule. A related, but different, result for the homotopy category of acyclic complexes of projective modules is given. Restricting these equivalences to compact objects, we obtain various descriptions of the singularity category of a finite-dimensional algebra with radical square zero, which contain previous results.

articleTitle: The Signed Euler Characteristic of Very Affine Varieties
abstract: A conjecture of Huh and Sturmfels predicts that the sign of the Euler characteristic of a complex very affine variety depends only on the parity of the dimension. The conjecture is true for locally complete intersections. Beyond this case, we construct counterexamples with arbitrarily bad failure.

articleTitle: Algebraic Complete Integrability of the Bloch–Iserles System
abstract: The goal of this paper is the proof of the algebraic complete integrability of the Bloch–Iserles Hamiltonian system [5]. This result was conjectured in [4], based on its validity in certain special cases.

articleTitle: Uhlenbeck Compactification As a Functor
abstract: We give a definition of a functor compactifying the functor of bundles on a surfaces. Earlier different authors have defined similar spaces as either images under a morphism or a quotient by an equivalence relation. We use the technique of multiplicative functors to explain what kind of objects are parameterized by the points of this compactification.

articleTitle: Families of Calabi–Yau Manifolds and Canonical Singularities
abstract: Given a polarized family of varieties over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>, smooth over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta ^{\times }$</tex> and with smooth fibers Calabi–Yau, we show that the origin lies at finite Weil–Petersson distance if and only if after a finite base change the family is birational to one with central fiber a Calabi–Yau variety with at worst canonical singularities, answering a question of C.-L. Wang. This condition also implies that the Ricci-flat Kähler metrics in the polarization class on the smooth fibers have uniformly bounded diameter, or are uniformly volume non-collapsed.

articleTitle: Rational Values of Entire Functions of Finite Order
abstract: We prove a bound of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c(\log H)^n$</tex> for the number of rational points of height at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> on the graph of the restriction to a compact set of an entire function of finite order and positive lower order. The exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> depends only on the order and lower order of the function and can be effectively computed from them. The constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> can also be effectively computed from certain data associated with the function and the compact set to which it is restricted. We give the result more generally for algebraic points of bounded degree, using the absolute multiplicative height. We construct examples showing that a power-of-log bound is optimal, that there is no absolute <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> which works for all choices of finite order and positive lower order and that the assumption of positive lower order cannot be removed.

articleTitle: Quadro-Quadric Special Birational Transformations of Projective Spaces
abstract: Special birational transformations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi:\mathbb P^r\longrightarrow Z$</tex> defined by quadric hypersurfaces are studied by means of the variety of lines <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal L_Z\subset\mathbb P^{r-1}$</tex> passing through a general point z∈Z. Classification results are obtained when Z is either a Grassmannian of lines, or the 10-dimensional spinor variety, or the E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-variety. In the particular case of quadro-quadric transformations, we extend the well-known classification of Ein and Shepherd-Barron coming from Zak's classification of Severi varieties to a wider class of prime Fano manifolds Z. Combining both results, we get a classification of special birational transformations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi:\mathbb P^r\longrightarrow Z$</tex> defined by quadric hypersurfaces onto (a linear section of) a rational homogeneous variety different from a projective space and a quadric hypersurface.

articleTitle: J-Holomorphic Curves in a Nef Class
abstract: Taubes established fundamental properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-holomorphic subvarieties in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex> in [8]. In this paper, we further investigate properties of reducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-holomorphic subvarieties. We offer an upper bound of the total genus of a subvariety when the class of the subvariety is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-nef. For a spherical class, it has particularly strong consequences. It is shown that, for any tamed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>, each irreducible component is a smooth rational curve. It might be even new when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is integrable. We also completely classify configurations of maximal dimension. To prove these results, we treat subvarieties as weighted graphs and introduce several combinatorial moves.

articleTitle: DGA-Structure on Additive Higher Chow Groups
abstract: We construct a graded-commutative differential graded algebra structure on additive higher Chow groups of a smooth projective variety over a perfect field. We show that these groups are equipped with Frobenius and Verschiebung operators that turn the collection into a Witt complex.

articleTitle: A Compactness Result for Dimension Datum
abstract: Given a compact Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> and a closed subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>, the dimension datum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> is the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {D}_{H}:\hat {G}\to {{\BBZ}}$</tex> which assigns to each irreducible complex linear representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> the dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{H}$</tex>, the subspace of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-invariant vectors. We prove that as a subspace of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBZ}}^{\hat G}$</tex> the set consisting of dimension data of closed subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is compact. We obtain new proofs of some previously known finiteness and rigidity results and we give an application to spectral geometry.

articleTitle: On Weingarten Transformations of Hyperbolic Nets
abstract: Weingarten transformations of smooth surfaces, which, by definition, preserve asymptotic lines have been studied extensively in classical differential geometry, and they also play an important role in connection with the modern geometric theory of integrable systems. Their natural discrete analogs have been investigated in great detail in the area of (integrable) discrete differential geometry and can be traced back at least to the early 1950s. Here, we propose a canonical analog of (discrete) Weingarten transformations for hyperbolic nets, that is, C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-surfaces which constitute hybrids of smooth and discrete surfaces “parameterized” in terms of asymptotic coordinates. We prove the existence of Weingarten pairs and analyze their geometric and algebraic properties.

articleTitle: The Skeleton of the Jacobian, the Jacobian of the Skeleton, and Lifting Meromorphic Functions From Tropical to Algebraic Curves
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be an algebraically closed field which is complete with respect to a nontrivial, non-Archimedean valuation and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex> be its value group. Given a smooth, proper, connected <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and a skeleton <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> of the Berkovich analytification <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{{\rm an}}$</tex>, there are two natural real tori which one can consider: the tropical Jacobian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {Jac}(\Gamma )$</tex> and the skeleton of the Berkovich analytification <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {Jac}(X)^{\rm an}$</tex>. We show that the skeleton of the Jacobian is canonically isomorphic to the Jacobian of the skeleton as principally polarized tropical abelian varieties. In addition, we show that the tropicalization of a classical Abel–Jacobi map is a tropical Abel–Jacobi map. As a consequence of these results, we deduce that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-rational principal divisors on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex>, in the sense of tropical geometry, are exactly the retractions of principal divisors on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We actually prove a more precise result which says that, although zeros and poles of divisors can cancel under the retraction map, in order to lift a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-rational principal divisor on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> to a principal divisor on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> it is never necessary to add more than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> extra zeros and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> extra poles. Our results imply that a continuous function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F:\Gamma \to {\bf{R}}$</tex> is the restriction to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\log |f|$</tex> for some nonzero meromorphic function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-rational tropical meromorphic function, and we use this fact to prove that there is a rational map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: X -\!-\!\rightarrow {\bf{P}}^{3}$</tex> whose tropicalization, when restricted to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex>, is an isometry onto its image.Throughout this paper, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> denotes a field which is complete with respect to a nontrivial, non-Archimedean valuation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {val}: K\to {\bf{R}}\cup {\{ }\infty {\} }$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> be its valuation ring, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be its residue field, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda = \hbox {val}(K^\times )$</tex> be its value group. Note that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex> is either discrete or dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf{R}}$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\,\cdot \,| = \exp (-\hbox {val}(\cdot ))$</tex> be an associated absolute value.

articleTitle: Residues of Intertwining Operators for U(3,3) and Base Change
abstract: Let F be a p-adic local field with characteristic 0 and E/F a quadratic extension. Let σ=π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>⊗π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf> be a supercuspidal representation of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(E)×U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E/F</inf>(1,1) with π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> conjugate self-dual. In this paper, we use a local approach developed by Shahidi to study the residue of the standard intertwining operator on the parabolic induced representation from σ to the quasi-split unitary group U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E/F</inf>(3,3) at s=0, and show that if π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> is a standard base change from U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E/F</inf>(1,1), then the residue at s=0 is nonzero if and only if π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> is the standard base change of π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf>.

articleTitle: A Problem on Sums of Two Squares
abstract: Krishnapur et al. [15] studied the length of the fluctuations of nodal lengths of random Laplace eigenfunctions on the standard 2-torus. A key step in the paper is a nontrivial bound for the sixth-order correlation of the integer solutions of the equation m=x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This is a problem about a certain diophantine equation, studied here in depth using a variety of methods.

articleTitle: Sturm–Liouville Estimates for the Spectrum and Cheeger Constant
abstract: Buser's inequality gives an upper bound on the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplacian of a closed manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> in terms of the Cheeger constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(M)$</tex>. Agol later gave a quantitative improvement of Buser's inequality. Agol's result is less transparent since it is given implicitly by a set of equations, one of which is a differential equation Agol could not solve except when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is 3D. We show that a substitution transforms Agol's differential equation into the Riemann differential equation. Then, we give a proof of Agol's result and also generalize it using the Sturm–Liouville theory. Under the same assumptions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, we are able to give upper bounds on the higher eigenvalues of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _k(M)$</tex>, in terms of the eigenvalues of a Sturm–Liouville problem which depends on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(M)$</tex>. We then compare the Weyl asymptotic of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _k(M)$</tex> given by the works of Cheng, Gromov, and Bérard–Besson–Gallot to the asymptotics of our Sturm–Liouville problems given by Atkinson–Mingarelli.

articleTitle: The Hasse Principle for Lines on del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we consider the following problem: Does there exist a cubic surface over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> which contains no line over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>, yet contains a line over every completion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>? This question may be interpreted as asking whether the Hilbert scheme of lines on a cubic surface can fail the Hasse principle. We also consider analogous problems, over arbitrary number fields, for other del Pezzo surfaces and complete intersections of two quadrics.

articleTitle: Shimura Curves and Special Values of p-adic L-functions
abstract: We construct “generalized Heegner cycles” on a variety fibered over a Shimura curve, defined over a number field. We show that their images under the p-adic Abel–Jacobi map coincide with the values (outside the range of interpolation) of a p-adic L-function L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(f,χ) which interpolates special values of the Rankin–Selberg convolution of a fixed newform f and a theta-series θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">χ</inf> attached to an unramified Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field K. This generalizes previous work of Bertolini, Darmon, and Prasanna, which demonstrated a similar result in the case of modular curves. Our main tool is the theory of Serre–Tate coordinates, which yields p-adic expansions of modular forms at CM points, replacing the role of q-expansions in computations on modular curves.

articleTitle: On the Classification of Discrete Hirota-Type Equations in 3D
abstract: In the series of recent publications [16, 17, 19, 21], we have proposed a novel approach to the classification of integrable differential/difference equations in three dimensions based on the requirement that hydrodynamic reductions of the corresponding dispersionless limits are ‘inherited’ by the dispersive equation. Here we extend this to the fully discrete case. Based on the method of deformations of hydrodynamic reductions, we classify 3D discrete integrable Hirota-type equations within various particularly interesting subclasses. Our method can be viewed as an alternative to the conventional multi-dimensional consistency approach.

articleTitle: Dimensional Differences Between Faces of the Cones of Nonnegative Polynomials and Sums of Squares
abstract: We study dimensions of the faces of the cone of nonnegative polynomials and the cone of sums of squares; we show that there are dimensional differences between corresponding faces of these cones. These dimensional gaps occur in all cases where there exist nonnegative polynomials that are not sums of squares. The gaps occur generically, they are not the product of selecting special faces of the cones. For ternary forms and quaternary quartics, we characterize when these differences are observed. Moreover, we provide an explicit description for these differences in the two smallest cases, in which the cone of nonnegative polynomials and the cone of sums of squares are different. Our results follow from more general results concerning the relationship between the degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2d$</tex> component of the second symbolic power of the vanishing ideal of points in projective space and the square of the degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> component of the vanishing ideal.

articleTitle: A Limit Theorem at the Spectral Edge for Corners of Time-Dependent Wigner Matrices
abstract: For the eigenvalues of principal submatrices of stochastically evolving Wigner matrices, we construct and study the edge scaling limit: a random decreasing sequence of continuous functions of two variables, which at every point has the distribution of the Airy point process. The analysis is based on the methods developed by Soshnikov to study the extreme eigenvalues of a single Wigner matrix.

articleTitle: Some Examples of Isotropic SL(2, ℝ)-Invariant Subbundles of the Hodge Bundle
abstract: We construct some examples of origamis (square-tiled surfaces) such that the Hodge bundles over the corresponding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}(2,{\BBR})$</tex>-orbits on the moduli space admit nontrivial isotropic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}(2,{\BBR})$</tex>-invariant subbundles. This answers a question posed to the authors by Eskin and Forni.

articleTitle: Localization of Zeros for Cauchy Transforms
abstract: We study the localization of zeros for Cauchy transforms of discrete measures on the real line. This question is motivated by the theory of canonical systems of differential equations. In particular, we prove that the spaces of Cauchy transforms having the localization property are in one-to-one correspondence with the canonical systems of special type, namely, those whose Hamiltonians consist only of indivisible intervals accumulating on the left. Various aspects of the localization phenomena are studied in details. Connections with the density of polynomials and other topics in analysis are discussed.

articleTitle: A Generalization of Reilly's Formula and its Applications to a New Heintze–Karcher Type Inequality
abstract: In this paper, we prove a generalization of Reilly's formula in [10]. We apply such general Reilly's formula to give alternative proofs of the Alexandrov's Theorem and the Heintze–Karcher inequality in the hemisphere and in the hyperbolic space. Moreover, we use the general Reilly's formula to prove a new Heintze–Karcher inequality for Riemannian manifolds with boundary and sectional curvature bounded below.

articleTitle: The Divisor Function in Arithmetic Progressions to Smooth Moduli
abstract: By using the q-analog of van der Corput's method, we study the divisor function in an arithmetic progression to modulus q. We show that the expected asymptotic formula holds for a larger range of q than was previously known, provided that q has a certain factorization.

articleTitle: Enumeration of Grothendieck's Dessins and KP Hierarchy
abstract: Branched covers of the complex projective line ramified over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0,1,$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex> (Grothendieck's dessins d'enfant) of fixed genus and degree are effectively enumerated. More precisely, branched covers of a given ramification profile over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex> and given numbers of preimages of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> are considered. The generating function for the numbers of such covers is shown to satisfy a partial differential equation (PDE) that determines it uniquely modulo a simple initial condition. Moreover, this generating function satisfies an infinite system of PDE's called the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy. A specification of this generating function for certain values of parameters generates the numbers of dessins of given genus and degree, thus providing a fast algorithm for computing these numbers.

articleTitle: Low-Lying Zeros of Maass Form L-Functions
abstract: The Katz–Sarnak density conjecture states that the scaling limits of the distributions of zeros of families of automorphic L-functions agree with the scaling limits of eigenvalue distributions of classical subgroups of the unitary groups U(N). This conjecture is often tested by way of computing particular statistics, such as the one-level density, which evaluates a test function with compactly supported Fourier transform at normalized zeros near the central point. Iwaniec, Luo, and Sarnak studied the one-level densities of cuspidal newforms of weight k and level N. They showed in the limit as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kN \to \infty $</tex> that these families have one-level densities agreeing with orthogonal type for test functions with Fourier transform supported in (−2,2). Exceeding (−1,1) is important as the three orthogonal groups are indistinguishable for support up to (−1,1) but are distinguishable for any larger support. We study the other family of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> automorphic forms over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>: Maass forms. To facilitate the analysis, we use smooth weight functions in the Kuznetsov formula which, among other restrictions, vanish to order 2M at the origin. For test functions with Fourier transform supported inside <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-2 + {2 \over 2M+1}, 2 - {2 \over 2M+1})$</tex>, we unconditionally prove the one-level density of the low-lying zeros of level 1 Maass forms, as the eigenvalues tend to infinity, agrees only with that of the scaling limit of orthogonal matrices.

articleTitle: Rabinowitz–Floer Homology on Brieskorn Spheres
abstract: In this paper, we will show how to distinguish contact structures using Rabinowitz–Floer homology—a homology for strong exactly fillable contact manifolds, which was recently introduced by Cieliebak and Frauenfelder [3]. Unlike contact homology, this invariant is not S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-equivariant. As an application we give a new proof for the following result due to Ilya Ustilovsky: There are infinitely many nondiffeomorphic contact structures in every formal homotopy class of S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4m+1</sup>. Furthermore, we construct nondiffeomorphic contact structures lying in the same formal homotopy class on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4m−1</sup>.

articleTitle: A Remark About the Spectral Radius
abstract: We show that for any finitely generated nonamenable group and any ε>0, there exists some finite symmetric generating set with spectral radius less than ε. We give applications to percolation theory and the theory of operator spaces.

articleTitle: Singular Degree of a Rational Matrix Pseudodifferential Operator
abstract: In our previous work, we studied minimal fractional decompositions of a rational matrix pseudodifferential operator: H=AB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, where A and B are matrix differential operators, and B is nondegenerate of minimal possible degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\deg (B)$</tex>. In the present paper, we introduce the singular degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {sdeg}} (H)=\deg (B)$</tex>, and show that, for an arbitrary rational expression <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=\sum _{\alpha }A^\alpha _1(B^\alpha _1)^{-1}\cdots A^\alpha _n(B^\alpha _n)^{-1}$</tex>, we have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {sdeg}} (H)\leq \sum _{\alpha ,i}\deg (B^\alpha _i)$</tex>. If the equality holds, we call such an expression minimal. We study the properties of the singular degree and of minimal rational expressions. These results are important for the computations involved in the Lenard–Magri scheme of integrability.

articleTitle: On a Family of Surfaces of General Type Attached to Abelian Four-Folds and the Weyl Group W(E6)
abstract: We study a family of surfaces of general type that arises from the intersections of two translates of the theta divisor on a principally polarized complex abelian four-fold. In particular, we determine the Néron-Severi lattices of these surfaces and show that for a general abelian four-fold the monodromy group of the associated variation of Hodge structures is a subgroup of index at most two in the Weyl group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W(E_6)$</tex>, whereas for a Jacobian variety it degenerates to a subgroup of the symmetric group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur S}_6$</tex>.

articleTitle: Harish-Chandra Series in Finite Unitary Groups and Crystal Graphs
abstract: The distribution of the unipotent modules (in nondefining prime characteristic) of the finite unitary groups into Harish-Chandra series is investigated. We formulate a series of conjectures relating this distribution with the crystal graph of an integrable module for a certain quantum group. Evidence for our conjectures is presented, as well as proofs for some of their consequences for the crystal graphs involved. In the course of our work we also generalize Harish-Chandra theory for some of the finite classical groups, and we introduce their Harish-Chandra branching graphs.

articleTitle: Boundary Behavior of Harmonic Functions on Gromov Hyperbolic Manifolds
abstract: Let M be a complete simply connected manifold which is in addition Gromov hyperbolic, coercive, and roughly starlike. For a given harmonic function on M, a local Fatou Theorem and a pointwise criteria of nontangential convergence coming from the density of energy are shown: at almost all points of the boundary, the harmonic function converges nontangentially if and only if the supremum of the density of energy is finite. As an application of these results, a Calderón–Stein Theorem is proved, that is, the nontangential properties of convergence, boundedness, and finiteness of energy are equivalent at almost every point of the boundary.

articleTitle: Automorphisms of ℂ3 Commuting with a ℂ+-Action
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> be an algebraic action of the additive group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{{\BBC}}}}^+ $</tex> on the three-dimensional affine space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{{\BBC}}}}^3$</tex>. We describe the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {Cent}}}(\rho )$</tex> of polynomial automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{{\BBC}}}}^3$</tex> that commute with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex>. A particular emphasis lies in the description of the automorphisms in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {Cent}}}(\rho )$</tex> coming from algebraic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{{\BBC}}}}^+ $</tex>-actions. As an application, we prove that the automorphisms in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {Cent}}}(\rho )$</tex> that are the identity on the algebraic quotient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> form a characteristic subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {Cent}}}(\rho )$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Theta Period of a Cuspidal Automorphic Representation of GL(n)
abstract: Let E(⋯) be an Eisenstein series corresponding to an automorphic cuspidal representation τ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {GL}}_{n}({\BBA})$</tex>, induced to a representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {SO}}_{2n+1}({\BBA})$</tex> through the Siegel parabolic subgroup. The presence of a pole of E at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s={1\over 2}$</tex>, or the nonvanishing of the residue E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</inf>, is determined by the presence of a pole of the partial symmetric square L-function at s=1. We define a co-period integral of E, involving the integration of E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</inf> against a pair of automorphic forms in the space of the small representation of Bump, Friedberg, and Ginzburg. We compute the co-period and relate it to a “theta period” integral of τ—an integral of a cusp form against two theta functions corresponding to the exceptional representation of Kazhdan and Patterson.

articleTitle: Invariant Vector Fields and Groupoids
abstract: We use the notion of isomorphism between two invariant vector fields to shed new light on the issue of linearization of an invariant vector field near a relative equilibrium. We argue that the notion is useful in understanding the passage from the space of invariant vector fields in a tube around a group orbit to the space invariant vector fields on a slice to the orbit. The notion comes from Hepworth's study of vector fields on stacks.

articleTitle: Thue–Morse Constant is Not Badly Approximable
abstract: We prove that Thue–Morse constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\tau _{\rm TM}}=0.01101001\dots _2$</tex> is not a badly approximable number. Moreover, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\tau _{\rm TM}}(a)=0.01101001\dots _a$</tex> is not badly approximable for every integer base <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a\geq 2$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> is not divisible by 15. At the same time, we provide a precise formula for convergents of the Laurent series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\tilde {f}_{\rm TM}}(z) = z^{-1}\prod _{n=1}^\infty (1-z^{-2^n})$</tex>, thus developing further the research initiated by Alf van der Poorten and others.

articleTitle: σ-Galois Theory of Linear Difference Equations
abstract: We develop a Galois theory for systems of linear difference equations with an action of an endomorphism σ. This provides a technique to test whether solutions of such systems satisfy σ-polynomial equations and, if yes, then characterize those. We also show how to apply our work to study isomonodromic difference equations and difference algebraic properties of meromorphic functions.

articleTitle: Long Gaps Between Sign-Changes of Gaussian Stationary Processes
abstract: We study the probability of a real-valued stationary process to be positive on a large interval [0,N]. We show that if in some neighborhood of the origin the spectral measure of the process has density which is bounded away from zero and infinity, then the decay of this probability is bounded between two exponential functions in N. This generalizes similar bounds obtained for particular cases, such as a recent result by Antezana, Buckley, Marzo, Olsen.

articleTitle: Lattice and Heegaard Floer Homologies of Algebraic Links
abstract: We compute the Heegaard Floer link homology of algebraic links in terms of the multi-variate Hilbert function of the corresponding plane curve singularities. The main result of the paper identifies four homologies: (a) the Heegaard Floer link homology of the local embedded link, (b) the lattice homology associated with the Hilbert function, (c) the homologies of the projectivized complements of local hyperplane arrangements cut out from the local algebra, and (d) a generalized version of the Orlik–Solomon algebra of these local arrangements. In particular, the Poincaré polynomials of all these homology groups are the same, and we also show that they agree with the coefficients of the motivic Poincaré series of the singularity.

articleTitle: Supports of Measures in a Free Additive Convolution Semigroup
abstract: In this paper, we study the supports of measures in the free additive convolution semigroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\mu ^{\boxplus t}:t \gt 1\}$</tex>, where μ is a Borel probability measure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>. We give a formula for the density of the absolutely continuous part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{\boxplus t}$</tex> and use this formula to obtain certain regularizing properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{\boxplus t}$</tex>. We show that the number n(t) of the components in the support of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{\boxplus t}$</tex> is a nonincreasing function of t and give equivalent conditions so that n(t)=1 for sufficiently large t. Moreover, a measure μ so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu ^{\boxplus t}$</tex> has infinitely many components in the support for all t>1 is given.

articleTitle: Homogeneous Ricci Solitons in Low Dimensions
abstract: In this article, we classify expanding homogeneous Ricci solitons up to dimension 5, according to their presentation as homogeneous spaces. We obtain that they are all isometric to solvsolitons, and this, in particular, implies that the generalized Alekseevskii conjecture holds in these dimensions. In addition, we prove that the conjecture holds in dimension 6 provided the transitive group is not semi-simple.

articleTitle: Dubrovin's Conjecture for IG(2, 6)
abstract: We show that the big quantum cohomology of the symplectic isotropic Grassmanian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm IG}(2,6)$</tex> is generically semisimple, whereas its small quantum cohomology is known to be non-semisimple. This gives yet another case where Dubrovin's conjecture holds and stresses the need to consider the big quantum cohomology in its formulation.

articleTitle: New Examples of Extremal Domains for the First Eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami Operator in a Riemannian Manifold with Boundary
abstract: We build new examples of extremal domains with small prescribed volume for the first eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami operator in some Riemannian manifolds with boundary. These domains are close to half-balls of small radius centered at a nondegenerate critical point of the mean curvature function of the boundary of the manifold, and their boundary intersects the boundary of the manifold orthogonally.

articleTitle: A Proof of Walsh's Convergence Theorem Using Couplings
abstract: Walsh has recently proved the norm convergence of all nonconventional ergodic averages corresponding to polynomial sequences in discrete nilpotent acting groups. He deduced this convergence from an equivalent “finitary” assertion of stability over arbitrarily long-time intervals for these averages, which is proved by essentially finitary means. The present paper shows how the induction at the heart of Walsh's proof can also be implemented using more classical notions of ergodic theory, such as couplings and characteristic factors.

articleTitle: n-Level Densities of Artin L-Functions
abstract: In this paper, we consider a family of twisted Artin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(s,\pi \times \rho )$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> is a fixed self-dual cuspidal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_m$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> is given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(s,\rho ,K)= {\zeta _K(s) \over \zeta (s)}$</tex> attached to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{d+1}$</tex>-field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>. By the strong Artin conjecture, we consider <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> as a cuspidal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_d$</tex>. We obtain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-level densities for our families under certain counting conjectures. Our result is unconditional for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_3$</tex>-fields regardless of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>, which is of symplectic type or of orthogonal type. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> of orthogonal type (i.e., the symmetric square <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-function has a pole at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s=1$</tex>), the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-level density computation is unconditional for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_4$</tex>-fields (and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_5$</tex>-fields under the strong Artin conjecture for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex>).

articleTitle: Totally Disconnected Locally Compact Groups with a Linear Open Subgroup
abstract: We describe the global structure of totally disconnected locally compact groups having a linear open compact subgroup. Among the applications, we show that if a nondiscrete, compactly generated, topologically simple, totally disconnected locally compact group is locally linear, then it is a simple algebraic group over a local field.

articleTitle: On Manin's Conjecture for a Certain Singular Cubic Surface Over Imaginary Quadratic Fields
abstract: We prove Manin's conjecture over imaginary quadratic number fields for a cubic surface with a singularity of type E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>.

articleTitle: On the Ascending Chain Condition for Mixed Difference Ideals
abstract: We show that the ring of difference polynomials over a difference field does not satisfy the ascending chain condition for mixed difference ideals. This result solves an open problem of difference algebra stated by Hrushovski in connection with the development of difference algebraic geometry.

articleTitle: A Deformation of the Method of Characteristics and the Cauchy Problem for Hamiltonian PDEs in the Small Dispersion Limit
abstract: We introduce a deformation of the method of characteristics valid for Hamiltonian perturbations of a scalar conservation law in the small dispersion limit. Our method of analysis is based on the “variational string equation”, a functional-differential relation originally introduced by Dubrovin in a particular case, of which we lay the mathematical foundation. Starting from first principles, we construct the string equation explicitly up to the fourth order in perturbation theory, and we show that the solution to the Cauchy problem of the Hamiltonian partial differential equation (PDE) satisfies the appropriate string equation in the small dispersion limit. We apply our construction to explicitly compute the first two perturbative corrections of the solution to the general Hamiltonian PDE. In the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) case, we prove the existence of a quasitriviality transformation at any order and for arbitrary initial data.

articleTitle: Witt Vectors and a Question of Entin, Keating, and Rudnick
abstract: This is Part II of the paper “Witt vectors and a question of Keating and Rudnick” [6]. Here, we prove an independence result for tuples of character sums, formed with a variable character and its powers. In the Appendix, we prove an independence result for tuples of character sums formed with variable pairs of characters and products of the two.

articleTitle: Big Polygon Spaces
abstract: We study a new class of compact orientable manifolds, called big polygon spaces. They are intersections of real quadrics and related to polygon spaces, which appear as their fixed point set under a canonical torus action.What makes big polygon spaces interesting is that they exhibit remarkable new features in equivariant cohomology: The Chang–Skjelbred sequence can be exact for them and the equivariant Poincaré pairing perfect although their equivariant cohomology is never free as a module over the cohomology ring of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BT$</tex>. More generally, big polygon spaces show that a certain bound on the syzygy order of the equivariant cohomology of compact orientable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>-manifolds obtained by Allday, Puppe, and the author is sharp.

articleTitle: Canonical Extension of Submanifolds and Foliations in Noncompact Symmetric Spaces
abstract: We propose a method to extend submanifolds, singular Riemannian foliations and isometric actions from a boundary component of a noncompact symmetric space to the whole space. This extension method preserves minimal submanifolds, isoparametric foliations, and polar actions, among other properties. One of the several applications yields the first examples of inhomogeneous isoparametric hypersurfaces in noncompact symmetric spaces of rank at least 2.

articleTitle: Bounded Negativity and Arrangements of Lines
