abstract: The Bounded Negativity Conjecture predicts that for any smooth complex surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> there exists a lower bound for the selfintersection of reduced divisors on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. This conjecture is open. It is also not known if the existence of such a lower bound is invariant in the birational equivalence class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. In the present note, we introduce certain constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H(X)$</tex> which measure in effect the variance of the lower bounds in the birational equivalence class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We focus on rational surfaces and relate the value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H({\BBP}^2)$</tex> to certain line arrangements. Our main result is Theorem 3.3 and the main open challenge is Problem 3.10.

articleTitle: Simple Counter-Examples to Kotani–Last Conjecture Via Reducibility
abstract: Kotani–Last conjecture says that if an ergodic 1D operator possesses absolutely continuous spectrum, then the potential is almost periodic. In this paper, we give counter-examples to the conjecture via reducibility.

articleTitle: Locally Harmonic Maass Forms and the Kernel of the Shintani Lift
abstract: In this paper, we define a new type of modular object and construct explicit examples of such functions. Our functions are closely related to cusp forms constructed by Zagier [37] which played an important role in the construction by Kohnen and Zagier [26] of a kernel function for the Shimura and Shintani lifts between half-integral and integral weight cusp forms. Although our functions share many properties in common with harmonic weak Maass forms, they also have some properties which strikingly contrast those exhibited by harmonic weak Maass forms. As a first application of the new theory developed in this paper, one obtains a new proof of the fact that the even periods of Zagier's cusp forms are rational as an easy corollary.

articleTitle: Exceptional Sheaves on the Hirzebruch Surface 𝔽2
abstract: We investigate exceptional sheaves on the Hirzebruch surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {{\BBF}}_2 $</tex>, as the first attempt toward the classification of exceptional objects on weak del Pezzo surfaces.

articleTitle: Symplectic Resolutions for Conical Symplectic Varieties
abstract: We introduce the notion of a conical symplectic variety, and show that any symplectic resolution of such a variety is isomorphic to the Springer resolution of a nilpotent orbit closure in a semisimple Lie algebra, composed with a linear projection.

articleTitle: Spectral Data for U(m,m)-Higgs Bundles
abstract: We define and study spectral data associated to U(m,m)-Higgs bundles through the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {GL}}(2m,{\BBC})$</tex> Hitchin fibration. We give a new interpretation of the topological invariants involved as well as a geometric description of the moduli space.

articleTitle: Strong Orthogonality between the Möbius Function and Nonlinear Exponential Functions in Short Intervals
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu (n)$</tex> be the Möbius function, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e(z) = \exp (2\pi iz)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> real and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\leq y \leq x$</tex>. This paper proves two sequences <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu (n))$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(e(n^k \alpha ))$</tex> are strongly orthogonal in short intervals. That is, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 3$</tex> being fixed and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y\geq x^{1-1/4+\varepsilon }$</tex>, then for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A \gt 0,$</tex> we have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\sum_{x \lt n \leq x+y} \mu(n) e(n^k \alpha) \ll y(\log y)^{-A}$$</tex> uniformly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \in {\BBR}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Regularization of Non-Normal Matrices by Gaussian Noise
abstract: We consider the regularization of matrices <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^N$</tex> in Jordan form by additive Gaussian noise <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N^{-\gamma }G^N$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^N$</tex> is a matrix of i.i.d. standard Gaussians and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma \gt { {1 \over 2}}$</tex> so that the operator norm of the additive noise tends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>. Under mild conditions on the structure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^N,$</tex> we evaluate the limit of the empirical measure of eigenvalues of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^N+N^{-\gamma } G^N$</tex> and show that it depends on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>, in contrast with the case of a single Jordan block.

articleTitle: On the Spectral Flow for Dirac Operators with Local Boundary Conditions
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> be an even dimensional compact Riemannian manifold with boundary and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> be a Dirac operator acting on the sections of the Clifford module <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {E}$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. We impose certain local elliptic boundary conditions for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> obtaining a selfadjoint extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_F$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>. For a smooth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(n)$</tex>-valued function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \colon M \to U(n)$</tex> we establish a formula for the spectral flow along the straight line between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_F$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g^{-1} D_F g$</tex>. This spectral flow is motivated by index theory: in odd dimensions, it gives the natural pairing between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-homology class of the operator and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-theory class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>. In our situation, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim M$</tex> having the “wrong” parity, the answer can be expressed in terms of the natural spectral flow pairing on the odd-dimensional boundary. Our result generalizes a recent paper by Prokhorova [21] in which the two-dimensional case is treated. Furthermore, our paper may be seen as an odd-dimensional analogue of a paper by Freed [15]. As an application we obtain a new proof of the cobordism invariance of the spectral flow.

articleTitle: Decomposition of Direct Images of Logarithmic Differentials
abstract: The purpose of this note is to give a short proof of a theorem of Kollár that the derived direct image of the canonical sheaf splits into a sum of its cohomology sheaves. This is deduced from a stronger decomposition theorem for direct images of sheaves of logarithmic differentials, together with the weak semistable reduction theorem.

articleTitle: Uniqueness Theorems for Free Boundary Minimal Disks in Space Forms
abstract: We show that a minimal disk satisfying the free boundary condition in a constant curvature ball of any dimension is totally geodesic. We weaken the condition to parallel mean curvature vector in which case we show that the disk lies in a three dimensional constant curvature submanifold and is totally umbilic. These results extend to higher dimensions earlier three dimensional work of J. C. C. Nitsche and R. Souam.

articleTitle: On Quotients of Affine Spherical Varieties by Certain Unipotent Subgroups
abstract: Let G be a connected reductive group and X be an affine spherical G-variety. Then any Borel subgroup B⊆G has finitely many orbits on X. Let H⊂B be a normal unipotent subgroup such that the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBC}}[G/H]$</tex> is finitely generated. Then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBC}}[X]^H$</tex> is finitely generated, too, and one may consider the categorical quotient map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi :X\to X/\!\!/{H}:={\rm {Spec}}\ {{\BBC}}[X]^H$</tex>. Clearly, B/H acts on X//H. Recently, Panyushev posed a question whether this action has finitely many orbits. (The point is that π is not always surjective.) He conjectured that this is always true for H=[U,U], the commutator of the maximal unipotent subgroup U⊂B. We discuss an approach to answering the question, give a positive answer in some cases, and provide a counterexample to the above conjecture.

articleTitle: Gevrey Expansions of Hypergeometric Integrals I
abstract: We study integral representations of the Gevrey series solutions of irregular hypergeometric systems. In this paper, we consider the case of the systems associated with a one-row matrix, for which the integration domains are of dimension 1. We prove that any Gevrey series solution along the singular support of the system is the asymptotic expansion of a holomorphic solution given by a carefully chosen integral representation.

articleTitle: Minkowski Valuations in a 2-Dimensional Complex Vector Space
abstract: A classification of continuous, translation invariant Minkowski valuations that are contravariant (or covariant) with respect to the complex special linear group is established in a 2-dimensional complex vector space. Every such valuation is given by the sum of a valuation of degree of homogeneity 1 and 3. In dimensions m≥3 such a classification was previously established and only valuations of a degree of homogeneity 2m–1 appear.

articleTitle: On K2 of Certain Families of Curves
abstract: We construct families of smooth, proper, algebraic curves in characteristic 0, of arbitrary genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>, together with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> elements in the kernel of the tame symbol. We show that those elements are in general independent by a limit calculation of the regulator. Working over a number field, we show that in some of those families the elements are integral. We determine when those curves are hyperelliptic, finding, in particular, that over any number field we have nonhyperelliptic curves of all composite genera <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> independent integral elements in the kernel of the tame symbol. We also give families of elliptic curves over real quadratic fields with two independent integral elements.

articleTitle: Decay and Scattering for the Chern–Simons–Schrödinger Equations
abstract: We consider the Chern–Simons–Schrödinger model in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+2$</tex> dimensions, and prove scattering for small solutions of the Cauchy problem in the Coulomb gauge. This model is a gauge covariant Schrödinger equation, with a potential decaying like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r^{-1}$</tex> at infinity. To overcome the difficulties due to this long-range decay, we perform <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-based estimates covariantly. This procedure gives favorable commutation identities so that only curvature terms, which decay faster than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r^{-1}$</tex>, appear in our weighted energy estimates. We then select the Coulomb gauge to reveal a genuinely cubic null structure, which allows us to establish scattering to linear solutions by Fourier methods.

articleTitle: Localized Standard Versus Reduced Formula and Genus 1 Local Gromov–Witten Invariants
abstract: For local Calabi–Yau (CY) manifolds which are total spaces of vector bundle over algebraic Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifolds, we propose a formal definition of reduced genus 1 Gromov–Witten (GW) invariants, by assigning contributions from the refined decorated rooted trees. We show that this definition satisfies a localized version of the standard versus reduced (LSvR) formula, whose global version in the compact cases is due to Zinger. As an application, we prove the conjecture in a previous article on the genus 1 GW invariants of local CY manifolds which are total spaces of concave splitting vector bundles over projective spaces. In particular, we prove the mirror formulae for genus 1 GW invariants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{{\BBP}^{2}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{{\BBP}^{3}}$</tex>, conjectured by Klemm, Zaslow, and Pandharipande. In the appendix, we derive the modularity of genus 1 GW invariants for the local <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{2}$</tex> as a consequence of the results on Ramanujan's cubic transformation. Inspired by the LSvR formula, we show that the ordinary genus 1 GW invariants of CY hypersurfaces in projective spaces can be computed by virtual localization and quantum hyperplane property after the contribution of a genus 1 vertex is replaced by a modified one.

articleTitle: Deformations and Obstructions of Pairs (X, D)
abstract: We study infinitesimal deformations of pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,D)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> smooth projective variety and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> a smooth or a normal crossing divisor, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>. Using the differential-graded Lie algebras theory and the Cartan homotopy construction, we are able to prove in a completely algebraic way the unobstructedness of the deformations of the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,D)$</tex> in many cases, for example, whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,D)$</tex> is a log Calabi–Yau pair, in the case of a smooth divisor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> in a Calabi–Yau variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> is a smooth divisor in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|-m K_X|$</tex>, for some positive integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>.

articleTitle: Reconstruction and Convergence in Quantum K-Theory via Difference Equations
abstract: We give a new reconstruction method of big quantum K-ring based on the q-difference module structure in quantum K-theory [12, 13]. The q-difference structure yields commuting linear operators A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> i,com</inf> on the K-group as many as the Picard number of the target manifold. The genus-zero quantum K-theory can be reconstructed from the q-difference structure at the origin t=0 if the K-group is generated by a single element under the actions of A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> i,com</inf>. This method allows us to prove the convergence of the big quantum K-rings of certain manifolds, including the projective spaces and the complete flag manifold Fl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>.

articleTitle: Global Weyl Modules for Equivariant Map Algebras
abstract: Equivariant map algebras are Lie algebras of algebraic maps from a scheme (or algebraic variety) to a target finite-dimensional Lie algebra (in the case of the current paper, we assume the latter is a simple Lie algebra) that are equivariant with respect to the action of a finite group. In the first part of this paper, we define global Weyl modules for equivariant map algebras satisfying a mild assumption. We then identify a commutative algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}^{\lambda} _\Gamma $</tex> that acts naturally on the global Weyl modules, which leads to a Weyl functor from the category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}^{\lambda} _{\Gamma} $</tex>-modules to the category of modules for the equivariant map algebra in question. These definitions extend the ones previously given for generalized current algebras (i.e., untwisted map algebras) and twisted loop algebras. In the second part of the paper, we restrict our attention to equivariant map algebras where the group involved is abelian, acts on the target Lie algebra by diagram automorphisms, and freely on (the set of rational points of) the scheme. Under these additional assumptions, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}^{\lambda}_{\Gamma} $</tex> is finitely generated and the global Weyl module is a finitely generated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}^{\lambda}_{\Gamma} $</tex>-module. We also define local Weyl modules via the Weyl functor and prove that these coincide with the local Weyl modules defined directly in [18]. Finally, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}^{\lambda}_{\Gamma} $</tex> is the algebra of coinvariants of the analogous algebra in the untwisted case.

articleTitle: Stochastic Monotonicity in Young Graph and Thoma Theorem
abstract: We show that the order on probability measures, inherited from the dominance order on the Young diagrams, is preserved under natural maps reducing the number of boxes in a diagram by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>. As a corollary, we give a new proof of the Thoma theorem on the structure of characters of the infinite symmetric group. We present several conjectures generalizing our result. One of them (if it is true) would imply the Kerov's conjecture on the classification of all homomorphisms from the algebra of symmetric functions into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\BBR$</tex>, which are non-negative on Hall–Littlewood polynomials.

articleTitle: Statistics on Hilbert's 16th Problem
abstract: We study the statistics of the number of connected components and the volume of a random real algebraic hypersurface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}\hbox {P}^n$</tex> defined by a homogeneous polynomial f of degree d in the real Fubini–Study ensemble. We prove that for the expectation of the number of connected components, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${\BBE} b_0(Z_{{\BBR}\hbox{P}^n}(f))=\Theta(d^n), \qquad\qquad\qquad{(1)}$$</tex> the asymptotic being in d for n fixed. We do not restrict ourselves to the random homogeneous case, and we consider more generally random polynomials belonging to a window of eigenspaces of the Laplacian on the sphere S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, proving that the same asymptotic holds. As for the volume properties, we provide an exact formula: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${\BBE}\,\hbox{Vol}(Z_{{\BBR}\hbox{P}^n}(f)) =\delta^{1/2}\,\rm {Vol}(S^{n-1}), \qquad\qquad{(2)}$$</tex> where δ (which we specify exactly) is asymptotically a constant times d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Both Equations (1) and (2) exhibit expectation of maximal order in light of Milnor's bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_0(Z_{{\BBR}\hbox {P}^n}(f)) = O(d^n)$</tex> and the bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {Vol}(Z_{{\BBR}\hbox {P}^n}(f)) = O(d)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Renormalized Energy Equidistribution and Local Charge Balance in 2D Coulomb Systems
abstract: We consider two related problems: the first is the minimization of the “Coulomb renormalized energy” of Sandier–Serfaty, which corresponds to the total Coulomb interaction of point charges in a uniform neutralizing background (or rather variants of it). The second corresponds to the minimization of the Hamiltonian of a 2D “Coulomb gas” or “one-component plasma”, a system of n point charges with Coulomb pair interaction, in a confining potential (minimizers of this energy also correspond to “weighted Fekete sets”). In both cases, we investigate the microscopic structure of minimizers, that is, at the scale corresponding to the interparticle distance. We show that in any large enough microscopic set, the value of the energy and the number of points are “rigid” and completely determined by the macroscopic density of points. In other words, points and energy are “equidistributed” in space (modulo appropriate scalings). The number of points in a ball is in particular known up to an error proportional to the radius of the ball. We also prove a result on the maximal and minimal distances between points. Our approach involves fully exploiting the minimality by reducing to minimization problems with fixed boundary conditions posed on smaller subsets.

articleTitle: Rational Curves on Hyperkähler Manifolds
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> be an irreducible holomorphically symplectic manifold. We show that all faces of the Kähler cone of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> are hyperplanes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_i$</tex> orthogonal to certain homology classes, called monodromy birationally minimal (MBM) classes. Moreover, the Kähler cone is a connected component of a complement of the positive cone to the union of all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_i$</tex>. We provide several characterizations of the MBM classes. We show the invariance of MBM property by deformations, as long as the class in question stays of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,1)$</tex>. For hyperkähler manifolds with Picard group generated by a negative class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm z$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>-effective if and only if it is an MBM class. We also prove some results toward the Morrison–Kawamata cone conjecture for hyperkähler manifolds.

articleTitle: On the Grid Ramsey Problem and Related Questions
abstract: The Hales–Jewett theorem is one of the pillars of Ramsey theory, from which many other results follow. A celebrated theorem of Shelah says that Hales–Jewett numbers are primitive recursive. A key tool used in his proof, now known as the cube lemma, has become famous in its own right. In its simplest form, this lemma says that if we color the edges of the Cartesian product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_n \times K_n$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> colors, then, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> sufficiently large, there is a rectangle with both pairs of opposite edges receiving the same color. Shelah's proof shows that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n = r^{\left ({\matrix{r+1}\atop {2}}\right ) } +1$</tex> suffices. More than 20 years ago, Graham, Rothschild, and Spencer asked whether this bound can be improved to a polynomial in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>. We show that this is not possible by providing a superpolynomial lower bound in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>. We also discuss a number of related problems.

articleTitle: Quaternion-Sasakian Manifolds and Reduction
abstract: We introduce the process of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-Sasakian reduction and use isometric circle actions to reduce homogeneous examples when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=3,7$</tex>. We use circle and torus reduction to arrive at new quaternion-Sasakian manifolds.

articleTitle: Flow Polytopes of Signed Graphs and the Kostant Partition Function
abstract: We establish the relationship between volumes of flow polytopes associated to signed graphs and the Kostant partition function. A special case of this relationship, namely, when the graphs are signless, has been studied in detail by Baldoni and Vergne using techniques of residues. In contrast with their approach, we provide entirely combinatorial proofs inspired by the work of Postnikov and Stanley on flow polytopes. As an interesting special family of flow polytopes, we study the Chan–Robbins–Yuen (CRY) polytopes. Motivated by the volume formula <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi^{n-2}_{k=1}\ {\mathrm Cat}(k)$</tex> for the type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> version, where Cat(k) is the kth Catalan number, we introduce type C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</inf> and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</inf> CRY polytopes along with intriguing conjectures about their volumes.

articleTitle: Some Sharp Restriction Inequalities on the Sphere
abstract: In this paper, we find the sharp forms and characterize the complex-valued extremizers of the adjoint Fourier restriction inequalities on the sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\|\widehat {f \sigma }\|_{L^{p}({\BBR} ^{d})} \lesssim \|f\|_{L^{q}({\BBS} ^{d-1},\sigma )}$$</tex> in the cases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d,p,q) = (d,2k, q)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d,k \in {\BBN}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\in {\BBR} ^+ \cup {\{ }\infty {\} }$</tex> satisfying: (a) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k = 2$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \geq 2$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \leq d\leq 7$</tex>; (b) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k = 2$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \geq 4$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 8$</tex>; (c) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 3$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q \geq 2k$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \geq 2$</tex>. We also prove a sharp multilinear weighted restriction inequality, with weight related to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-fold convolution of the surface measure.

articleTitle: Polynomial Functors from Algebras Over a Set-Operad and Nonlinear Mackey Functors
abstract: In this paper, we give a description of polynomial functors from (finitely generated free) groups to abelian groups in terms of nonlinear Mackey functors, generalizing those given in a paper of Baues–Dreckmann–Franjou–Pirashvili published in 2001. This description is a consequence of our two main results: a description of functors from (finitely generated free) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {P}}$</tex>-algebras (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {P}}$</tex> a set-operad) to abelian groups in terms of nonlinear Mackey functors and the isomorphism between polynomial functors on (finitely generated free) monoids and those on (finitely generated free) groups. Polynomial functors from (finitely generated free) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {P}}$</tex>-algebras to abelian groups and from (finitely generated free) groups to abelian groups are described explicitly by their cross-effects and maps relating them which satisfy a list of relations.

articleTitle: The Deficiency of being a Congruence Group for Veech Groups of Origamis
abstract: We study “how far away” a finite index subgroup Γ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {SL}}_2({\BBZ})$</tex> is from being a congruence group. For this, we define its deficiency of being a congruence group. We show that the index of the image of Γ in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {SL}}_2({\BBZ}/n{\BBZ})$</tex> is the biggest, if n is the general Wohlfahrt level. We, furthermore, show that the Veech groups of origamis (or square-tiled surfaces) in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}_{2}(2)$</tex> are far away from being congruence groups and that in each genus 1 finds an infinite family of origamis such that they are “as far as possible” from being a congruence group.

articleTitle: Higher-Dimensional Solutions for a Nonuniformly Elliptic Equation
abstract: We prove m-dimensional symmetry results, which we call m-Liouville theorems, for stable and monotone solutions of the following nonuniformly elliptic equation: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$-{\mathrm div}(\gamma({\mathrm x}')\nabla u({\mathrm x}))=\lambda ({\mathrm x}')f(u({\mathrm x}))\quad {\mathrm for}\ {\mathrm x}=({\mathrm x}',{\mathrm x}'')\in{\mathrm R}^d\times {\mathrm R}^s={\mathrm R}^n,$$</tex> where 0≤m<n and 0<λ,γ are smooth functions and f∈C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(R). The interesting fact is that the decay assumptions on the weight function γ(x′) play the fundamental role in deriving m-Liouville theorems. We show that, under certain assumptions on the sign of the nonlinearity f, the above equation satisfies a 0-Liouville theorem. More importantly, we prove that, for the double-well potential nonlinearities, that is, f(u)=u−u<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the above equation satisfies a (d+1)-Liouville theorem. This can be considered as a higher-dimensional counterpart of the celebrated conjecture of De Giorgi for the Allen–Cahn equation. The remarkable phenomenon is that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm tanh}$</tex> function that is the profile of monotone and bounded solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation appears towards constructing higher-dimensional Liouville theorems.

articleTitle: Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the 3D Ginzburg–Landau Superconductivity Model
abstract: We prove the uniqueness of weak solutions of the 3D time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau model for superconductivity with L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> initial data in the case of Coulomb and type I Lorentz gauges.

articleTitle: Linear Growth for Certain Elliptic Fibrations
abstract: We prove that the number of rational points of bounded height on certain del Pezzo surfaces of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> grows linearly, as predicted by Manin's conjecture.

articleTitle: A Diagrammatic Categorification of a Clifford Algebra
abstract: We give a graphical calculus for a categorification of a Clifford algebra and its Fock space representation via differential graded categories. The categorical action is motivated by the gluing action between Honda's contact categories of infinite strips.

articleTitle: On the Moduli Description of Local Models for Ramified Unitary Groups
abstract: Local models are schemes which are intended to model the étale-local structure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic integral models of Shimura varieties. Pappas and Zhu have recently given a general group-theoretic construction of flat local models with parahoric level structure for any tamely ramified group, but it remains an interesting problem to characterize the local models, when possible, in terms of an explicit moduli problem. In the setting of local models for ramified, quasi-split <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GU_n$</tex>, work toward an explicit moduli description was initiated in the general framework of Rapoport and Zink's book and was subsequently advanced by Pappas and Pappas–Rapoport. In this paper, we propose a further refinement to their moduli problem, which we show is both necessary and sufficient to characterize the (flat) local model in a certain special maximal parahoric case with signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n-1,1)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Characteristic Laplacian in Sub-Riemannian Geometry
abstract: We study a Laplacian operator related to the characteristic cohomology of a smooth manifold endowed with a distribution. We prove that this Laplacian does not behave very well: it is not hypoelliptic in general and does not respect the bigrading on forms in a complex setting. We also discuss the consequences of these negative results for a conjecture of P. Griffiths, concerning the characteristic cohomology of period domains.

articleTitle: On the Discrete Functional Lp Minkowski Problem
abstract: The discrete functional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_p$</tex> Minkowski problem is posed and solved. As a consequence, the general affine Pólya–Szegö principle and the general affine Sobolev inequalities are established.

articleTitle: Polynomials and Primes in Generalized Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: We provide upper bounds on the density of a symmetric generalized arithmetic progression lacking nonzero elements of the form h(n) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\in {\BBN}$</tex> or h(p) with p prime for appropriate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h\in {\BBZ}[x]$</tex>. The prime variant can be interpreted as a multi-dimensional, polynomial extension of Linnik’s theorem.

articleTitle: Flat Bundles and Hyper-Hodge Decomposition on Solvmanifolds
abstract: We study rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> flat bundles over solvmanifolds whose cohomologies are nontrivial. By using Hodge theoretical properties for all topologically trivial rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> flat bundles, we represent the structure theorem of Kähler solvmanifolds as extensions of Hasegawa's result and Benson–Gordon's result for nilmanifolds.

articleTitle: Reductive Linear Differential Algebraic Groups and the Galois Groups of Parameterized Linear Differential Equations
abstract: We develop the representation theory for reductive linear differential algebraic groups (LDAGs). In particular, we exhibit an explicit sharp upper bound for orders of derivatives in differential representations of reductive LDAGs, extending existing results, which were obtained for SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the case of just one derivation. As an application of the above bound, we develop an algorithm that tests whether the parameterized differential Galois group of a system of linear differential equations is reductive and, if it is, calculates it.

articleTitle: Convergence Groups are not Invariably Generated
abstract: It was conjectured by Kantor, Lubotzky and Shalev that nonelementary word hyperbolic groups are never invariably generated. We show that this is indeed the case even for the much larger class of convergence groups.

articleTitle: The Distribution of the Variance of Primes in Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: Hooley conjectured that the variance V (x;q) of the distribution of primes up to x in the arithmetic progressions modulo q is asymptotically <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\log q$</tex>, in some unspecified range of q≤x. On average over 1≤q≤Q, this conjecture is known unconditionally in the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x/(\log x)^A \leq Q \leq x$</tex>; this last range can be improved to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x^{{1\over 2}+\epsilon } \leq Q \leq x$</tex> under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Keating and Rudnick established a function field analog of Hooley's Conjecture which suggests that it holds in the wider range x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ϵ</sup>≤q≤x. We argue that Hooley's conjecture should hold down to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\log \log x)^{1+o(1)} \leq q \leq x$</tex> for all values of q, and that this range is best possible. We show under GRH and a linear independence hypothesis on the zeros of Dirichlet L-functions that for moderate values of q, ϕ(q) e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−y</sup>V (e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup>;q) has the same distribution as that of a certain random variable of mean asymptotically <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi (q)\log q$</tex> and of variance asymptotically <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\phi (q)(\log q)^2$</tex>. Our estimates on the large deviations of this random variable allow us to predict the range of validity of Hooley's Conjecture.

articleTitle: Extensions of Büchi's Higher Powers Problem to Positive Characteristic
abstract: Büchi's nth power problem on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBQ}}$</tex> asks whether there exist an integer M such that the only monic polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F\in {{\BBQ}}[X]$</tex> of degree n satisfying that F(1),…,F(M) are nth power rational numbers, are precisely of the form F(X)=(X+c)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c\in {{\BBQ}}$</tex>. In this paper, we study analogs of this problem for algebraic function fields of positive characteristic. We formulate and prove an analog (indeed, such a formulation for n>2 was missing in the literature due to some unexpected phenomena), which we use to derive some definability and undecidability consequences. Moreover, in the case of characteristic zero, we extend some known results by improving the bounds for M (from quadratic on n to linear on n).

articleTitle: Commutative Formal Groups Arising from Schemes
abstract: We prove the following criterion for the pro-representability of the deformation cohomology of a commutative formal Lie group. Let f be a flat morphism between Noetherian schemes. Assume that the target of f is flat over the integers. For a commutative formal Lie group E, we have the deformation cohomology of f with coefficients in E at our disposal. If the higher direct images of the tangent space of E are locally free and of finite rank then the deformation cohomology is pro-representable by a commutative formal Lie group.

articleTitle: The Number of Roots of Polynomials of Large Degree in a Prime Field
abstract: We establish asymptotic upper bounds on the number of roots modulo p of some polynomials with rational coefficients, with p an arbitrarily large prime numbers, using a variant of Stepanov's method. The polynomials we consider have degree of size close to p and are obtained by truncating power series of polylogarithms, polyexponentials, and Bessel functions. This answers a question of Heath-Brown.

articleTitle: Irreducible Components of Deformation Spaces: Wild 2-Adic Exercises
abstract: We prove that the irreducible components of the space of framed deformations of the trivial two-dimensional mod 2 representation of the absolute Galois group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}_2$</tex> are in natural bijection with those of the trivial character, confirming a conjecture of Böckle. We deduce from this result that crystalline points are Zariski dense in that space: this provides the missing ingredient for the surjectivity of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_2({\BBQ}_p)$</tex> in the case p=2 (the result was already known for p≥3).

articleTitle: Algebro-Geometric Solution to the Bullough–Dodd–Zhiber–Shabat Equation
abstract: Based on solutions of the stationary zero-curvature equation associated with a 3×3 matrix spectral problem, we introduce a trigonal curve related to the Bullough–Dodd–Zhiber–Shabat equation and define Baker–Akhiezer functions and appropriate meromorphic function on the trigonal curve. Resorting to the algebro-geometric characters of the trigonal curve and properties of the three kinds of Abel differentials, we arrive at the explicit Riemann theta function representations of the Baker–Akhiezer functions and the meromorphic function. The algebro-geometric solution for the Bullough–Dodd–Zhiber–Shabat equation is obtained with the help of the asymptotic properties of the meromorphic function.

articleTitle: Energy Integrals and Metric Embedding Theory
abstract: For some centrally symmetric convex bodies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\subset {\BBR}^n$</tex>, we study the energy integral <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\sup \int _{K} \int _{K} \|x - y\|_r^{p}\, {\rm d} \mu (x) \,{\rm d} \mu (y),$$</tex> where the supremum runs over all finite signed Borel measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> of total mass one. In the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K = B_q^n$</tex>, the unit ball of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell _q^n$</tex> (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \lt q \leq 2$</tex>) or an ellipsoid, we obtain the exact value or the correct asymptotical behavior of the supremum of these integrals. We apply these results to a classical embedding problem in metric geometry. We consider in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}^n$</tex> the Euclidean distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt \alpha \lt 1$</tex>, we estimate the minimum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> for which the snowflaked metric space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(K, d_2^{\alpha })$</tex> may be isometrically embedded on the surface of a Hilbert sphere of radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>.

articleTitle: Rank of Divisors on Hyperelliptic Curves and Graphs Under Specialization
abstract: Let (G,ω) be a hyperelliptic vertex-weighted graph of genus g≥2. We give a characterization of (G,ω) for which there exists a smooth projective curve X of genus g over a complete discrete valuation field with reduction graph (G,ω) such that the ranks of any divisors are preserved under specialization. We explain, for a given vertex-weighted graph (G,ω) in general, how the existence of such X relates the Riemann–Roch formulae for X and (G,ω), and also how the existence of such X is related to a problem by Caporaso.

articleTitle: Reduction Theorem for Lattice Cohomology
abstract: The lattice cohomology of a plumbed 3-manifold M associated with a connected negative definite plumbing graph is an important tool in the study of topological properties of M and in the comparison of the topological properties with analytic ones, whenever M is realized as complex analytic singularity link. By definition, its computation is based on the (Riemann–Roch) weights of the lattice points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}^s$</tex>, where s is the number of vertices of the plumbing graph. The present article reduces the rank of this lattice to the number of “bad” vertices of the graph. Usually, the geometry/topology of M is codified exactly by these “bad” vertices via surgery or other constructions. Their number measures how far is the plumbing graph from a rational one (or, how far is M from an L-space). The effect of the reduction appears also at the level of certain multivariable (topological Poincaré) series. Since from these series, one can also read the Seiberg–Witten invariants, the Reduction Theorem provides new formulae for these invariants too. The reduction also implies the vanishing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^q=0$</tex> of the lattice cohomology for q≥ν, where ν is the number of “bad” vertices. (This bound is sharp.)

articleTitle: Restriction Bounds for the Free Resolvent and Resonances in Lossy Scattering
abstract: We establish high energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex> estimates for the restriction of the free Green's function to hypersurfaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR} ^d$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\ge 1$</tex>. As an application, we estimate the size of a logarithmic resonance-free region for scattering by potentials of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V\otimes \delta _{\Gamma }$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \subset {\BBR} ^d$</tex> is a finite union of compact subsets of embedded hypersurfaces. In odd dimensions, we prove a resonance expansion for solutions to the wave equation with such a potential.

articleTitle: Mass Formulas for Local Galois Representations and Quotient Singularities. I: A Comparison of Counting Functions
abstract: We study a relation between the Artin conductor and the weight coming from the motivic integration over wild Deligne–Mumford stacks. As an application, we prove some version of the McKay correspondence, which relates Bhargava's mass formula for extensions of a local field and the Hilbert scheme of points.

articleTitle: Hodge Structures of Type (n, 0, …, 0, n)
abstract: This paper determines all the possible endomorphism algebras for polarizable Q-Hodge structures with Hodge numbers (n,0,…,0,n). This generalizes the classification of the possible endomorphism algebras of abelian varieties by Albert and Shimura. As with abelian varieties, the most interesting feature of the classification is that in certain cases, every Hodge structure on which a given algebra acts must have extra endomorphisms.

articleTitle: Finite Energy Local Well-Posedness for the Yang–Mills–Higgs Equations in Lorenz Gauge
abstract: The Yang–Mills–Higgs equations (Y–M–H), when written relative to Lorenz gauge, become a system of nonlinear wave equations. The key bilinear terms in the resulting system turn out to be null forms—this is in light of a recent discovery of null structure by Selberg and the present author for Yang–Mills equations in Lorenz gauge. Using the null structure found and bilinear space-time estimates, we prove local well-posedness of Y–M–H in Lorenz gauge for finite energy data.

articleTitle: A Symmetry Problem for the Infinity Laplacian
abstract: Aim of this paper is to prove necessary and sufficient conditions on the geometry of a domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset {\BBR} ^n$</tex> in order that the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for the infinity-Laplace equation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> with constant source term admits a viscosity solution depending only on the distance from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial \Omega$</tex>. This problem was previously addressed and studied by Buttazzo and Kawohl [7]. In the light of some geometrical achievements reached in our recent paper [14], we revisit the results obtained in [7] and we prove strengthened versions of them, where any regularity assumption on the domain and on the solution is removed. Our results require a delicate analysis based on viscosity methods. In particular, we need to build suitable viscosity test functions, whose construction involves a new estimate of the distance function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{\partial \Omega }$</tex> near singular points.

articleTitle: On p-adic L-Functions for GL (n) × GL (n-1) Over Totally Real Fields
abstract: We refine and extend previous constructions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions for Rankin–Selberg convolutions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {\rm {GL}} (n)\times \rm {\rm {GL}} (n-1)$</tex> to the case of cuspidal regular algebraic representations of finite slope over totally real fields without any restrictions on class numbers or the residual characteristic. We also prove an intrinsic functional equation for these <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions, which will be of interest in further study of their arithmetic properties.

articleTitle: Connection Problem for the Sine-Gordon/Painlevé III Tau Function and Irregular Conformal Blocks
abstract: The short-distance expansion of the tau function of the radial sine-Gordon/Painlevé III equation is given by a convergent series which involves irregular <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c=1$</tex> conformal blocks and possesses certain periodicity properties with respect to monodromy data. The long-distance irregular expansion exhibits a similar periodicity with respect to a different pair of coordinates on the monodromy manifold. This observation is used to conjecture an exact expression for the connection constant providing relative normalization of the two series. Up to an elementary prefactor, it is given by the generating function of the canonical transformation between the two sets of coordinates.

articleTitle: Sasakian Nilmanifolds
abstract: We prove that a compact nilmanifold admits a Sasakian structure if and only if it is a compact quotient of the generalized Heisenberg group of odd dimension by a cocompact discrete subgroup.

articleTitle: Boundary Gradient Estimates for Parabolic and Elliptic Systems from Linear Laminates
abstract: We study boundary gradient estimates for second-order divergence form parabolic and elliptic systems in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{1,\sigma }$</tex>-domains. The coefficients and data are assumed to be Hölder in the time variable and all but one spatial variables. This type of systems arises from the problems of linearly elastic laminates and composite materials.

articleTitle: On Deformation Quantization of Poisson–Lie Groups and Moduli Spaces of Flat Connections
abstract: We give simple explicit formulas for deformation quantization of Poisson–Lie groups and of similar Poisson manifolds which can be represented as moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces. The star products depend on a choice of Drinfeld associator and are obtained by applying certain monoidal functors (fusion and reduction) to commutative algebras in Drinfeld categories. From a geometric point of view, this construction can be understood as a quantization of the quasi-Poisson structures on moduli spaces of flat connections.

articleTitle: On the Second Nilpotent Quotient of Higher Homotopy Groups, for Hypersolvable Arrangements
abstract: We examine the first nonvanishing higher homotopy group, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _p$</tex>, of the complement of a hypersolvable, nonsupersolvable, complex hyperplane arrangement, as a module over the group ring of the fundamental group, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}\pi _1$</tex>. We give a presentation for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>-adic completion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _p$</tex>. We deduce that the second nilpotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>-adic quotient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _p$</tex> is determined by the combinatorics of the arrangement, and we give a combinatorial formula for the second associated graded piece, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm gr}^1_I \pi _p$</tex>. We relate the torsion of this graded piece to the dimensions of the minimal generating systems of the Orlik–Solomon ideal of the arrangement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {A}$</tex> in degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p+2$</tex>, for various field coefficients. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {A}$</tex> is associated to a finite simple graph, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm gr}^1_I \pi _p$</tex> is torsion-free, with rank explicitly computable from the graph.

articleTitle: Analysis of Blow-up Locus and Existence of Weak Solutions for Nonlinear Supercritical Problems
abstract: We give a qualitative analysis of sequences of stationary solutions to the supercritical problem <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$-\Delta u= |u|^{p-1} u \quad \hbox{in}\ \Omega,\quad p \gt {n+2}{ \over n-2}.$$</tex> A consequence of the analysis is the existence of positive singular weak solutions on a convex domain when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \in \big ({n+2 \over n-2}, {n+1 \over n-3}\big)$</tex>, with only isolated singularities.

articleTitle: Weak Approximation for Tori Over p-adic Function Fields
abstract: We study local–global questions for Galois cohomology over the function field of a curve defined over a p-adic field, the main focus being weak approximation of rational points. We construct a 9-term Poitou–Tate-type exact sequence for tori over a field as above (and also a 12-term sequence for finite modules). Like in the number field case, part of the sequence can then be used to analyze the defect of weak approximation for a torus. We also show that the defect of weak approximation is controlled by a certain subgroup of the third unramified cohomology group of the torus.

articleTitle: The Covariance of Almost-Primes in 𝔽q[T]
abstract: We estimate the covariance in counts of almost-primes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBF}_q[T]$</tex>, weighted by higher-order von Mangoldt functions. The answer takes a pleasant algebraic form. This generalizes recent work of Keating and Rudnick that estimates the variance of primes, and makes use, as theirs, of a recent equidistribution result of Katz. In an Appendix, we prove some related identities for random matrix statistics, which allows us to give a quick proof of a 2×2 ratio theorem for the characteristic polynomial of the unitary group. We additionally identify arithmetic functions whose statistics mimic those of hook Schur functions.

articleTitle: There Exist Non-CM Hilbert Modular Forms of Partial Weight 1
abstract: In this note, we prove that there exists a conjugate pair of classical Hilbert modular cuspidal eigenforms over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bf{Q}(\sqrt {5})$</tex> of partial weight 1 which do not arise from the induction of a Grössencharacter from a complex multiplication extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bf{Q}(\sqrt {5})$</tex>.

articleTitle: On An Elliptic Equation Arising from Photo-Acoustic Imaging in Inhomogeneous Media
abstract: We study an elliptic equation with measurable coefficients arising from photo-acoustic imaging in inhomogeneous media. We establish Hölder continuity of weak solutions and obtain pointwise bounds for Green's functions subject to Dirichlet or Neumann condition.

articleTitle: Erratum to “Support Varieties and Representation Type of Small Quantum Groups”
abstract: Some of the general results in the paper require an additional hypothesis, such as quasitriangularity. Applications to specific types of Hopf algebras are correct, as some of these are quasitriangular, and for those that are not, the Hochschild support variety theory may be applied instead.

articleTitle: Effective Reconstruction of Generic Genus 4 Curves from Their Theta Hyperplanes
abstract: Effective reconstruction formulas of a curve from its theta hyperplanes are known classically in genus 2 (where the theta hyperplanes are Weierstrass points), and 3 (where, for a generic curve, the theta hyperplanes are bitangents to a plane quartic). However, for higher genera, no formula or algorithm is known. In this paper, we give an explicit (and simple) algorithm for computing a generic genus 4 curve from its theta hyperplanes.

articleTitle: Twisting of Affine Algebraic Groups, I
abstract: We continue the study of twisting of affine algebraic groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> (i.e., of Hopf <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-cocycles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> for the function algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)$</tex>), which was started in [7, 8], and initiate the study of the associated one-sided twisted function algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)_J$</tex>. We first show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is supported on a closed subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> (defined up to conjugation), and that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)_J$</tex> is finitely generated with center <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G/H)$</tex>. We then use it to study the structure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)_J$</tex> for connected nilpotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. We show that, in this case, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)_J$</tex> is a Noetherian domain, which is a simple algebra if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is supported on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, and describe the simple algebras that arise in this way. We also use [8] to obtain a classification of Hopf <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-cocycles for connected nilpotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, hence of fiber functors <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {Rep}} (G)\to {\rm {Vect}}$</tex>. Along the way we provide many examples, and at the end formulate several ring-theoretical questions about the structure of the algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}(G)_J$</tex> for arbitrary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>.

articleTitle: Zeros of Large Degree Vorob’ev–Yablonski Polynomials via a Hankel Determinant Identity
abstract: In the present paper, we derive a new Hankel determinant representation for the square of the Vorob’ev–Yablonski polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}_n(x),x\in {\BBC}$</tex>. These polynomials are the major ingredients in the construction of rational solutions to the second Painlevé equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{xx}=xu+2u^3+ \alpha$</tex>. As an application of the new identity, we study the zero distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}_n(x)$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\rightarrow \infty$</tex> by asymptotically analyzing a certain collection of (pseudo)-orthogonal polynomials connected to the aforementioned Hankel determinant. Our approach reproduces recently obtained results in the same context by Buckingham and Miller [3], which used the Jimbo–Miwa Lax representation of PII equation and the asymptotic analysis thereof.

articleTitle: Fano Varieties with Small Non-klt Locus
abstract: Let X be a Fano variety of index k such that the non-klt locus Nklt(X) is not empty. We prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim {\rm {Nklt}}(X) \geq k-1$</tex> and equality holds if and only if Nklt(X) is a linear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{k-1}$</tex>. In this case, X has lc singularities and is a generalized cone with Nklt(X) as vertex. If X has lc singularities and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim {\rm {Nklt}}(X)=k$</tex> we describe the non-klt locus Nklt(X) and the global geometry of X. Moreover, we construct examples to show that all the classification results are effective.

articleTitle: Super Duality and Crystal Bases for Quantum Ortho-Symplectic Superalgebras
abstract: We introduce a semisimple tensor category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {O}^{\rm int}_q(m|n)$</tex> of modules over a quantum ortho-symplectic superalgebra. It is a natural counterpart of the category of finitely dominated integrable modules over the quantum classical (super) algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{m+n}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{m+n}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_{m+n}$</tex>, or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(0,m+n)$</tex> from a viewpoint of super duality. We classify the irreducible modules in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {O}^{\rm int}_q(m|n)$</tex> and show that an irreducible module in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {O}^{\rm int}_q(m|n)$</tex> has a unique crystal base in case of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>. An explicit description of the crystal graph is given in terms of a new combinatorial object called ortho-symplectic tableaux. Communicated by Prof. Weiqiang Wang

articleTitle: A Log-Free Zero-Density Estimate and Small Gaps in Coefficients of L-Functions
abstract: Let L(s,π×π′) be the Rankin–Selberg L-function attached to automorphic representations π and π′. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {\pi }$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde {\pi }'$</tex> denote the contragredient representations associated to π and π′. Under the assumption of certain upper bounds for coefficients of the logarithmic derivatives of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(s, \pi \times \tilde {\pi })$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(s, \pi '\times \tilde {\pi }')$</tex>, we prove a log-free zero-density estimate for L(s,π×π′) which generalizes a result due to Fogels in the context of Dirichlet L-functions. We then employ this log-free estimate in studying the distribution of the Fourier coefficients of an automorphic representation π. As an application, we examine the nonlacunarity of the Fourier coefficients b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>(p) of a modular newform <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(z)=\sum _{n=1}^{\infty } b_f(n) \,{\rm {e}}^{{2\pi {\rm i} n z}}$</tex> of weight k, level N, and character χ. More precisely, for f(z) and a prime p, set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j_f(p):=\max _{x;x \gt p} J_{f} (p, x)$</tex>, where J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>(p,x):=#{prime q; a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf>(q)=0 for all p<q≤x}. We prove that j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>(p)≪<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f,θ</inf>p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sup> for some 0<θ<1.

articleTitle: Large Data Local Well-Posedness for a Class of KdV-Type Equations II
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for an equation of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\partial _t+ \partial _x^3)u=F(u,u_x,u_{xx})$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is a polynomial with no constant or linear terms and no quadratic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$uu_{xx}$</tex> term. For a polynomial nonlinearity with no quadratic terms, Kenig–Ponce–Vega proved local well-posedness in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^s$</tex> for large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>. In this paper, we prove local well-posedness in low regularity Sobolev spaces and extend the result to certain quadratic nonlinearities. The result is based on spaces and estimates similar to those used by Marzuola–Metcalfe–Tataru for quasilinear Schrödinger equations.

articleTitle: A Scale Invariant Form of a Critical Hardy Inequality
abstract: We present a new form of the logarithmic Hardy inequality on the unit ball in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^N$</tex> with its optimal constant. One of the novelties of our inequality is the scale invariance under the natural scaling. We also discuss the nonexistence of a minimizer for an associated minimizing problem via a scaling argument.

articleTitle: Surfaces in 4-Manifolds: Concordance, Isotopy, and Surgery
abstract: In this paper, we will show that two surfaces of the same genus and homology class in a simply connected 4-manifold are concordant. We will show they are often topologically isotopic when their complements have cyclic fundamental group. Finally, we will show that if they are 0-concordant, then surgery on one is equivalent to surgery on the other.

articleTitle: A Remark on Solutions of the Pell Equation
abstract: The main purpose of this note is to provide a nontrivial bound on certain Kloosterman sums as considered in the recent paper of Fouvry [4], leading to a small improvement of his result on the Pell equation.

articleTitle: Some Arithmetic Dynamics of Diagonally Split Polynomial Maps
abstract: Let n≥2, and let f be a polynomial of degree at least 2 with coefficients in a number field or a characteristic 0 function field K. We present two arithmetic applications of a recent theorem of Medvedev–Scanlon to the dynamics of the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f,...,f):\ (\mathbb P^1_K)^n\rightarrow(\mathbb P^1_K)^n$</tex>, namely the dynamical analogs of the Hasse principle and the Bombieri–Masser–Zannier height bound theorem. In particular, we prove that the Hasse principle holds when we intersect an orbit and a preperiodic subvariety, and that points in the intersection of a curve with the union of all periodic hypersurfaces have bounded heights unless that curve is vertical or contained in a periodic hypersurface.

articleTitle: On Topological Upper-Bounds on the Number of Small Cuspidal Eigenvalues of Hyperbolic Surfaces of Finite Area
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> be a noncompact, finite area hyperbolic surface of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(g, n)$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta _S$</tex> denote the Laplace operator on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>. As <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> varies over the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {M}_{g, n}}$</tex> of finite area hyperbolic surfaces of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(g, n)$</tex>, we study, adapting methods of Ji [8] and Wolpert [15], the behavior of small cuspidal eigenpairs of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta _S$</tex>.
