In Theorem 1.7, we describe limiting behavior of these eigenpairs on surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${S_m} \in {\cal {M}_{g, n}}$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({S_m})$</tex> converges to a point in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\cal {M}}_{g, n}$</tex>. Then, we consider the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>th cuspidal eigenvalue, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lambda ^c_i}(S)$</tex>, of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S \in {\cal {M}_{g, n}}$</tex>. Since noncuspidal eigenfunctions (residual eigenfunctions or generalized eigenfunctions) may converge to cuspidal eigenfunctions, it is not known if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lambda ^c_i}(S)$</tex> is a continuous function. However, applying Theorem 1.7 we prove that, for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 2g-2$</tex>, the sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${{\cal{C}_{g, n}^{{1 \over 4}}}}(k)= \Big\{ S \in {\cal{M}_{g, n}}: {\lambda_k^c}(S) \gt {1 \over 4} \Big\}$$</tex> are open and contain a neighborhood of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bigcup _{i=1}^n{\cal {M}_{0, 3}} \cup {\cal {M}_{g-1, 2}}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\cal {M}}_{g, n}$</tex>. Moreover, using topological properties of nodal sets of small eigenfunctions from [12], we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal {C}_{g, n}^{{1 \over 4}}}}(2g-1)$</tex> contains a neighborhood of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {M}_{0, n+1}} \cup {\cal {M}_{g, 1}}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\cal {M}}_{g, n}$</tex>. These results provide evidence in support of a conjecture of Otal and Rosas [13].

articleTitle: Remarks on a Liouville-Type Theorem for Beltrami Flows
abstract: We present a simple, short, and elementary proof that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex> is a Beltrami flow with a finite energy in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\BBR^3$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=0$</tex>. In the case of the Beltrami flows satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v\in L^\infty _{loc} (\BBR^3) \cap L^q(\BBR^3)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\in [2, 3)$</tex>, or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|v(x)|=O(1/|x|^{1+ \varepsilon })$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \gt 0$</tex>, we provide a different, simple proof that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=0$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Closure of the Tame Automorphism Group of Affine Three-Space
abstract: We provide explicit families of tame automorphisms of the complex affine three-space which degenerate to wild automorphisms. This shows that the tame subgroup of the group of polynomial automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBC}}^3$</tex> is not closed, when the latter is seen as an infinite-dimensional algebraic group.

articleTitle: Reversed Hardy–Littewood–Sobolev Inequality
abstract: In this paper, we obtain a reversed Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev inequality: for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt p,\ t \lt 1,$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda =n-\alpha \lt 0$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/p +1 /t+ \lambda /n=2$</tex>, there is a best constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N(n,\lambda ,p) \gt 0$</tex>, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\left |\int _{{\BBR}^n} \int _{{\BBR}^n} f(x)|x-y|^{-\lambda } g(y) \,{{\rm d}}x \,{{\rm d}}y\right |\ge N(n,\lambda ,p) \|f\|_{L^p({\BBR}^n)}\|g\|_{L^t({\BBR}^n)}$$</tex> holds for all nonnegative functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in L^p({\BBR}^n),\ g\in L^t({\BBR}^n)$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=t$</tex>, we prove the existence of extremal functions, classify all extremal functions via the method of moving sphere, and compute the best constant.

articleTitle: Rotor-Routing and Spanning Trees on Planar Graphs
abstract: The sandpile group Pic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(G) of a finite graph G is a discrete analog of the Jacobian of a Riemann surface which was rediscovered several times in the contexts of arithmetic geometry, self-organized criticality, random walks, and algorithms. Given a ribbon graph G, Holroyd et al. used the “rotor-routing” model to define a free and transitive action of Pic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(G) on the set of spanning trees of G. However, their construction depends a priori on a choice of basepoint vertex. Ellenberg asked whether this action does in fact depend on the choice of basepoint. We answer this question by proving that the action of Pic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>(G) is independent of the basepoint if and only if G is a planar ribbon graph.

articleTitle: The Dimension of Affine Deligne–Lusztig Varieties in the Affine Grassmannian
abstract: We calculate the dimension of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties inside the affine Grassmannian of an arbitrary reductive connected group over a finite field. Our result generalizes the dimension formula for split groups, which was determined by the works of Görtz, Haines, Kottwitz, and Reuman and Viehmann.

articleTitle: Nonproper Complete Minimal Surfaces Embedded in ℍ2 × ℝ
abstract: Examples of complete minimal surfaces properly embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^2\times {\BBR}$</tex> have been extensively studied and the literature contains a plethora of nontrivial ones. In this paper, we construct a large class of examples of complete minimal surfaces embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^2\times {\BBR}$</tex>, not necessarily proper, which are invariant by a vertical translation or by a screw motion. In particular, we construct a large family of nonproper complete minimal disks embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^2\times {\BBR}$</tex> invariant by a vertical translation and a screw motion and whose importance is two-fold. They have finite total curvature in the quotient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^2\times {\BBR}$</tex> by the isometry, thus highlighting a very different behavior from minimal surfaces embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^3$</tex> satisfying the same properties. They show that the Calabi–Yau conjectures for embedded minimal surfaces do not hold in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^2\times {\BBR}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Bernstein- and Markov-Type Inequalities for Trigonometric Polynomials on General Sets
abstract: Bernstein- and Markov-type inequalities are discussed for the derivatives of trigonometric and algebraic polynomials on general subsets of the real axis and of the unit circle. It has recently been proved by A. Lukashov that the sharp Bernstein factor for trigonometric polynomials is the equilibrium density of the image of the set on the unit circle under the mapping t→e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">it</sup>. In this paper, Lukashov's theorem is extended to entire functions of exponential type using a result of Achieser and Levin. The asymptotically sharp Markov factors for trigonometric polynomials on several intervals is also found via the so-called T-sets of F. Peherstorfer and R. Steinbauer. This sharp Markov factor is again intimately connected with the equilibrium measure of the aforementioned image set.

articleTitle: Sphere Equivalence, Banach Expanders, and Extrapolation
abstract: We study the Banach spectral gap λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(G;X,p) of finite graphs G for pairs (X,p) of Banach spaces and exponents. We define the notion of sphere equivalence between Banach spaces and show a generalization of Matoušek's extrapolation for Banach spaces sphere equivalent to uniformly convex ones. As a byproduct, we prove that expanders are automatically expanders with respect to (X,p) for any X sphere equivalent to a uniformly curved Banach space and for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\in (1,\infty)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Schur–Weyl Duality for Deligne Categories
abstract: This paper gives an analog to the classical Schur–Weyl duality in the setting of Deligne categories. Given a finite-dimensional unital vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> (i.e., a vector space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> with a distinguished nonzero vector <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{1}}}$</tex>), we give a definition of a complex tensor power of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>. This is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Ind}$</tex>-object of the Deligne category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline {{\rm Rep}}(S_{t})$</tex> equipped with a natural action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur {gl}}}(V)$</tex>. This construction allows us to describe a duality between the abelian envelope of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline {{\rm Rep}}(S_{t})$</tex> and a localization of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{O}}^{\Fraktur {p}}_{V}$</tex> (the parabolic category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{O}}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur {gl}}}(V)$</tex> associated with the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V, { {{1}}})$</tex>). In particular, we obtain an exact contravariant functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {{\rm SW}}_{t}$</tex> from the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline {{\rm Rep}}^{\rm ab}(S_{t})$</tex> (the abelian envelope of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline {{\rm Rep}}(S_{t})$</tex>) to a certain quotient of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{O}}^{\Fraktur {p}}_{V}$</tex>. This quotient, denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat {{{O}}}^{\Fraktur {p}}_{t, V}$</tex>, is obtained by taking the full subcategory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{O}}^{\Fraktur {p}}_{V}$</tex> consisting of modules of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>, and localizing by the subcategory of finite-dimensional modules. It turns out that the contravariant functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {{\rm SW}}_{t}$</tex> makes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat {{{O}}}^{\Fraktur {p}}_{t, V}$</tex> a Serre quotient of the category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline {{\rm Rep}}^{\rm ab}(S_{t})^{\rm op}$</tex>, and the kernel of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {{\rm SW}}_{t}$</tex> can be explicitly described.

articleTitle: Refinements of the One Dimensional Free Poincaré Inequality
abstract: We present two extensions of the 1D free Poincaré inequality similar in spirit to two classical refinements.

articleTitle: Homological Mirror Symmetry and Fourier–Mukai Transform
abstract: We interpret symplectic geometry as certain sheaf theory by constructing a sheaf of curved <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_\infty$</tex> algebras which in some sense plays the role of a “structure sheaf” for symplectic manifolds. An interesting feature of this “structure sheaf” is that the symplectic form itself is part of its curvature term. Using this interpretation homological mirror symmetry can be understood by well-known duality theories in mathematics: Koszul duality or Fourier–Mukai transform. In this paper, we perform the above constructions over a small open subset inside the smooth locus of a Lagrangian torus fibration. In a subsequent work, we shall use the language of derived geometry to obtain a global theory over the whole smooth locus. However, we do not know how to extend this construction to the singular locus. As an application of the local theory, we prove a version of homological mirror symmetry between a toric symplectic manifold and its Landau–Ginzburg mirror.

articleTitle: The Relative Breuil–Kisin Classification of p-Divisible Groups and Finite Flat Group Schemes
abstract: Assume that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \gt 2$</tex>, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {O} _K$</tex> be a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic discrete valuation ring with residue field admitting a finite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-basis, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> be a formally smooth formally finite-type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {O} _K$</tex>-algebra. (Indeed, we allow slightly more general rings <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>.) We construct an anti-equivalence of categories between the categories of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-divisible groups over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> and certain semi-linear algebra objects which generalize <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varphi ,\Fraktur {S})$</tex>-modules of height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leqslant 1$</tex> (or Kisin modules). A similar classification result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-power order finite flat group schemes is deduced from the classification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-divisible groups. We also show compatibility of various construction of (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ} _p$</tex>-lattice or torsion) Galois representations, including the relative version of Faltings’ integral comparison theorem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-divisible groups. We obtain partial results when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=2$</tex>.

articleTitle: On Pleijel's Nodal Domain Theorem
abstract: A slight improvement of Pleijel's estimate on the number of nodal domains is obtained, exploiting a refinement of the Faber–Krahn inequality and packing density of disks.

articleTitle: On the c-Vectors of an Acyclic Cluster Algebra
abstract: We prove that the set of c-vectors of the cluster algebra associated to an acyclic quiver Q coincides with the set of real Schur roots and their opposites in the root system associated to Q.

articleTitle: On the Concordance Genus of Topologically Slice Knots
abstract: The concordance genus of a knot K is the minimum Seifert genus of all knots smoothly concordant to K. Concordance genus is bounded below by the 4-ball genus and above by the Seifert genus. We give a lower bound for the concordance genus of K coming from the knot Floer complex of K. As an application, we prove that there are topologically slice knots with 4-ball genus equal to 1 and arbitrarily large concordance genus.

articleTitle: The Generic Nontriviality of the Faber–Pandharipande Cycle
abstract: We present a simple and characteristic-free proof of a result of Green and Griffiths, which states that for the generic curve C of genus g≥4, the Faber–Pandharipande cycle K×K−(2g−2)K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf> is nontorsion in CH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(C×C).

articleTitle: Generating the Ideals Defining Unions of Schubert Varieties
abstract: This note computes a Gröbner basis for the ideal defining a union of Schubert varieties. More precisely, it computes a Gröbner basis for unions of schemes given by northwest rank conditions on the space of all matrices of a fixed size. Schemes given by northwest rank conditions include classical determinantal varieties and matrix Schubert varieties—closures of Schubert varieties lifted from the flag manifold to the space of matrices.

articleTitle: Proper Toric Maps Over Finite Fields
abstract: We determine a strong form of the decomposition theorem for proper toric maps over finite fields.

articleTitle: On Satake Parameters for Representations with Parahoric Fixed Vectors
abstract: This article, a continuation of [13], constructs the Satake parameter for any irreducible smooth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-spherical representation of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic group, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is any parahoric subgroup. This parameterizes such representations when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> is a special maximal parahoric subgroup. The main novelty is for groups which are not quasi-split, and the construction should play a role in formulating a geometric Satake isomorphism for such groups over local function fields.

articleTitle: Computing Upper Cluster Algebras
abstract: This paper develops techniques for producing presentations of upper cluster algebras. These techniques are suited to computer implementation, and will always succeed when the upper cluster algebra is totally coprime and finitely generated. We include several examples of presentations produced by these methods.

articleTitle: A Uniform Model for Kirillov–Reshetikhin Crystals I: Lifting the Parabolic Quantum Bruhat Graph
abstract: We lift the parabolic quantum Bruhat graph (QBG) into the Bruhat order on the affine Weyl group and into Littelmann's poset on level-zero weights. We establish a quantum analog of Deodhar's Bruhat-minimum lift from a parabolic quotient of the Weyl group. This result asserts a remarkable compatibility of the QBG on the Weyl group, with the cosets for every parabolic subgroup. Also, we generalize Postnikov's lemma from the QBG to the parabolic one; this lemma compares paths between two vertices in the former graph. The results in this paper will be applied in a second paper to establish a uniform construction of tensor products of one-column Kirillov–Reshetikhin (KR) crystals, and the equality, for untwisted affine root systems, between the Macdonald polynomial with t set to zero and the graded character of tensor products of one-column KR modules.

articleTitle: Local Brunella's Alternative II. Partial Separatrices
abstract: Here we state a conjecture concerning a local version of Brunella's alternative: any codimension one foliation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\BBC}^3,0)$</tex> without germ of invariant surface has a neighborhood of the origin formed by leaves containing a germ of analytic curve at the origin. We prove the conjecture for the class of codimension one foliations whose reduction of singularities is obtained by blowing-up points and curves of equireduction and such that the final singularities are free of saddle-nodes. The concept of “partial separatrix” for a given reduction of singularities has a central role in our argumentations, as well as the quantitative control of the generic Camacho-Sad index in dimension three. The “nodal components” are the only possible obstructions to get such germs of analytic curves. We use the partial separatrices to push the leaves near a nodal component towards compact dicritical divisors, finding in this way the desired analytic curves.

articleTitle: Root Polytopes and Borel Subalgebras
abstract: Let Φ be a finite crystallographic irreducible root system and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}_{\Phi }$</tex> be the convex hull of the roots in Φ. We give a uniform explicit description of the polytope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}_{\Phi }$</tex>, analyze the algebraic-combinatorial structure of its faces, and provide connections with the Borel subalgebra of the associated Lie algebra. We also give several enumerative results.

articleTitle: Universal Gröbner Bases for Maximal Minors
abstract: Bernstein, Sturmfels, and Zelevinsky proved in 1993 that the maximal minors of a matrix of variables form a universal Gröbner basis. We present a very short proof of this result, along with broad generalization to matrices with multihomogeneous structures. Our main tool is a rigidity statement for radical Borel fixed ideals in multigraded polynomial rings.

articleTitle: Arithmeticity of Four Hypergeometric Monodromy Groups Associated to Calabi–Yau Threefolds
abstract: In [12], we show that three of the fourteen hypergeometric monodromy groups associated to Calabi–Yau threefolds are arithmetic. Brav–Thomas (in [3]) show that seven of the remaining eleven are thin. In this article, we settle the arithmeticity problem for the fourteen monodromy groups, by showing that, the remaining four are arithmetic.

articleTitle: On the Dual Graphs of Cohen–Macaulay Algebras
abstract: Given an equidimensional algebraic set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\subset {\BBP} ^n$</tex>, its dual graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(X)$</tex> is the graph whose vertices are the irreducible components of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and whose edges connect components that intersect in codimension one. Hartshorne's connectedness theorem says that if (the coordinate ring of) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is Cohen–Macaulay, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(X)$</tex> is connected. We present two quantitative variants of Hartshorne's result: (1) If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is a Gorenstein subspace arrangement, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(X)$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>-connected, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> is the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. (The bound is best possible. For coordinate arrangements, it yields an algebraic extension of Balinski's theorem for simplicial polytopes.) (2) If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is an arrangement of lines no three of which meet in the same point, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is canonically embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP} ^n$</tex>, then the diameter of the graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(X)$</tex> is less than or equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {codim} _{{\BBP} ^n}X$</tex>. (The bound is sharp; for coordinate arrangements, it yields an algebraic expansion on the recent combinatorial result that the Hirsch conjecture holds for flag normal simplicial complexes.) On the way to these results, we show that there exists a graph which is not the dual graph of any simplicial complex (no matter the dimension).

articleTitle: Norm Continuous Unitary Representations of Lie Algebras of Smooth Sections
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur K}}\to X$</tex> be a smooth Lie algebra bundle over a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex>-compact manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> whose typical fiber is the compact Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur k}}$</tex>. We give a complete description of the irreducible bounded (i.e., norm continuous) unitary representations of the Fréchet–Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ({{\Fraktur K}})$</tex> of all smooth sections of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur K}}$</tex>, and of the LF-Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _c({{\Fraktur K}})$</tex> of compactly supported smooth sections. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ({{\Fraktur K}})$</tex>, irreducible bounded unitary representations are finite tensor products of so-called evaluation representations, hence in particular finite dimensional. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _{c}({{\Fraktur K}})$</tex>, bounded unitary irreducible (factor) representations are possibly infinite tensor products of evaluation representations, which reduces the classification problem to results of Glimm and Powers on irreducible (factor) representations of UHF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^* $</tex>-algebras. The key part in our proof is the result that every irreducible bounded unitary representation of a Lie algebra of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\Fraktur k}}\otimes _{{\BBR}} {\cal {A}}_{{\BBR}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {A}}_{{\BBR}}$</tex> is a unital real complete continuous inverse algebra, is a finite product of evaluation representations. On the group level, our results cover in particular the bounded unitary representations of the identity component <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\rm Gau}}}(P)_0$</tex> of the group of smooth gauge transformations of a principal fiber bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P \to X$</tex> with compact base and structure group, and the groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\rm SU}}}_n({\cal {A}})_0$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {A}}$</tex> a complete involutive commutative continuous inverse algebra.

articleTitle: Sharp Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev Inequality on the Upper Half Space
abstract: The sharp Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev inequality on the upper half space is proved. The existences of extremal functions are obtained. For certain exponent, we classify all extremal functions via the method of moving sphere, and compute the best constants for the sharp inequality.

articleTitle: Singular-Value Decomposition of Solution Operators to Model Evolution Equations
abstract: We consider evolution equations generated by quadratic operators admitting a decomposition in creation–annihilation operators without usual ellipticity-type hypotheses; this class includes hypocoercive model operators. We identify the singular-value decomposition of their solution operators with the evolution generated by an operator of harmonic oscillator type, and in doing so derive exact characterizations of return to equilibrium and regularization for any complex time.

articleTitle: Correlations and Pairing between Zeros and Critical Points of Gaussian Random Polynomials
abstract: Let p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> be a degree N random polynomial in a complex variable. We obtain an explicit asymptotic formula for the covariance between the counting measures of its zeros and critical points, which we denote Cov<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(z,w). This formula shows that the correlation between a zero at z and a critical point at w is short range, decaying like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{-N|z-w|^2}$</tex> With <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|z-w|$</tex> on the order of N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>, however, Cov<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(z,w) is sharply peaked near z=w, causing zeros and critical points to appear in pairs. We prove bounds on the expected distance and angular dependence between a critical point and its paired zero.

articleTitle: Associated Varieties of Modules Over Kac–Moody Algebras and C2-Cofiniteness of W-Algebras
abstract: First, we establish the relation between the associated varieties of modules over Kac–Moody algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\hat {\Fraktur {g}}}$</tex> and those over affine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>-algebras. Secondly, we prove the Feigin–Frenkel conjecture on the singular supports of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-integrable admissible representations. In fact, we show that the associated varieties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>-integrable admissible representations are irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {Ad}}}G$</tex>-invariant subvarieties of the nullcone of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur {g}}$</tex>, by determining them explicitly. Thirdly, we prove the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_2$</tex>-cofiniteness of a large number of simple <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>-algebras, including all the minimal series principal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>-algebras [22] and the exceptional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>-algebras recently discovered by Kac–Wakimoto [31].

articleTitle: Automorphisms of the Quot Schemes Associated to Compact Riemann Surfaces
abstract: Let X be a compact connected Riemann surface of genus at least 2. Fix positive integers r and d. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}$</tex> denote the Quot scheme that parameterizes all the torsion quotients of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}^{\oplus r}_X$</tex> of degree d. This <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}$</tex> is also the moduli space of vortices for the standard action of U(r) on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^r$</tex>. The group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {PGL}(r, {\BBC})$</tex> acts faithfully on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}$</tex> via the standard action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {GL}(r, {\BBC})$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal O}^{\oplus r}_X$</tex>. We prove that this subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {PGL}(r, {\BBC})$</tex> is the connected component, containing the identity element, of the holomorphic automorphism group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {Aut}(\cal {Q})$</tex>. As an application, we prove that the isomorphism class of the complex manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Q}$</tex> uniquely determines the isomorphism class of the Riemann surface X.

articleTitle: Fluctuations in the Zero Set of the Hyperbolic Gaussian Analytic Function
abstract: The zero set of the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function is a random point process in the unit disk whose distribution is invariant under automorphisms of the disk. We study the variance of the number of points in a disk of increasing radius. Somewhat surprisingly, we find a change of behavior at a certain value of the “intensity” of the process, which appears to be novel.

articleTitle: Energy Integrals Over Local Fields and Global Height Bounds
abstract: We solve an energy minimization problem for local fields. As an application of these results, we improve on lower bounds set by Bombieri and Zannier for the limit infimum of the Weil height in fields of totally p-adic numbers and generalizations thereof. In the case of fields with mixed archimedean and nonarchimedean splitting conditions, we are able to combine our bounds with similar bounds at the archimedean places for totally real fields.

articleTitle: The Arc Complex and Contact Geometry: Nondestabilizable Planar Open Book Decompositions of the Tight Contact 3-Sphere
abstract: In this note, we introduce the (homologically essential) arc complex of a surface as a tool for studying properties of open book decompositions and contact structures. After characterizing destabilizability in terms of the essential translation distance of the monodromy of an open book, we given an application of this result to show that there are planar open books of the standard contact structure on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with five (or any number larger than five) boundary components that do not destabilize. We also show that any planar open book with four or fewer boundary components does destabilize.

articleTitle: The Weak Haagerup Property II: Examples
abstract: The weak Haagerup property for locally compact groups and the weak Haagerup constant were recently introduced by the second author [27]. The weak Haagerup property is weaker than both weak amenability introduced by Cowling and the first author [9] and the Haagerup property introduced by Connes [6] and Choda [5]. In this paper, it is shown that a connected simple Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> has the weak Haagerup property if and only if the real rank of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is zero or one. Hence for connected simple Lie groups the weak Haagerup property coincides with weak amenability. Moreover, it turns out that for connected simple Lie groups the weak Haagerup constant coincides with the weak amenability constant, although this is not true for locally compact groups in general. It is also shown that the semidirect product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^2 \rtimes {\rm SL}(2,{\BBR})$</tex> does not have the weak Haagerup property.

articleTitle: Density of Rational Points on a Certain Smooth Bihomogeneous Threefold
abstract: We establish sharp upper and lower bounds for the number of rational points of bounded anticanonical height on a smooth bihomogeneous threefold defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> and of bidegree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,2)$</tex>. These bounds are in agreement with Manin's conjecture.

articleTitle: Coupled GUE-Minor Processes and Domino Tilings
abstract: This paper deals with two Gaussian unitary ensemble (GUE)-matrices, coupled together through some inequalities between the spectra of the first few (small) principal minors. The main results of the paper is to show that the spectra of the principal minors of these coupled matrices behave statistically as the domino tilings of finitely overlapping Aztec diamonds when their sizes become very large, with horizontal and vertical dominos being equally likely. This extends naturally a result of Johansson and Nordenstam [20], stating that the spectra of the principal minors of a GUE-matrix behave statistically as domino tilings of an Aztec diamond, near the middle of its edge. Given the spectra of the two coupled matrices, the joint spectra of the underlying principal minors of the two GUE-matrices are uniformly distributed in a certain “double cone”. In particular, this leads to two GUE-matrices, whose spectra share the same real line, with one spectrum being completely to the left of the other spectrum; this gives a new and simple extension of GUE. Also note that all statements concerning these coupled random matrices have a domino tiling counterpart.

articleTitle: Algebraic Dynamical Systems and Dirichlet's Unit Theorem on Arithmetic Varieties
abstract: The effectivity of pseudo-effective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>-divisor is an important and difficult problem in algebraic geometry. In the Arakelov geometry framework, this problem can be considered as a generalization of Dirichlet's unit theorem for number fields. In this article, we propose obstructions to the Dirichlet property by two approaches, that is, the denseness of nonpositive points and functionals on adelic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>-divisors. Applied to the algebraic dynamical systems, these results provide examples of nef adelic arithmetic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}$</tex>-Cartier divisor which does not have the Dirichlet property. We hope the obstructions obtained in the article will give ways toward criteria of the Dirichlet property.

articleTitle: Strichartz Inequalities on Surfaces with Cusps
abstract: We prove Strichartz inequalities for the wave and Schrödinger equations on noncompact surfaces with ends of finite area, that is, with ends isometric to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$((r_0,\infty ) \times {\BBS}^1$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${d}r^2 + {\rm {e}}^{- 2 \phi (r)}\,{d} \theta ^2)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {e}}^{-\phi }$</tex> integrable. We prove first that all Strichartz estimates, with any derivative loss, fail to be true in such ends. We next show, for the wave equation, that by projecting off the zero mode of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBS}^1 $</tex>, we recover the same inequalities as on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\BBR}^2 $</tex>. On the other hand, for the Schrödinger equation, we prove that even by projecting off the zero angular modes, we have to consider additional losses of derivatives compared to the case of closed surfaces; in particular, we show that the semiclassical estimates of Burq–Gérard–Tzvetkov do not hold in such geometries. Moreover, our semiclassical estimates with loss are sharp.

articleTitle: Radial Density in Apollonian Packings
abstract: Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}$</tex>, an Apollonian Circle Packing, and a circle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_0 = \partial B(z_0, r_0)$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}$</tex>, color the set of disks in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal P}$</tex> tangent to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_0$</tex> red. What proportion of the concentric circle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\epsilon } = \partial B(z_0, r_0 + \epsilon )$</tex> is red, and what is the behavior of this quantity as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon \rightarrow 0$</tex>? Using equidistribution of closed horocycles on the modular surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ \BBH}^2/{\rm SL}(2, { \BBZ})$</tex>, we show that the answer is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${3 \over \pi } = 0.9549\ldots .$</tex> We also describe an observation due to Alex Kontorovich connecting the rate of this convergence in the Farey–Ford packing to the Riemann hypothesis. For the analogous problem for Soddy sphere packings, we find that the limiting radial density is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\sqrt {3} \over 2V_{\rm T}}=0.853\ldots$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\rm T}$</tex> denotes the volume of an ideal hyperbolic tetrahedron with dihedral angles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi /3$</tex>.

articleTitle: Representation Type of Finite Quiver Hecke Algebras of Type A(1)ℓ for Arbitrary Parameters
abstract: We give Erdmann–Nakano type theorem for the finite quiver Hecke algebras R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Λ</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(β) of affine type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^{(1)}_{\ell }$</tex>. Note that each finite quiver Hecke algebra lies in one-parameter family, and the original Erdmann–Nakano theorem studied the finite quiver Hecke algebra at a special parameter value. We study the general case in our paper. Our result shows, in particular, that their representation type does not depend on the parameter. Moreover, when the parameter value is nonzero, we show that finite quiver Hecke algebras of tame representation type are biserial algebras.

articleTitle: Julia and Escaping Set Spiders’ Webs of Positive Area
abstract: We study the dynamics of a collection of families of transcendental entire functions which generalizes the well-known exponential and cosine families. We show that, for functions in many of these families, the Julia set, the escaping set, and the fast escaping set are all spiders’ webs of positive area. This result is unusual in that most of these functions lie outside the Eremenko–Lyubich class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {B}$</tex>. This is also the first result on the area of a spider's web.

articleTitle: The Density of Primes in Orbits of zd+c
abstract: Given a polynomial f(z)=z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>+c∈K[z] over a global field K and a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>∈K, we study the density of prime ideals of K dividing at least one element of the orbit of a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> under f. We show that for many choices of d and c this density is zero for all a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, assuming K contains a primitive dth root of unity. The proof relies on several new results, including some giving criteria to ensure the number of irreducible factors of the nth iterate of f remains bounded as n grows, and others on the ramification above certain primes in iterated extensions. Together these allow for nearly complete information when K is a global function field or when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K={{\BBQ}}(\zeta _d)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Isomonodromy Aspects of the tt* Equations of Cecotti and Vafa I. Stokes Data
abstract: We describe all smooth solutions of the two-function tt*-Toda equations (a version of the tt* equations or equations for harmonic maps into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {SL}}_n{\BBR}/{\rm {SO}}_n$</tex>) in terms of (1) asymptotic data, (2) holomorphic data, and (3) monodromy data, and we compute all of this data explicitly. This allows us, in particular, to find all solutions with integral Stokes data. These include solutions associated to non-linear sigma models (quantum cohomology) or Landau–Ginzburg models (unfoldings of singularities), as conjectured by Cecotti and Vafa in the 1990s.

articleTitle: On the Tube Occupancy of Sets in ℝd
abstract: Call a pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(s,t) \in [0,d] \times [0,d]$</tex> admissible, if there exists a compact set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K \subset {{\BBR}}^{d}$</tex> and a constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C \gt 0$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt {\cal {H}}^{s}(K) \lt \infty$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${\cal {H}}_{s}(K \cap T) \leq Cw(T)^{t}$$</tex> for all tubes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T \subset {{\BBR}}^{d}$</tex> of width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w(T)$</tex>. The purpose of this paper is to show that all pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(s,s)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \lt d - 1$</tex> are admissible. Combined with previous results, this settles a question of A. Carbery.

articleTitle: Local Energy Decay for Maxwell Fields Part I: Spherically Symmetric Black-Hole Backgrounds
abstract: We prove integrated local energy decay for solutions to the inhomogeneous Maxwell system on a general class of spherical black hole backgrounds.

articleTitle: On the Range of the Attenuated Ray Transform for Unitary Connections
abstract: We describe the range of the attenuated ray transform of a unitary connection on a simple surface acting on functions and 1-forms. We use this description to determine the range of the ray transform acting on symmetric tensor fields.

articleTitle: On the Extended W-Algebra of Type sl2 at Positive Rational Level
abstract: The extended W-algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_2$</tex> at positive rational level, denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{p_+,p_-}$</tex>, is a vertex operator algebra (VOA) that was originally proposed in [16]. This VOA is an extension of the minimal model VOA and plays the role of symmetry algebra for certain logarithmic conformal field theories. We give a construction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{p_+,p_-}$</tex> in terms of screening operators and use this construction to prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{p_+,p_-}$</tex> satisfies Zhu's c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-cofiniteness condition, calculate the structure of the zero mode algebra (also known as Zhu's algebra), and classify all simple <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}_{p_+,p_-}$</tex>-modules.

articleTitle: Twisted Geometric Langlands Correspondence for a Torus
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> be a split torus over local or global function field. The theory of Brylinski–Deligne gives rise to the metaplectic central extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> by a finite cyclic group. The representation theory of these metaplectic tori has been developed to some extent in the works of M. Weissman, G. Savin, W. T. Gan, P. McNamara, and others. In this paper we propose a geometrization of this theory in the framework of the geometric Langlands program (in the everywhere nonramified case).

articleTitle: Module Varieties and Representation Type of Finite-Dimensional Algebras
abstract: In this paper, we seek geometric and invariant-theoretic characterizations of (Schur)-representation-finite algebras. To this end, we introduce two classes of finite-dimensional algebras: those with the dense-orbit property and those with the multiplicity-free property. We first show that when a connected algebra admits a preprojective component, each of these properties is equivalent to it being representation-finite. Next, we give an example of an algebra which is not representation-finite but still has the dense-orbit property. We also show that the string algebras with the dense orbit-property are precisely the representation-finite ones. Finally, we show that a tame algebra has the multiplicity-free property if and only if it is Schur-representation-finite.

articleTitle: New Estimates of the Nonlinear Fourier Transform for the Defocusing NLS Equation
abstract: The defocusing NLS equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {i} u_t = -u_{xx} +2|u|^2u$</tex> on the circle admits a global nonlinear Fourier transform, also known as Birkhoff map, linearizing the NLS flow. The regularity properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> are known to be closely related to the decay properties of the corresponding nonlinear Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we quantify this relationship by providing two-sided polynomial estimates of all integer Sobolev norms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\|u\|_m$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m\geqslant 0$</tex>, in terms of the weighted norms of the nonlinear Fourier transformed.

articleTitle: Boundedness for Weyl–Pedersen Calculus on Flat Coadjoint Orbits
abstract: We describe boundedness and compactness properties for the operators obtained by the Weyl–Pedersen calculus in the case of the irreducible unitary representations of nilpotent Lie groups that are associated with flat coadjoint orbits. We use spaces of smooth symbols satisfying appropriate growth conditions expressed in terms of invariant differential operators on the coadjoint orbit under consideration. Our method also provides conditions for these operators to belong to one of the Schatten ideals of compact operators. In the special case of the Schrödinger representation of the Heisenberg group, we recover some classical properties of the pseudo-differential Weyl calculus, as the Calderón–Vaillancourt theorem, and the Beals characterization in terms of commutators.

articleTitle: Holomorphic Double Fibration and the Mapping Problems of Classical Domains
abstract: We construct holomorphic double fibrations to link up certain pairs of classical domains on Grassmannians. By analyzing the geometric properties of these double fibrations including the projections of the associated fibers and their intersections, we obtain rigidity results for holomorphic mappings between certain pairs of Type-I irreducible bounded symmetric domains Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> r,s</inf> that are well adapted to the double fibrations. As one application of our results, we prove that, for s≥r≥2 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${r}'{\leq \rm min}(2r-\rm l,s)$</tex>, every proper holomorphic map from Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> r,s</inf> to Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> r′,s</inf> is equivalent to a linear embedding.

articleTitle: Infinitely Many Knots Admitting the Same Integer Surgery and a Four-Dimensional Extension
abstract: We prove that for any integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> there exist infinitely many different knots in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^3$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-surgery on those knots yields the same <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifold. In particular, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|n|=1$</tex> homology spheres arise from these surgeries. This answers Problem 3.6(D) on the Kirby problem list. We construct two families of examples, the first by a method of twisting along an annulus and the second by a generalization of this procedure. The latter family also solves a stronger version of Problem 3.6(D), that for any integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, there exist infinitely many mutually distinct knots such that 2-handle addition along each with framing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> yields the same <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex>-manifold.

articleTitle: Generalized Virtual Braid Groups, Quasi-Shuffle Product and Quantum Groups
abstract: We introduce in this notice the generalized virtual braid group on n strands GVB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, generalizing simultaneously the braid groups and their virtual versions. A Matsumoto–Tits-type section lifting shuffles in a symmetric group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {S}_n$</tex> to the monoid associated to GVB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is constructed, which is then applied to characterize the quantum quasi-shuffle product. A family of representations of GVB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is constructed using quantum groups.

articleTitle: On the Fundamental Group of a Variety with Quotient Singularities
abstract: Let k be a field, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi:\tilde X\rightarrow X$</tex> be a proper birational morphism of irreducible k-varieties, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde X$</tex> is smooth and X has at worst quotient singularities. When the characteristic of k is zero, a theorem of Kollár [7] says that π induces an isomorphism of étale fundamental groups. We give a proof of this result which works for all characteristics. As an application, we prove that for a smooth projective irreducible surface X over an algebraically closed field k, the étale fundamental group of the Hilbert scheme of n points of X, where n>1, is canonically isomorphic to the abelianization of the étale fundamental group of X. Kollár has pointed out how the proof of the first result can be extended to cover the case of quotients by finite group schemes.

articleTitle: Bianchi Hypercubes and a Geometric Unification of the Hirota and Miwa Equations
abstract: We present a geometric and algebraic way of unifying two discrete master equations of soliton theory, namely the dKP (Hirota) and dBKP (Miwa) equations. We demonstrate that so-called Cox lattices encapsulate Bianchi (hyper)cubes associated with either simultaneous solutions of a novel 14-point and the dBKP equations or solutions of the dKP equation, depending on whether the Cox lattices are nondegenerate or degenerate.

articleTitle: A Characterization of Toric Varieties in Characteristic p
abstract: If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is a smooth toric variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is an invertible sheaf on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, it has been shown by Thomsen that the push-forward of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> along the Frobenius morphism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> splits into a direct sum of invertible sheaves. We show that this property characterizes smooth projective toric varieties.

articleTitle: Groups of Lie Type, Vertex Algebras, and Modular Moonshine
abstract: It is known that an ADE-type lattice vertex operator algebra has an integral form containing a Chevalley basis of its degree 1 Lie algebra. One can then define a vertex algebra (VA) over any commutative ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>. We also define VAs of types BCFG over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>. For these VAs, we construct Chevalley or Steinberg groups acting as VA automorphisms. These groups are essentially the full automorphism groups when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> is a field. We define reduced VAs. In characteristics 2 and 3, there are exceptionally large automorphism groups. A covering idea of Frohardt–Griess for Lie algebras is adapted. Related covering procedures complete Borcherds–Ryba modular moonshine program for proving an embedding of the Thompson sporadic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_3$</tex> of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{15}3^{10}5^3 7^2 13\cdot 19\cdot 31$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_8(3)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Dimension Conservation for Self-Similar Sets and Fractal Percolation
abstract: We introduce a technique that uses projection properties of fractal percolation to establish dimension conservation results for sections of deterministic self-similar sets. For example, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a self-similar subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^2$</tex> with Hausdorff dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim _H K \gt 1$</tex> such that the rotational components of the underlying similarities generate the full rotation group. Then, for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon \gt 0$</tex>, writing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _\theta $</tex> for projection onto the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\theta $</tex> in direction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta $</tex>, the Hausdorff dimensions of the sections satisfy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim _H (K\cap \pi _\theta ^{-1}x) \gt \dim _H K - 1 - \epsilon $</tex> for a set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in L_\theta $</tex> of positive Lebesgue measure for all directions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta $</tex> except for those in a set of Hausdorff dimension 0. For a class of self-similar sets, we obtain a similar conclusion for all directions, but with lower box dimension replacing Hausdorff dimensions of sections. We obtain similar inequalities for the dimensions of sections of Mandelbrot percolation sets.

articleTitle: On Subfields of the Function Field of a General Surface in ℙ3
abstract: In this paper, we study birational immersions from a very general smooth plane curve to a nonrational surface with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_g=q=0$</tex> to treat dominant rational maps from a very general surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 5$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^3$</tex> to smooth projective surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>. Based on the classification theory of algebraic surfaces, Hodge theory, and deformation theory, we prove that there is no dominant rational map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> unless <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is rational or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is birational to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: Large-N Asymptotic Expansion for Mean Field Models with Coulomb Gas Interaction
abstract: We derive the large-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>, all order asymptotic expansion for a system of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> particles with mean field interactions on top of a Coulomb repulsion at temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/\beta$</tex>, under the assumptions that the interactions are analytic, off-critical, and satisfy a local strict convexity assumption.

articleTitle: On Lifting and Modularity of Reducible Residual Galois Representations Over Imaginary Quadratic Fields
abstract: In this paper, we study deformations of mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> Galois representations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex> (over an imaginary quadratic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>) of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> whose semi-simplification is the direct sum of two characters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau _1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau _2$</tex>. As opposed to [7], we do not impose any restrictions on the dimension of the crystalline Selmer group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1_{\Sigma }(F, {\rm Hom}(\tau _2, \tau _1)) \subset {\rm Ext}^1(\tau _2, \tau _1)$</tex>. We establish that there exists a basis <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {B}}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^1_{\Sigma }(F, {\rm Hom}(\tau _2, \tau _1))$</tex> arising from automorphic representations over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> (Theorem 8.1). Assuming among other things that the elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {B}}$</tex> admit only finitely many crystalline characteristic 0 deformations, we prove a modularity lifting theorem asserting that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex> itself is modular then so is its every crystalline characteristic zero deformation (Theorems 8.2 and 8.5).

articleTitle: Derived-Equivalent Rational Threefolds
abstract: We describe an infinite set of smooth projective threefolds that have equivalent derived categories but are not isomorphic, contrary to a conjecture of Kawamata. These arise as blow-ups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^3$</tex> at various configurations of 8 points, which are related by Cremona transformations.

articleTitle: Clifford–Klein Forms and a-Hyperbolic Rank
abstract: The purpose of this article is to introduce and investigate properties of a tool (the a-hyperbolic rank) which enables us to obtain new examples of homogeneous spaces G/H which admit and do not admit a discontinuous action of a non virtually abelian discrete subgroup. We achieve this goal by exploring in greater detail the technique of adjoint orbits developed by Okuda combined with the well-known conditions of Benoist. We find easy-to-check conditions on G and H expressed directly in terms of the Satake diagrams of the corresponding Lie algebras, in cases when G is a real form of a complex Lie group of type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2k+1</inf>, or E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. One of the advantages of this approach is the fact, that we do not need to know the embedding of H into G. Using the a-hyperbolic rank we also show that the homogeneous space E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IV</sup>/H of reductive type admits a discontinuous action of a non virtually abelian discrete subgroup if and only if H is compact. Also, inspired by the work of Okuda on symmetric spaces G/H we find a list of simply connected 3-symmetric spaces admitting a discontinuous action of a non virtually abelian discrete subgroup. This list yields almost complete classification of such spaces (there is one exception).

articleTitle: Sign of Green's Function of Paneitz Operators and the Q Curvature
abstract: In a conformal class of metrics with positive Yamabe invariant, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of metrics with positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> curvature. The condition is conformally invariant. We also prove some inequalities between the Green's functions of the conformal Laplacian operator and the Paneitz operator.

articleTitle: All Admissible Meromorphic Solutions of Hayman's Equation
abstract: We find all nonrational meromorphic solutions of the equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ww''-(w')^2=\alpha (z)w+ \beta (z)w'+ \gamma (z)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta ,$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> are rational functions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>. In so doing, we answer a question of Hayman by showing that all such solutions have finite order. Apart from special choices of the coefficient functions, the general solution is not meromorphic and contains movable branch points. For some choices for the coefficient functions, the equation admits a one-parameter family of nonrational meromorphic solutions. Nevanlinna theory is used to show that all such solutions have been found and allows us to avoid issues that can arise from the fact that resonances can occur at arbitrarily high orders. We actually solve the more general problem of finding all meromorphic solutions that are admissible in the sense of Nevanlinna theory, where the coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta ,$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> are meromorphic functions.

articleTitle: On Transcendence of the Uniformizing Map
abstract: The main purpose of the note is provide some new examples of a conjecture of Lang about the transcendence of the derivative of a normalized uniformization map for a hyperbolic Riemann surface. The examples are obtained by analyzing the geometry behind an analogous problem in higher dimensions.

articleTitle: On the Nonexistence of Pure Multi-solitons for the Quartic gKdV Equation
abstract: We consider the quartic (nonintegrable) (gKdV) equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\partial_tu+\partial_x(\partial^2_xu+u^4)=0,\quad t,x\in\mathbb R$$</tex> and u(t) an outgoing 2-soliton of the equation, that is, a solution satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\parallel u(t)-Q_{c_1}(.-c_1t)-Q_{c_2}(.-c_2t)\parallel_{H^1}=0,$$</tex> where 0<c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf><c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and where Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cj</inf>(x−c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>t) are explicit solitons of the equation. In [17], in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0<1-\frac {c_2}{c_1}=\in\leq\in_0$</tex>, where ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is a small enough, not explicit constant, the solution u(t,x) is computed up to some order of ϵ, for all t and x. In particular, it is deduced that u(t) is not a multi-soliton as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\rightarrow-\infty$</tex>, proving the nonexistence of pure multi-soliton in this context. In the present paper, we prove the same result for an explicit range of speeds: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {3}{4}c_1< c_2< c_1$</tex>, by a different approach, which does not longer require a precise description of the solution. In fact, the nonexistence result holds for outgoing N-solitons, for any N≥2, under the assumption: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma^N_{j=2}(1-c_j/c_1)^2\leq \frac {1}{16}$</tex>, which is a natural generalization of the condition for N=2.

articleTitle: Global Calderón–Zygmund Theory for Asymptotically Regular Nonlinear Elliptic and Parabolic Equations
