abstract: We consider nonhomogeneous elliptic and parabolic problems involving a discontinuous nonlinearity and an asymptotic regularity over an irregular domain in divergence form of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-Laplacian type, to establish the global Calderón–Zygmund estimate by converting a given asymptotically regular problem to a suitable regular problem.

articleTitle: The Riemann Zeta Function on Vertical Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: We show that the twisted second moments of the Riemann zeta function averaged over the arithmetic progression <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over 2} + {\rm i}(an+b)$</tex> with a>0, b real, exhibits a remarkable correspondence with the analogous continuous average and derive several consequences. For example, motivated by the linear independence conjecture, we show at least one third of the elements in the arithmetic progression an+b are not the ordinates of some zero of ζ(s) lying on the critical line. This improves on an earlier work of Martin and Ng. We then complement this result by producing large values of ζ(s) on arithmetic progressions which are of the same quality as the best Ω results currently known for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta({1 \over 2}+{\rm i}t)$</tex> with t real.

articleTitle: An Algorithm to Compute Automorphism Groups of K3 Surfaces and an Application to Singular K3 Surfaces
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be a complex algebraic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surface or a supersingular <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surface in odd characteristic. We present an algorithm by which, under certain assumptions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, we can calculate a finite set of generators of the image of the natural homomorphism from the automorphism group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> to the orthogonal group of the Néron–Severi lattice of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We then apply this algorithm to certain complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces, among which are singular <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surfaces whose transcendental lattices are of small discriminants.

articleTitle: On a Fractional Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence of Solutions
abstract: This paper is a continuation of our earlier work “[Jin, T., Y. Y. Li and J. Xiong. “On a fractional Nirenberg problem, part I: blow up analysis and compactness of solutions.” J. Eur. Math. Soc., to appear]”, where compactness results were given on a fractional Nirenberg problem. We prove two existence results stated there. We also obtain a fractional Aubin inequality.

articleTitle: Exterior Mass Estimates and L2-Restriction Bounds for Neumann Data Along Hypersurfaces
abstract: We study the problem of estimating the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-norm of Laplace eigenfunctions on a compact Riemannian manifold M when restricted to a hypersurface H. We prove mass estimates for the restrictions of eigenfunctions ϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>, (h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Δ−1)ϕ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>=0, to H in the region exterior to the coball bundle of H, on h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ</sup>-scales (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\leq \delta \lt {2 \over 3}$</tex>). We use this estimate to obtain an O(1) L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-restriction bound for the Neumann data along H. The estimate also applies to eigenfunctions of semiclassical Schrödinger operators.

articleTitle: The Distribution of Directions in an Affine Lattice: Two-Point Correlations and Mixed Moments
abstract: We consider an affine Euclidean lattice and record the directions of all lattice vectors of length at most T. Strömbergsson and the second author proved in [Ann. Math. 173 (2010), 1949–2033] that the distribution of gaps between the lattice directions has a limit as T tends to infinity. For a typical affine lattice, the limiting gap distribution is universal and has a heavy tail; it differs markedly from the gap distribution observed in a Poisson process, which is exponential. The present study shows that the limiting two-point correlation function of the projected lattice points exists and is Poissonian. This answers a recent question by Boca, Popa, and Zaharescu [arXiv:1302.5067]. The existence of the limit is subject to a certain Diophantine condition. We also establish the convergence of more general mixed moments.

articleTitle: Some Type I Solutions of Ricci Flow with Rotational Symmetry
abstract: We prove that the Ricci flow on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}{\BBP}^n$</tex> blown-up at one point starting with any rotationally symmetric Kähler metric must develop Type I singularities. In particular, if the total volume does not go to zero at the singular time, the parabolic blow-up limit of the Type I Ricci flow along the exceptional divisor is a complete nonflat shrinking gradient Kähler-Ricci soliton on a complete Kähler manifold homeomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^n$</tex> blown-up at one point.

articleTitle: Dunkl Operators at Infinity and Calogero–Moser Systems
abstract: We define the Dunkl and Dunkl–Heckman operators in infinite number of variables and use them to construct the quantum integrals of the Calogero–Moser–Sutherland (CMS) problems at infinity. As a corollary, we have a simple proof of integrability of the deformed quantum CMS systems related to classical Lie superalgebras. We show how this naturally leads to a quantum version of the Moser matrix, which in the deformed case was not known before.

articleTitle: Random Walk Questions for Linear Quantum Groups
abstract: We study the discrete quantum groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> whose group algebra has an inner faithful representation of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi :C^*(\Gamma )\to M_K({\BBC})$</tex>. Such a representation can be thought of as coming from an embedding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \subset U_K$</tex>. Our main result, concerning a certain class of examples of such quantum groups, is an asymptotic convergence theorem for the random walk on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. The proof uses various algebraic and probabilistic techniques.

articleTitle: Monadicity Theorem and Weighted Projective Lines of Tubular Type
abstract: We formulate a version of Beck's monadicity theorem for abelian categories, which is applied to the equivariantization of an abelian category with respect to a finite group action. We prove that the equivariantization is compatible with the construction of quotient abelian categories by Serre subcategories. We prove that the equivariantization of the graded module category over a graded ring is equivalent to the graded module category over the same ring but with a different grading. We deduce from these results two equivalences between the category of (equivariant) coherent sheaves on a weighted projective line of tubular type and that on an elliptic curve, where the acting groups are cyclic and the two equivalences are adjoint to each other.

articleTitle: An Open Adelic Image Theorem for Abelian Schemes
abstract: In this note, we prove an adelic open image theorem for abelian schemes and, more generally, families of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>-motives. This result, which can be interpreted as an adelic specialization theorem, shows for instance the abundancy of Galois-generic closed points on most connected Shimura varieties.

articleTitle: On Involutivity of p-Support
abstract: The p-support of a holonomic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal D}$</tex>-module was introduced by Kontsevich. Thomas Bitoun in his PhD thesis proved several properties of p-support conjectured by Kontsevich. In this note, we give an alternative proof for involutivity by reducing it to a slight extension of Gabber's theorem on the integrability of the characteristic variety. For the benefit of the reader, we review how this extension follows from Kaledin's proof of Gabber's theorem.

articleTitle: Darboux Transformations and Random Point Processes
abstract: In this paper, we describe a general method to derive formulas relating the gap probabilities of some classical determinantal random point processes (Airy, Pearcey, and Hermite) with the gap probability of the same processes with “wanderers”, “inliers”, and “outliers”. In this way, we generalize the Painlevé-like formula found by Baik for the Baik–Ben Arous–Péché distribution to many different cases, both in the one and multi-time setting. The method is not ad hoc and relies upon the notion of Schlesinger transformations for Riemann–Hilbert problems.

articleTitle: Deformations of Log-Lagrangian Submanifolds of Poisson Manifolds
abstract: We consider Lagrangian-like submanifolds in certain even-dimensional “symplectic-like” Poisson manifolds. We show, under a suitable transversality hypothesis, that the pair consisting of the ambient Poisson manifold and the submanifold has unobstructed deformations, and that the deformations automatically preserve the Lagrangian-like property.

articleTitle: The Polynomial Sieve and Equal Sums of Like Polynomials
abstract: A new “polynomial sieve” is presented and used to show that almost all integers have at most one representation as a sum of two values of a given polynomial of degree at least 3.

articleTitle: The Haagerup Property for Arbitrary von Neumann Algebras
abstract: We introduce a natural generalization of the Haagerup property of a finite von Neumann algebra to an arbitrary von Neumann algebra (with a separable predual) equipped with a normal, semi-finite, faithful weight and prove that this property does not depend on the choice of the weight. In particular, this defines the Haagerup property as an intrinsic invariant of the von Neumann algebra. We also show that such a generalized Haagerup property is preserved under taking crossed products by actions of amenable locally compact groups. Our results are motivated by recent examples from the theory of discrete quantum groups, where the Haagerup property appears a priori only with respect to the Haar state.

articleTitle: Mod-φ Convergence
abstract: Using Fourier analysis, we study local limit theorems in weak-convergence problems. Among many applications, we discuss random matrix theory, some probabilistic models in number theory, the winding number of complex Brownian motion and the classical situation of the central limit theorem, and a conjecture concerning the distribution of values of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line.

articleTitle: Holomorphic Lagrangian Fibrations on Hypercomplex Manifolds
abstract: A hypercomplex manifold is a manifold equipped with a triple of complex structures satisfying the quaternionic relations. A holomorphic Lagrangian variety on a hypercomplex manifold with trivial canonical bundle is a holomorphic subvariety which is calibrated by a form associated with the holomorphic volume form; this notion is a generalization of the usual holomorphic Lagrangian subvarieties known in hyperKähler geometry. An HKT (hyperKähler with torsion) metric on a hypercomplex manifold is a metric determined by a local potential, in a similar way to the Kähler metric. We prove that a base of a holomorphic Lagrangian fibration is always Kähler, if its total space is HKT. This is used to construct new examples of hypercomplex manifolds which do not admit an HKT structure.

articleTitle: On the Mean-Width of Isotropic Convex Bodies and their Associated Lp-Centroid Bodies
abstract: For any origin–symmetric convex body K in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex> in isotropic position, we obtain the bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^*(K) \leq C \sqrt {n} \log (n)^2 L_K$</tex>, where M*(K) denotes (half) the mean-width of K, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> is the isotropic constant of K, and C>0 is a universal constant. This improves the previous best-known estimate M*(K)≤Cn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/4</sup>L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>. Up to the power of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log (n)$</tex> term and the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> one, the improved bound is best possible, and implies that the isotropic position is (up to the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> term) an almost 2-regular M-position. The bound extends to any arbitrary position, depending on a certain weighted average of the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. Furthermore, the bound applies to the mean-width of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p </inf>-centroid bodies, extending a sharp upper bound of Paouris for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leq p \leq \sqrt {n}$</tex> to an almost-sharp bound for an arbitrary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \geq \sqrt {n}$</tex>. The question of whether it is possible to remove the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> term from the new bound is essentially equivalent to the Slicing Problem, to within logarithmic factors in n.

articleTitle: The Cohomological Excess of Certain Moduli Spaces of Curves of Genus g
abstract: The open set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline M^{\leqslant k}_g\subset \overline M_g$</tex> parameterizes stable curves of genus g having at most k rational components. By the work of Looijenga, one expects that the cohomological excess of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline M^{\leqslant k}_g$</tex> is at most g−1+k. In this paper, we show that when k=0, the conjectured upper bound is sharp by showing that there is a constructible sheaf on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline H^{\leqslant 0}_g$</tex> (the hyperelliptic locus) which has nonvanishing cohomology in degree 3g−2.

articleTitle: Counting Real Rational Curves on K3 Surfaces
abstract: We provide a real analog of the Yau–Zaslow formula counting rational curves on K3 surfaces.

articleTitle: On Nonlinear Schrödinger-Type Equations with Nonlinear Damping
abstract: We consider equations of nonlinear Schrödinger-type augmented by nonlinear damping terms. We show that nonlinear damping prevents finite time blow-up in several situations, which we describe. We also prove that the presence of a quadratic confinement in all spatial directions drives the solution of our model to zero for large time. In the case without external potential we prove that the solution may not go to zero for large time due to (nontrivial) scattering.

articleTitle: Affine Surfaces With a Huge Group of Automorphisms
abstract: We describe a family of rational affine surfaces S with huge groups of automorphisms in the following sense: the normal subgroup Aut(S)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> alg</inf> of Aut(S) generated by all algebraic subgroups of Aut(S) is not generated by any countable family of such subgroups, and the quotient Aut(S)/Aut(S)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> alg</inf> cointains a free group over an uncountable set of generators.

articleTitle: Frobenius Structures on Double Hurwitz Spaces
abstract: We present a construction Frobenius structures of “dual type” on the moduli space of ramified coverings of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^1$</tex> with given ramification type over two points, generalizing Dubrovin's construction of [4, 5]. A complete hierarchy of hydrodynamic type is obtained from the corresponding deformed flat connection. This provides a suitable framework for the theory of weakly deformed soliton lattices of an enlarged class of integrable equations; as applications we consider the q-deformed Gelfand–Dickey hierarchy and the sine-Gordon equation, and explicitly compute the corresponding solutions of the Witten-Dijkgraaf-Verlinde-Verlinde (WDVV) equations.

articleTitle: Mixing Properties and the Chromatic Number of Ramanujan Complexes
abstract: Ramanujan complexes are high-dimensional simplicial complexes generalizing Ramanujan graphs. A result of Oh on quantitative property <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T)$</tex> for Lie groups over local fields is used to deduce a Mixing Lemma for such complexes. As an application, we prove that nonpartite Ramanujan complexes have “high girth” and high-chromatic number, generalizing a well-known result about Ramanujan graphs.

articleTitle: Donaldson Invariants of Symplectic Manifolds
abstract: We prove that symplectic 4-manifolds with b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>>1 have nonvanishing Donaldson invariants, and that the canonical class is always a basic class when b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>=0. We also characterize in many situations the basic classes of a Lefschetz fibration over the sphere which evaluate maximally on a generic fiber.

articleTitle: On the Gluing Formula of Real Analytic Torsion Forms
abstract: In this paper, we extend first the Bismut–Lott's analytic torsion form for flat vector bundles to the boundary case, then we establish its gluing formula on a smooth fibration under the assumption that a fiberwise Morse function exists. We assume that the metrics have product structures near the cutting hypersurface.

articleTitle: Picard Groups on Moduli of K3 Surfaces with Mukai Models
abstract: We discuss the Picard group of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {K}}_g$</tex> of quasi-polarized K3 surfaces of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\leq 12$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\neq 11$</tex>. In this range, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {K}}_g$</tex> is unirational, and a general element in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {K}}_g$</tex> is a complete intersection with respect to a vector bundle on a homogenous space, by the work of Mukai. In this paper, we find generators for the Picard group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Pic}_{{\BBQ}}({\cal {K}}_g)$</tex> using the Noether–Lefschetz (NL) theory. This verifies the NL conjecture on the moduli of K3 surfaces in these cases.

articleTitle: On Models of the Braid Arrangement and their Hidden Symmetries
abstract: The De Concini–Procesi wonderful models of the braid arrangement of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{n-1}$</tex> are equipped with a natural <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_n$</tex> action, but only the minimal model admits an “hidden” symmetry, that is, an action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{n+1}$</tex> that comes from its moduli space interpretation. In this paper, we explain why the non minimal models do not admit this extended action: they are “too small”. In particular, we construct a supermaximal model which is the smallest model that can be projected on to the maximal model and again admits an extended <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{n+1}$</tex> action. We give an explicit description of a basis for the integer cohomology of this supermaximal model. Furthermore, we deal with another hidden extended action of the symmetric group: we observe that the symmetric group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{n+k}$</tex> acts by permutation on the set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-codimensional strata of the minimal model. Even if this happens at a purely combinatorial level, it gives rise to an interesting permutation action on the elements of a basis of the integer cohomology.

The Futaki Invariant on the Blowup of Kähler Surfaces
abstract: We prove the expansion formula for the classical Futaki invariants on the blowup of Kähler surfaces using the localization method, which explains the balancing condition of Arezzo–Pacard in [2].

articleTitle: New Bounds for the Discrete Fourier Restriction to the Sphere in 4D and 5D
abstract: We prove explicit upper bounds for local densities in the Siegel mass formula for systems of quadratic equations. Using this we derive sharp estimates for the additive energy of the lattice points on the 4D and 5D sphere. When combined with incidence geometry this leads to an improvement in the range for the discrete Fourier restriction for the sphere in 4D and 5D.

articleTitle: Ergodic Properties of Random Holomorphic Endomorphisms of ℙk
abstract: We study ergodic properties of compositions of holomorphic endomorphisms of the complex projective space chosen independently at random according to some probability distribution. Along the way, we construct positive closed currents which have good invariance and convergence properties. We provide a sufficient condition for these currents to have Hölder continuous quasi-potentials. We also prove central limit theorem for d.s.h and Hölder continuous observables.

articleTitle: Random Matrix Model for Free Meixner Laws
abstract: Applying the concept of matricial freeness which generalizes freeness in free probability, we have recently studied asymptotic joint distributions of symmetric blocks of Gaussian random matrices (Gaussian Symmetric Block Ensemble). This approach gives a block refinement of the fundamental result of Voiculescu on asymptotic freeness of independent Gaussian random matrices. In this paper, we show that this framework is natural for constructing a random matrix model for free Meixner laws. We also demonstrate that the ensemble of independent matrices of this type is asymptotically conditionally free with respect to the pair of partial traces.

articleTitle: Projective Generation of Curves (III)
abstract: Let A be an affine domain of dimension n over a field of characteristic zero. Let I⊂A[T] be a local complete intersection ideal of height n such that μ(I/I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)=n. This paper examines under what condition I is surjective image of a projective A[T]-module of rank n. More specifically, one is interested in knowing when is an element (I,ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</inf>) of the Euler class group E(A[T]) obtained as the Euler class of a projective A[T]-module. It is proved that such a phenomenon occurs if and only if the naturally induced element (I(0),ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I(0)</inf>) of the Euler class group E(A) is obtained as the Euler class of a projective A-module.

articleTitle: Conformal Embeddings and Simple Current Extensions
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the structure of intermediate vertex algebras associated with a maximal conformal embedding of a reductive Lie algebra in a semisimple Lie algebra of classical type.

articleTitle: C is not Equivalent to C− in its Jacobian: A Tropical Point of View
abstract: We show that the Abel–Jacobi image of a tropical curve C in its Jacobian J(C) is not algebraically equivalent to its reflection by using a simple calculation in tropical homology.

articleTitle: On Quasi-conformal Harmonic Maps Between Surfaces
abstract: The following theorem is proved: If w is a quasi-conformal harmonic mapping between two Riemann surfaces with compact and smooth boundaries and approximate analytic metrics, then w is bi-Lipschitz continuous with respect to internal metrics. If the surfaces are subsets of the Euclidean spaces, then w is bi-Lipschitz with respect to the Euclidean metrics.

articleTitle: Deformability of Lie Algebra Bundles and Geometry of Rational Surfaces
abstract: When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X=X_{n}$</tex> is a blowup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{2}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\leq 9$</tex>, there is a canonical (affine) Lie algebra bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {E}_{0}^{E_{n}}$</tex> over it, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{9}$</tex> is the affine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{8}$</tex>. In this paper, we will give a detail study of the relationship between the geometry of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{n}$</tex> and the deformability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {E}_{0}^{E_{n}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: On Higher Genus Welschinger Invariants of del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: The Welschinger invariants of real rational algebraic surfaces count real rational curves that represent a given divisor class and pass through a generic conjugation-invariant configuration of points. No invariants counting real curves of positive genera are known in general. We indicate particular situations, when Welschinger-type invariants counting real curves of positive genera can be defined. We also prove the positivity and give asymptotic estimates for such Welschinger-type invariants for several del Pezzo surfaces of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ge 2$</tex> and suitable real nef and big divisor classes. In particular, this yields the existence of real curves of given genus and of given divisor class passing through any appropriate configuration of real points on the given surface.

articleTitle: Nonexistence of Quasiconformal Maps Between Certain Metric Measure Spaces
abstract: We provide new conditions that ensure that two metric measure spaces are not quasiconformally equivalent. As an application, we deduce that there exists no quasiconformal map between the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg and roto-translation groups.

articleTitle: On Global Existence of 3D Charge Critical Dirac–Klein–Gordon System
abstract: In this paper, we prove the global well-posedness property of charge critical Dirac–Klein–Gordon (DKG) system in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^{3+1}$</tex> for small initial data in a space of scale invariant data which has extra weighted regularity in the angular variables. Therefore, by finite speed propagation, we could also derive the local well-posedness property for large initial data in the same space. To the best of author's knowledge, our result appears to be the first result on the critical 3D DKG concerning initial data in a scale invariant space.

articleTitle: Adler–Gelfand–Dickey Approach to Classical W-Algebras Within the Theory of Poisson Vertex Algebras
abstract: We put the Adler–Gelfand–Dickey approach to classical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}$</tex>-algebras in the framework of Poisson vertex algebras. We show how to recover the bi-Poisson structure of the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy, together with its generalizations and reduction to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>th Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, using the formal distribution calculus and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-bracket formalism. We apply the Lenard–Magri scheme to prove integrability of the corresponding hierarchies. We also give a simple proof of a theorem of Kupershmidt and Wilson in this framework. Based on this approach, we generalize all these results to the matrix case. In particular, we find (nonlocal) bi-Poisson structures of the matrix KP and the matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>th KdV hierarchies, and we prove integrability of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>th matrix KdV hierarchy.

articleTitle: 3-Manifolds that Can Be Made Acyclic
abstract: We determine which 3-manifolds admit a unitary representation such that the corresponding twisted chain complex is acyclic.

articleTitle: Sur L’algébrisation Des Tissus De Rang Maximal
abstract: Soit n≥2, r≥2 et d≥(r+1)(n−1)+2 des entiers. Nous montrons qu’un d-tissu de codimension r sur un germe de variété de dimension rn est algébrisable au sens classique s’il est de rang maximal, sauf peut-être lorsque n≥3 et d=(r+2)(n−1)+1. Dans ce dernier cas, nous montrons qu’il est algébrisable, mais en un sens généralisé.

articleTitle: A Cocycle in the Adjoint Representation of the Orthogonal Free Quantum Groups
abstract: We show that the orthogonal free quantum groups are not inner amenable and we construct an explicit proper cocycle weakly contained in the regular representation. This strengthens the result of Vaes and the second author, showing that the associated von Neumann algebras are full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm II}_1$</tex>-factors and Brannan's result showing that the orthogonal free quantum groups have Haagerup's approximation property. We also deduce Ozawa–Popa's property strong (HH) and give a new proof of Isono's result about strong solidity.

articleTitle: On Two Questions of Entin, Keating, and Rudnick on Primitive Dirichlet Characters
abstract: This is Part II of the paper “A question of Keating and Rudnick about primitive Dirichlet characters with squarefree conductor” [4]. Here, we prove two independence results for tuples of character sums, either formed with a variable character and its powers or formed with two characters and their product.

articleTitle: Equivariant Cohomology of Weighted Grassmannians and Weighted Schubert Classes
abstract: In this paper, we study the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>-equivariant cohomology of the weighted Grassmannians wGr(d,n) introduced by Corti–Reid [4], where T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf> is the n-dimensional torus that naturally acts on wGr(d,n). We introduce the equivariant weighted Schubert classes and, after we show that they form a basis of the equivariant cohomology, we give an explicit formula for the structure constants with respect to this Schubert basis. We also find a linearly independent subset {wu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,wu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</inf>} of Lie(T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>)* such that those structure constants are polynomials in wu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>'s with nonnegative coefficients, up to a permutation on the weights.

articleTitle: An Algebro-geometric Construction of Lower Central Series of Associative Algebras
abstract: The lower central series invariants M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> of an associative algebra A are the two-sided ideals generated by k-fold iterated commutators; the M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> provide a filtration of A. We study the relationship between the geometry of X=Spec A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ab</inf> and the associated graded components N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> of this filtration. We show that the N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> form coherent sheaves on a certain nilpotent thickening of X, and that Zariski localization on X coincides with noncommutative localization of A. Under certain freeness assumptions on A, we give an alternative construction of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> purely in terms of the geometry of X (and in particular, independent of A). Applying a construction of Kapranov, we exhibit the N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> as natural vector bundles on the category of smooth schemes.

articleTitle: Class Numbers of Central Simple Algebras Over Global Function Fields
abstract: Let K be a global function field together with a place <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex>, and A be the subring of functions regular outside <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex>. In this paper we present an effective method to evaluate the (locally free) class number of an arbitrary hereditary A-order in an arbitrary definite central simple K-algebra. We also show that the class number of any nonprincipal genus for a hereditary order in D can be reduced to that of the principal genus for another hereditary order in D.

articleTitle: An Infinite Family of 2-Groups with Mixed Beauville Structures
abstract: We construct an infinite family of triples (G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>,H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>,T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>), where G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> are 2-groups of increasing order, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> are index 2 subgroups of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>, and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> are pairs of generators of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>. We show that the triples u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>=(G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>,H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>,T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>) are mixed Beauville structures if k is not a power of 2. This is the first known infinite family of 2-groups admitting mixed Beauville structures. Moreover, the associated Beauville surface S(u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) is real and, for k>3 not a power of 2, the Beauville surface S(u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>) is not biholomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline {S(u_k)}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Local Triviality for Continuous Field C*-Algebras
abstract: Let X be a finite-dimensional compact metrizable space. Let A be a separable continuous field C*-algebra over X with all fibers isomorphic to the same stable Kirchberg algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal D$</tex>. We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mathcal D$</tex> has finitely generated K-theory and it satisfies the Universal Coefficient Theorem in KK-theory, then there exists a dense open subset U of X such that the ideal A(U) is locally trivial. The assumptions that the space X is finite-dimensional and that the K-theory of the fiber is finitely generated are both necessary.

articleTitle: Lattice Points in Polytopes, Box Splines, and Todd Operators
abstract: Let X be a list of vectors that is unimodular and let B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> be the box spline defined by X. In a previous article, the author proved that every real-valued function on the set of interior lattice points of the zonotope defined by X can be extended to a function on the whole zonotope of the form p(D)B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> in a unique way, where p(D) is a differential operator that is contained in the so-called internal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {P}$</tex>-space. In this paper, we construct an explicit solution to this interpolation problem as a truncation of the Todd operator. This slightly generalizes the De Concini–Procesi–Vergne deconvolution formula. As a corollary we obtain a slight generalization of the Khovanskii–Pukhlikov formula that relates the volume and the number of integer points in a smooth lattice polytope.

articleTitle: Bounded Gaps Between Primes of a Special Form
abstract: For each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m\geq 1$</tex>, there exist infinitely many primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ p_1 \lt p_2 \lt \cdots \lt p_{m+1} $</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ p_{m+1}-p_1=O\left(m^4{\rm e}^{8m}\right)$$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_j+2$</tex> has at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${16m \over \log 2}+{5\log m \over \log 2}+37$$</tex> prime divisors for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j$</tex>.

articleTitle: Discrete Time q-TASEPs
abstract: We introduce two new exactly solvable (stochastic) interacting particle systems which are discrete time versions of q-TASEP. We call these geometric and Bernoulli discrete time q-TASEP. We obtain concise formulas for expectations of a large enough class of observables of the systems to completely characterize their fixed time distributions when started from step initial condition. We then extract Fredholm determinant formulas for the marginal distribution of the location of any given particle.Underlying this work is the fact that these expectations solve closed systems of difference equations which can be rewritten as free evolution equations with k−1 two-body boundary conditions—discrete q-deformed versions of the quantum delta Bose gas. These can be solved via a nested contour integral ansatz. The same solutions also arise in the study of Macdonald processes, and we show how the systems of equations our expectations solve are equivalent to certain commutation relations involving the Macdonald first difference operator.

articleTitle: Deficiency Symmetries of Surgeries in S3
abstract: We examine certain symmetries in the deficiencies of a rational surgery on a knot in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^3$</tex> by comparing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Spin}^c$</tex>-structures on the rational surgery with those on a related integral surgery. We then provide an application of these symmetries in the form of a theorem that obstructs Dehn surgeries in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^3$</tex>. This last part unifies and generalizes two theorems by Greene which underlie his work on the cabling conjecture, the lens space realization problem, and the unknotting number of alternating 3-braids.

articleTitle: Chord Diagrams and Generic Real Rational Planar Curves of Degree 4
abstract: We associate a chord diagram to each generic real degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4$</tex> planar rational curve and prove that the rigid isotopy classes of such curves are determined completely by their chord diagrams.

articleTitle: On the Concavity of the Arithmetic Volumes
abstract: In this paper, we study the differentiability of the arithmetic volumes along arithmetic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}$</tex>-divisors, and give some equality conditions for the Brunn–Minkowski inequality for arithmetic volumes over the cone of nef and big arithmetic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}$</tex>-divisors.

articleTitle: Short-Time Regularity for the H-Surface Flow
abstract: We consider the heat flow associated with the H-surface system given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\eqalignno{\partial_tu-\Delta u =-2 (H\circ u)D_1u\times D_2u \quad\rm {on} \ B\times(0,\infty),\cr\quad u(\cdot,0)=u_o\hbox{ on }B,\quad u=g \hbox{ on }\partial B\times(0,\infty),}$$</tex> for a prescribed bounded and continuous function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\colon {{\BBR}}^3\to {{\BBR}}$</tex> satisfying an isoperimetric condition of type c for 0<c<1 and time-independent Dirichlet data g of class C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,γ</sup>. Here, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\subset {{\BBR}}^2$</tex> denotes the unit disk. For the global solutions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\colon B\to {{\BBR}}^3$</tex> constructed in a preceding work, we prove short-time regularity in the sense that u and Du are locally Hölder continuous on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {B}\times (0,T)$</tex> up to a singular time T>0. From this, we deduce the existence of a global solution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde u\colon B\times (0,\infty)\to {{\BBR}}^3$</tex> that is regular except from finitely many singular times.

articleTitle: Classification of the Invariant Subspaces of the Cohen–Wales Representation of the Artin Group of Type Dn
abstract: Recently, Cohen and Wales built a faithful linear representation of the Artin group of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_n$</tex>, hence showing the linearity of this group. It was later discovered that this representation is reducible for some complex values of its two parameters. It was also shown that when the representation is reducible, the action on a proper invariant subspace is a Hecke algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_n$</tex> action. The goal of this paper is to classify these proper invariant subspaces in terms of Specht modules indexed by double partitions of the integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. This work is the continuation of [9].

articleTitle: A Trace Formula for the Quantization of Coadjoint Orbits
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to compute the characteristic class of the Alekseev–Lachowska <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\star$</tex>-product on coadjoint orbits. We deduce an analog of the Weyl dimension formula in the context of deformation quantization.

articleTitle: Six-Dimensional Solvmanifolds with Holomorphically Trivial Canonical Bundle
abstract: We determine the 6D solvmanifolds admitting an invariant complex structure with holomorphically trivial canonical bundle. Such complex structures are classified up to isomorphism, and the existence of strong Kähler with torsion, generalized Gauduchon, balanced and strongly Gauduchon metrics is studied. As an application, we construct a holomorphic family <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,J_a)$</tex> of compact complex manifolds such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,J_a)$</tex> satisfies the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial {\bar {\partial }}$</tex>-lemma and admits a balanced metric for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a\not =0$</tex>, but the central limit neither satisfies the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial {\bar {\partial }}$</tex>-lemma nor admits balanced metrics.

articleTitle: An Analytic Framework for the Supercritical Lane–Emden Equation and its Gradient Flow
abstract: The natural setting for the Lane–Emden equation −Δu=|u|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p−2</sup>u on a domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \subset {\BBR}^n$</tex>, n≥3, for supercritical exponents p>2*=2n/(n−2) is identified as the space of functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\in H^1_0\cap L^p(\Omega)$</tex> with finite scale-invariant Morrey norms. We show that this Morrey regularity is propagated by the heat flow associated with this equation, and we study the blow-up profiles.

articleTitle: Categorical Resolutions of Irrational Singularities
abstract: We show that the derived category of any singularity over a field of characteristic 0 can be embedded fully and faithfully into a smooth triangulated category that has a semiorthogonal decomposition with components equivalent to derived categories of smooth varieties. This provides a categorical resolution of the singularity.

articleTitle: Bounded Orbits of Diagonalizable Flows on SL3(ℝ)/SL3(ℤ)
abstract: We prove that for any countably many one-parameter diagonalizable subgroups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_n$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {SL}_3({\BBR})$</tex>, the set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda \in \hbox {SL}_3({\BBR})/\hbox {SL}_3({\BBZ})$</tex> such that all the orbits <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_n\Lambda $</tex> are bounded has full Hausdorff dimension.

articleTitle: Spectra for Semiclassical Operators with Periodic Bicharacteristics in Dimension Two
abstract: We study the distribution of eigenvalues for selfadjoint <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-pseudodifferential operators in dimension two, arising as perturbations of selfadjoint operators with a periodic classical flow. When the strength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> of the perturbation is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ll h$</tex>, the spectrum displays a cluster structure, and assuming that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \gg h^2$</tex> (or sometimes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gg h^{N_0}$</tex>, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_0 \gt 1$</tex> large), we obtain a complete asymptotic description of the individual eigenvalues inside subclusters, corresponding to the regular values of the leading symbol of the perturbation, averaged along the flow.

articleTitle: Fano Manifolds with Weak almost Kähler–Ricci Solitons
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a sequence of weak almost Kähler–Ricci solitons under further suitable conditions converges to a Kähler–Ricci soliton with complex codimension of singularities at least 2 in the Gromov–Hausdorff topology. As a corollary, we show that on a Fano manifold with the modified K-energy bounded below, there exists a sequence of weak almost Kähler–Ricci solitons which converges to a Kähler–Ricci soliton with complex codimension of singularities at least 2 in the Gromov–Hausdorff topology.

articleTitle: The Derived Category of Quasi-Coherent Modules on an Artin Stack Via Model Structures
abstract: We define the derived category of quasi-coherent sheaves for certain Artin stacks as the homotopy category of two Quillen monoidal model structures on the corresponding category of unbounded complexes of quasi-coherent sheaves.

articleTitle: Rigidity Theorems for Diameter Estimates of Compact Manifold with Boundary
abstract: Let (N,g) be an n-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold with nonempty boundary ∂N. Assume that the Ricci curvature of (N,g) has a negative lower bound Ric≥−(n−1)c<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for some c>0, and the mean curvature of the boundary ∂N satisfies H≥(n−1)c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>>(n−1)c for some c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>>c>0. Then a known result (cf. [12]) says that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sup _{x\in N}d(x,\partial N)\leq {1c \over \coth} ^{-1} {c_0\over c}$</tex>. In this paper, we prove the rigidity result that if N is compact, then the equality holds if and only if (N,g) is isometric to the geodesic ball of radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1c \over \coth} ^{-1} {c_0\over c}$</tex> in an n-dimensional hyperbolic space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBH}^n(-c^2)$</tex> of constant sectional curvature −c<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Moreover, we prove an analogous result for manifold with m-Bakry–Émery Ricci curvature bounded below by a negative constant.

articleTitle: Tetrahedron Equation and Cyclic Quantum Dilogarithm Identities
abstract: We establish a hierarchy of quantum dilogarithm identities associated to a sequence of triangular shaped quivers. The tetrahedron equation plays a key role in our construction.

articleTitle: On Three-Dimensional Alexandrov Spaces
abstract: We study three-dimensional (3D) Alexandrov spaces with a lower curvature bound, focusing on extending several results on closed 3D manifolds: first, we show that a closed 3D Alexandrov space of positive curvature, with at least one topological singularity, must be homeomorphic to the suspension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}P^2$</tex>; we use this to classify, up to homeomorphism, closed, positively curved Alexandrov spaces of dimension three. Secondly, we classify closed 3D Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature. Thirdly, we study the well-known Poincaré Conjecture in dimension three, in the context of Alexandrov spaces, in the two forms it is usually formulated for manifolds. We first show that the only closed 3D Alexandrov space that is also a homotopy sphere is the three-sphere; then we give examples of closed, geometric, simply connected 3D Alexandrov spaces for five of the eight Thurston geometries, proving along the way the impossibility of getting such examples for the Nil, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde {{\rm {SL}}_2({\BBR})}$</tex>, and Sol geometries. We conclude the paper by proving the analog of the geometrization conjecture for closed 3D Alexandrov spaces.

articleTitle: On the Topological Minimality of Unions of Planes of Arbitrary Dimension
abstract: In this article, we prove the topological minimality of unions of several almost orthogonal planes of arbitrary dimensions. A particular case was proved in [13], where we proved the Almgren minimality (which is a weaker property than the topological minimality) of the union of two almost orthogonal two-dimensional planes. On the one hand, the topological minimality is almost always proved by variations of calibration methods, but in this article, we give a continuous family topological minimal sets, hence calibrations cannot apply. The advantage of a set being topological minimal (compared with Almgren minimal) is that its product with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex> stays topological minimal. This leads also to finding minimal sets which are unions of non transversal (hence far from almost orthogonal) planes. Notice that the regularity for higher dimensional minimal sets is much less clear than those of dimension 2, hence more efforts are needed for the present higher dimensional case.

articleTitle: Foliations Modeling Nonrational Simplicial Toric Varieties
abstract: We establish a correspondence between simplicial fans, not necessarily rational, and certain foliated compact complex manifolds called LVMB-manifolds (named after López de Medrano, Verjovsky, Meersseman, Bosio-manifolds). In the rational case, Meersseman and Verjovsky have shown that the leaf space is the usual toric variety. We compute the basic Betti numbers of the foliation for shellable fans. When the fan is in particular polytopal, we prove that the basic cohomology of the foliation is generated in degree 2. We give evidence that the rich interplay between convex and algebraic geometries embodied by toric varieties carries over to our nonrational construction. In fact, our approach unifies rational and nonrational cases.

articleTitle: Tau Function and Moduli of Spin Curves
abstract: The goal of the paper is to give an analytic proof of the formula of G. Farkas for the divisor class of spinors with multiple zeros in the moduli space of odd spin curves. We make use of the technique developed by Korotkin and Zograf that is based on properties of the Bergman tau function.

articleTitle: R-Equivalence and 𝔸1-Connectedness in Anisotropic Groups
abstract: We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is an anisotropic, semisimple, absolutely almost simple, simply connected group over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>, then two elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> over any field extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-equivalent if and only if they are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-equivalent. This has two important consequences. First, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\BBA^1$</tex>-singular construction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Sing}_* (G)$</tex> cannot be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-local for such groups. Secondly, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-connected components of a semisimple, absolutely almost simple, simply connected algebraic group of classical type over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> form a sheaf of abelian groups.

articleTitle: A Note on Failure of Energy Reversal for Classical Fractional Singular Integrals
abstract: For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\leq \alpha \lt n$</tex>, we demonstrate the failure of energy reversal for the vector of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-fractional Riesz transforms, and more generally for the vector of all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-fractional convolution singular integrals having a kernel with vanishing integral on every great circle of the sphere.

articleTitle: Uniform Hyperbolicity for Szegő Cocycles and Applications to Random CMV Matrices and the Ising Model
abstract: We consider products of the matrices associated with the Szegő recursion from the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle and show that under suitable assumptions, their norms grow exponentially in the number of factors. In the language of dynamical systems, this result expresses a uniform hyperbolicity statement. We present two applications of this result. On the one hand, we identify explicitly the almost sure spectrum of extended CMV matrices with nonnegative random Verblunsky coefficients. On the other hand, we show that no Ising model in one dimension exhibits a phase transition. Also, in the case of dynamically generated interaction couplings, we describe a gap labeling theorem for the Lee-Yang zeros in the thermodynamic limit.

articleTitle: An Explicit Bound for the First Sign Change of the Fourier Coefficients of a Siegel Cusp Form
abstract: We give an explicit upper bound for the first sign change of the Fourier coefficients of an arbitrary nonzero Siegel cusp form F of even integral weight on the Siegel modular group of arbitrary genus g≥2.

articleTitle: Bridge Spectra of Twisted Torus Knots
abstract: We compute the genus zero bridge numbers and give lower bounds on the genus 1 bridge numbers for a large class of sufficiently generic hyperbolic twisted torus knots. As a result, the bridge spectra of these knots have two gaps which can be chosen to be arbitrarily large, providing the first known examples of hyperbolic knots exhibiting this property. In addition, we show that there are Berge and Dean knots with arbitrarily large genus 1 bridge numbers, and as a result, we give solutions to problems of Eudave-Muñoz concerning tunnel number one knots.

articleTitle: Rigidity of Complete Entire Self-Shrinking Solutions to Kähler–Ricci Flow
abstract: We show that every complete entire self-shrinking solution on complex Euclidean space to the Kähler–Ricci flow must be generated from a quadratic potential.

articleTitle: A Characterization of Holomorphic Borcherds Lifts by Symmetries
abstract: In this paper, we show that, in the holomorphic automorphic case, the Borcherds lifts on the orthogonal group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(2, n+2)$</tex> are characterized by certain symmetries and describe the inverse of the Borcherds lifting in terms of Fourier–Jacobi expansion. We also give a characterization of the modular polynomials by certain symmetries.

articleTitle: Uniform Bounds for Period Integrals and Sparse Equidistribution
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M=\Gamma \backslash \hbox {PSL}(2,{\BBR})$</tex> be a compact manifold, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in C^\infty (M)$</tex> be a function of zero average. We use spectral methods to get uniform (i.e., independent of spectral gap) bounds for twisted averages of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> along long horocycle orbit segments. We apply this to obtain an equidistribution result for sparse subsets of horocycles on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Simple Proof of the Formula for the Betti Numbers of the Quasihomogeneous Hilbert Schemes
abstract: In a recent paper, the first two authors proved that the generating series of the Poincare polynomials of the quasihomogeneous Hilbert schemes of points in the plane has a simple decomposition in an infinite product. In this paper, we give a very short geometrical proof of that formula.

articleTitle: Embeddability and Universal Theory of Partially Commutative Groups
abstract: The first part of the paper centers in the study of embeddability between partially commutative groups. In [10], for a finite simplicial graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>, the authors introduce an infinite, locally infinite graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ^e$</tex>, called the extension graph of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>. They show that each finite-induced subgraph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta $</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ^e$</tex> gives rise to an embedding between the partially commutative groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBG}}(\Delta )$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBG}}(\Gamma )$</tex>. Furthermore, it is proved that, in many instances, the converse also holds. Our first result is the decidability of the Extension Graph Embedding Problem: there is an algorithm that given two finite simplicial graphs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta $</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex> decides whether or not <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta $</tex> is an induced subgraph of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ^e$</tex>. As a corollary, we obtain the decidability of the Embedding Problem for 2D partially commutative groups. In the second part of the paper, we relate the Embedding Problem between partially commutative groups to the model-theoretic question of classification up to universal equivalence. We use our characterization to transfer algebraic and algorithmic results on embeddability to model-theoretic ones and obtain some rigidity results on the elementary theory of atomic pc groups as well as to deduce the existence of an algorithm to decide if an arbitrary pc group is universally equivalent to a 2D one.

articleTitle: Shimura Varieties in the Torelli Locus via Galois Coverings
abstract: Given a family of Galois coverings of the projective line, we give a simple sufficient condition ensuring that the closure of the image of the family via the period mapping is a special (or Shimura) subvariety of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_g$</tex>. By a computer program we get the list of all families in genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \leq {9}$</tex> satisfying our condition. There are no families with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g=8,9$</tex>; all of them are in genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \leq 7$</tex>. These examples are related to a conjecture of Oort. Among them we get the cyclic examples constructed by various authors (Shimura, Mostow, De Jong-Noot, Rohde, Moonen, and others) and the abelian noncyclic examples found by Moonen–Oort. We get seven new nonabelian examples.

articleTitle: Lp Geominimal Surface Areas and their Inequalities
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface area for all −n≠p<1, which extends the classical geominimal surface area (p=1) by Petty and the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface area by Lutwak (p>1). Our extension of the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface area is motivated by recent work on the extension of the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> affine surface area—a fundamental object in (affine) convex geometry. We prove some properties for the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface area and its related inequalities, such as, the affine isoperimetric inequality and a Santaló style inequality. Cyclic inequalities are established to obtain the monotonicity of the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface areas. Comparison between the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> geominimal surface area and the p-surface area is also provided.

articleTitle: Conformal Nets I: Coordinate-Free Nets
abstract: We describe a coordinate-free perspective on conformal nets, as functors from intervals to von Neumann algebras. We discuss an operation of fusion of intervals and observe that a conformal net takes a fused interval to the fiber product of von Neumann algebras. Though coordinate-free nets do not a priori have vacuum sectors, we show that there is a vacuum sector canonically associated to any circle equipped with a conformal structure. This is the first in a series of papers constructing a 3-category of conformal nets, defects, sectors, and intertwiners.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Resonances with a Potential: Multilinear Estimates and an Application to NLS
abstract: This paper considers the question of global in time existence and asymptotic behavior of small-data solutions of nonlinear dispersive equations with a real potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>. The main concern is treating nonlinearities whose degree is low enough as to preclude the simple use of classical energy methods and decay estimates. In their place, we present a systematic approach that adapts the space-time resonance method to the non-Euclidean setting using the spectral theory of the Schrödinger operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta +V$</tex>. We start by developing tools of independent interest, namely multilinear analysis (Coifman–Meyer type theorems) in the framework of the corresponding distorted Fourier transform. As a first application, this is then used to prove global existence and scattering for a quadratic Schrödinger equation.

articleTitle: Balanced Line Bundles and Equivariant Compactifications of Homogeneous Spaces
abstract: Manin's conjecture predicts an asymptotic formula for the number of rational points of bounded height on a smooth projective variety X in terms of global geometric invariants of X. The strongest form of the conjecture implies certain inequalities among geometric invariants of X and of its subvarieties. We provide a general geometric framework explaining these phenomena, via the notion of balanced line bundles, and prove the required inequalities for a large class of equivariant compactifications of homogeneous spaces.

articleTitle: Characters of Positive Height in Blocks of Finite Quasi-Simple Groups
abstract: Eaton and Moretó proposed an extension of Brauer's famous height zero conjecture on blocks of finite groups to the case of nonabelian defect groups, which predicts the smallest nonzero height in such blocks in terms of local data. We show that their conjecture holds for principal blocks of quasi-simple groups, for all blocks of finite reductive groups in their defining characteristic, as well as for all covering groups of symmetric and alternating groups. For the proof, we determine the minimal nontrivial character degrees of Sylow <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-subgroups of finite reductive groups in characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. We provide some further evidence for blocks of groups of Lie type considered in cross characteristic.

articleTitle: Characteristic Classes in Deformation Quantization
abstract: In deformation quantization, one can associate five characteristic functions to (stable) formality morphisms on cochains and chains and to “two-brane” formality morphisms. We show that these characteristic functions agree.

articleTitle: On the Mordell–Gruber Spectrum
abstract: We investigate the Mordell constant of certain families of lattices, in particular, of lattices arising from totally real fields. We define the almost sure value κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</inf> of the Mordell constant with respect to certain homogeneous measures on the space of lattices, and establish a strict inequality κμ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><κμ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> when the μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> are finite and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {supp}}(\mu _1) \varsubsetneq {\rm supp} (\mu _2)$</tex>. In combination with known results regarding the dynamics of the diagonal group we obtain isolation results as well as information regarding accumulation points of the Mordell–Gruber spectrum, extending previous work of Gruber and Ramharter. One of the main tools we develop is the associated algebra, an algebraic invariant attached to the orbit of a lattice under a block group, which can be used to characterize closed and finite volume orbits.

articleTitle: Bounded Rational Points on Curves
abstract: We establish the uniform estimate ≪<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/d</sup> for the number of rational points of height at most N on an irreducible curve of degree d. We deduce this from a result for general hypersurfaces that is sensitive to the coefficients of the corresponding form.

articleTitle: Distribution of Squares Modulo a Composite Number
abstract: In this paper, we study the distribution of squares modulo a square-free number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>. We also look at inverse questions for the large sieve in the distribution aspect and we make improvements on existing results on the distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-tuples of reduced residues.

articleTitle: h-Principle for Contact Foliations
abstract: In this article, we introduce the topological study of codimension-1 foliations which admit contact structures on the leaves. A parametric existence h-principle for foliated contact structures is provided for any cooriented foliation in a closed oriented four-fold.

articleTitle: Positively Curved GKM-Manifolds
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> be a torus of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\geq }k$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>-manifold. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is a GKM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_k$</tex>-manifold if the action is equivariantly formal, has only isolated fixed points, and any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> weights of the isotropy representation in the fixed points are linearly independent. In this paper, we compute the cohomology rings with real and integer coefficients of GKM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex>- and GKM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_4$</tex>-manifolds which admit invariant metrics of positive sectional curvature.

articleTitle: Covariograms Generated by Valuations
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> be a real-valued valuation on the family of compact convex subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a convex body in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^n$</tex>.
