We introduce the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>-covariogram <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{K,\phi }$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> as the function associating to each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in {\BBR}^n$</tex> the value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi (K \cap (K+x))$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is the volume, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{K,\phi }$</tex> is the covariogram, extensively studied in various sources. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is a quermassintegral (e.g., surface area or mean width) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{K,\phi }$</tex> has been introduced by Nagel [26]. We study various properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>-covariograms, mostly in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=2$</tex> and under the assumption that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is translation invariant, monotone, and even. We also consider the generalization of Matheron's covariogram problem to the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>-covariograms, that is, the problem of determining an unknown convex body <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>, up to translations and point reflections, by the knowledge of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_{K,\phi }$</tex>. A positive solution to this problem is provided under different assumptions, including the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is a polygon and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is either strictly monotone or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is the width in a given direction. We prove that there are examples in every dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 3$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is determined by its covariogram but it is not determined by its width-covariogram. We also present some consequence of this study in stochastic geometry.

articleTitle: Alpha Invariants and K-Stability for General Polarizations of Fano Varieties
abstract: We provide a sufficient condition for polarizations of Fano varieties to be K-stable in terms of Tian's alpha invariant, which uses the log canonical threshold to measure singularities of divisors in the linear system associated to the polarization. This generalizes a result of Odaka–Sano in the anti-canonically polarized case, which is the algebraic counterpart of Tian's analytic criterion implying the existence of a Kähler–Einstein metric. As an application, we give new K-stable polarizations of a general degree 1 del Pezzo surface. We also prove a corresponding result for log K-stability.

articleTitle: Model Transition for Representations of Metaplectic Type
abstract: We study the interplay between different models of the same irreducible representation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>-points of a reductive group over a local field.

articleTitle: Finiteness of Calabi–Yau Quasismooth Weighted Complete Intersections
abstract: We prove that there exist only finitely many families of Calabi–Yau quasismooth weighted complete intersections with every fixed dimension m. This generalizes a result of Johnson and Kollár to higher codimensions.

articleTitle: Symmetric Solutions to Dispersionless 2D Toda Hierarchy, Hurwitz Numbers, and Conformal Dynamics
abstract: We explicitly construct the series expansion for a certain class of solutions to the 2D Toda hierarchy in the zero dispersion limit, which we call symmetric solutions. We express the Taylor coefficients through some universal combinatorial constants and find recurrence relations for them. These results are used to obtain new formulas for the genus 0 double Hurwitz numbers. They can also serve as a starting point for a constructive approach to the Riemann mapping problem and the inverse potential problem in 2D.

articleTitle: A Dynamical Point of View on the Set of ℬ-Free Integers
abstract: Sarnak has recently initiated the study of the Möbius function and its square, the characteristic function of square-free integers, from a dynamical point of view, introducing the Möbius flow and the square-free flow as the action of the shift map on the respective subshfits generated by these functions. In this paper, we extend the study of the square-free flow to the more general context of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {B}$</tex>-free integers, that is to say integers with no factor in a given family <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {B}$</tex> of pairwise relatively prime integers, the sum of whose reciprocals is finite. Relying on dynamical arguments, we prove in particular that the distribution of patterns in the characteristic function of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {B}$</tex>-free integers follows a shift-invariant probability measure, and gives rise to a measurable dynamical system isomorphic to a specific minimal rotation on a compact group. As a by-product, we obtain the abundance of twin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {B}$</tex>-free numbers. Moreover, we show that the distribution of patterns in small intervals of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[N,N+ \sqrt {N})$</tex> also conforms to the same measure. When elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr {B}$</tex> are squares, we introduce a generalization of the Möbius function, and discuss a conjecture of Chowla in this broader context.

articleTitle: Vanishing of the First Continuous L2-Cohomology for II1 Factors
abstract: We prove that the continuous version of the Connes–Shlyakhtenko first L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-cohomology for II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> factors, as proposed by Thom [8], always vanishes.

articleTitle: Transitivity of Automorphism Groups of Gizatullin Surfaces
abstract: We show that the automorphism group of a certain subclass of smooth Gizatullin surfaces with a distinguished and rigid extended divisor is generated by automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\BBA^1$</tex>-fibrations. Moreover, such surfaces yield examples of smooth Gizatullin surfaces with a nontransitive action of the automorphism group. Thus, they represent counter-examples to Gizatullin's conjecture. For such surfaces, we give an explicit orbit decomposition of the natural action of the automorphism group in some special cases. It turns out that the automorphism groups of such surfaces are amalgamated products of two subgroups.

articleTitle: Littlewood Complexes and Analogues of Determinantal Varieties
abstract: One interesting combinatorial feature of classical determinantal varieties is that the character of their coordinate rings give a natural truncation of the Cauchy identity in the theory of symmetric functions. Natural generalizations of these varieties exist and have been studied for the other classical groups. In this paper, we develop the relevant properties from scratch. By studying the isotypic decomposition of their minimal free resolutions one can recover classical identities due to Littlewood for expressing an irreducible character of a classical group in terms of Schur functions. We propose generalizations for the exceptional groups. In type G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, we completely analyze the variety and its minimal free resolution and get an analog of Littlewood's identities. We have partial results for the other cases. In particular, these varieties are always normal with rational singularities.

articleTitle: The First Initial-Boundary Value Problem for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Parabolic Equations on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we study the first initial-boundary value problem for a class of fully nonlinear parabolic equations on Riemannian manifolds. The main part of this paper is to derive the a priori estimates for the second-order derivatives of solutions by using a new idea that works under very general structure conditions. As an application, the existence of smooth solutions is proved.

articleTitle: Rectifiability via a Square Function and Preiss’ Theorem
abstract: Let E be a set in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^d$</tex> with finite n-dimensional Hausdorff measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}^n$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\liminf _{r\to 0}r^{-n}{\cal H}^n(B(x,r)\cap E) \gt 0$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal H}^n$</tex>-a.e. x∈E. In this paper, it is shown that E is n-rectifiable if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\int_0^1 \left|{{\cal H}^n(B(x,r)\cap E) \over r^n} - {{\cal H}^n(B(x,2r)\cap E) \over (2r)^n} \right|^2 {{\rm d} r \over r} \lt \infty\quad \hbox{for } {\cal H}^n-\hbox{a.e. } x \in E, $$</tex> and also if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\lim_{r\to0}\left({{\cal H}^n(B(x,r)\cap E) \over r^n} - {{\cal H}^n(B(x,2r)\cap E) \over (2r)^n}\right) = 0 \quad \hbox{for } {\cal H}^n-\hbox{a.e. } x \in E. $$</tex> Other more general results involving Radon measures are also proved.

articleTitle: Classification of Positive Energy Representations of the Virasoro Group
abstract: We give a complete classification of all unitary positive energy representations of the Virasoro group. More precisely, we prove that every such representation can be expressed in an essentially unique way as a direct integral of irreducible highest weight representations.

articleTitle: On a Foliation-Covariant Elliptic Operator on Null Hypersurfaces
abstract: We introduce a new elliptic operator on null hypersurfaces of 4D Lorentzian manifolds. This operator depends on the first and second fundamental forms of the sections of a foliation of the null hypersurface and its novelty originates from its covariant transformation under change of foliation. It thus provides at any point an elliptic structure intimately connected with the geometry of the null hypersurface, independent of the choice of a specific section through that point. No symmetries or other conditions are imposed on the metric. The spectral properties of this elliptic operator are relevant to the evolution of the wave equation, and in particular, the existence of conservation laws along null hypersurfaces.

articleTitle: The Elliptic Law
abstract: We show that, under some general assumptions on the entries of a random complex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \times n$</tex> matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_n$</tex>, the empirical spectral distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over \sqrt {n}}X_n$</tex> converges to the uniform law of an ellipsoid as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> tends to infinity. This generalizes the well-known circular law in random matrix theory.

articleTitle: Aligned CP-Semigroups
abstract: A CP-semigroup is aligned if its set of trivially maximal subordinates is totally ordered by subordination. We prove that aligned spatial E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups are prime: they have no nontrivial tensor product decompositions up to cocycle conjugacy. As a consequence, we establish the existence of uncountably many noncocycle conjugate E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-semigroups of type II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> which are prime.

articleTitle: A Finiteness Theorem for the Brauer Group of K3 Surfaces in Odd Characteristic
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be an odd prime and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be a field finitely generated over the finite field with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> elements. For any K3 surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k,$</tex> we prove that the cokernel of the natural map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Br}(k)\to \rm {Br}(X)$</tex> is finite modulo the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-primary torsion subgroup.

articleTitle: Transitions Between Critical Kernels: From the Tacnode Kernel and Critical Kernel in the Two-Matrix Model to the Pearcey Kernel
abstract: In this paper, we study two multicritical correlation kernels and prove that they converge to the Pearcey kernel in a certain double scaling limit. The first kernel appears in a model of nonintersecting Brownian motions at a tacnode. The second arises as a triple scaling limit of the eigenvalue correlation kernel in the Hermitian two-matrix model with quartic/quadratic potentials. The two kernels are different but can be expressed in terms of the same tacnode Riemann–Hilbert problem. The proof is based on a steepest descent analysis of this Riemann–Hilbert problem. A special feature in the analysis is the introduction of an explicit meromorphic function on a Riemann surface with specified sheet structure.

articleTitle: Moduli Spaces of Quadratic Rational Maps with a Marked Periodic Point of Small Order
abstract: The surface corresponding to the moduli space of quadratic endomorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBP}}^1$</tex> with a marked periodic point of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is studied. It is shown that the surface is rational over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\le 5$</tex> and is of general type for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=6$</tex>. An explicit description of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=6$</tex> surface lets us find several infinite families of quadratic endomorphisms <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: {{\BBP}}^1 \to {{\BBP}}^1$</tex> defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> with a rational periodic point of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6$</tex>. In one of these families, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> also has a rational fixed point, for a total of at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7$</tex> periodic and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7$</tex> preperiodic points. This is in contrast with the polynomial case, where it is conjectured that no polynomial endomorphism defined over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex> admits rational periodic points of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \gt 3$</tex>.Communicated by Umberto Zannier

articleTitle: Refinements to Patching and Applications to Field Invariants
abstract: We introduce a notion of refinements in the context of patching, in order to obtain new results about local–global principles and field invariants in the context of quadratic forms and central simple algebras. The fields we consider are finite extensions of the fraction fields of two-dimensional complete domains that need not be local. Our results in particular give the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex>-invariant and period-index bound for these fields, as consequences of more general abstract results.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Behavior of Eigenvalues of Hankel Operators
abstract: We consider compact Hankel operators realized in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell ^2({\BBZ}_+ )$</tex> as infinite matrices <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> with matrix elements <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(j+k)$</tex>. Roughly speaking, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(j)\sim (b_{1}+ (-1)^j b_{-1}) j^{-1}(\log j)^{-\alpha }$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j\to \infty$</tex> for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \gt 0$</tex>, then the eigenvalues of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> satisfy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{n}^{\pm } (\Gamma )\sim c^{\pm } n^{-\alpha }$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\to \infty$</tex>. The asymptotic coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c^{\pm }$</tex> are explicitly expressed in terms of the asymptotic coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_{-1}$</tex>. Similar results are obtained for Hankel operators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ {\bf {\Gamma}}}$</tex> realized in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2({\BBR}_+ )$</tex> as integral operators with kernels <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bf h}}}(t+s)$</tex>. In this case, the asymptotics of eigenvalues <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _{n}^{\pm } ({ {\bf {\Gamma}}})$</tex> are determined by the behavior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bf h}}}(t)$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\to 0$</tex> and as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\to \infty$</tex>.

articleTitle: Classification of Resolving Subcategories and Grade Consistent Functions
abstract: We classify certain resolving subcategories of finitely generated modules over a commutative noetherian ring R by using integer-valued functions on SpecR. As an application, we give a complete classification of resolving subcategories when R is a locally hypersurface ring or a complete intersection. Our results also recover and categorify a “missing theorem” by Auslander.

articleTitle: On Derived Autoequivalences of Hilbert Schemes and Generalized Kummer Varieties
abstract: We show that, for every smooth projective surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 2,$</tex> the push-forward along the diagonal embedding gives a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{n-1}$</tex>-functor into the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {S}_n$</tex>-equivariant derived category of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{n}$</tex>. Using the Bridgeland–King–Reid–Haiman equivalence, this yields a new autoequivalence of the derived category of the Hilbert scheme of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> points on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. If the canonical bundle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is trivial and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=2,$</tex> this autoequivalence coincides with the known EZ-spherical twist induced by the boundary of the Hilbert scheme. We also find <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n^4$</tex> orthogonal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{n-1}$</tex>-objects on the generalized Kummer variety associated to an abelian surface. They generalize the 16 spherical objects on the Kummer surface given by the exceptional curves.

articleTitle: Extreme Values of Class Numbers of Real Quadratic Fields
abstract: We improve a result of H. L. Montgomery and J. P. Weinberger by establishing the existence of infinitely many fundamental discriminants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d \gt 0$</tex> for which the class number of the real quadratic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}(\sqrt {d})$</tex> exceeds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2e^{\gamma }+o(1)) \sqrt {d}(\log \log d)/\log d$</tex>. We believe this bound to be best possible. We also obtain upper and lower bounds of nearly the same order of magnitude, for the number of real quadratic fields with discriminant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\leq x$</tex> which have such an extreme class number.

articleTitle: Iwahori–Matsumoto Involution and Linear Koszul Duality
abstract: We use linear Koszul duality, a geometric version of the standard duality between modules over symmetric and exterior algebras, to give a geometric realization of the Iwahori–Matsumoto involution of affine Hecke algebras. More generally, we prove that linear Koszul duality is compatible with convolution in a general context related to convolution algebras.

articleTitle: On Singular Moduli for Arbitrary Discriminants
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex> be discriminants of distinct quadratic imaginary orders <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_2}$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J(d_1,d_2)$</tex> denote the product of differences of CM <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j$</tex>-invariants with discriminants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex>. In 1985, Gross and Zagier gave an elegant formula for the factorization of the integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J(d_1,d_2)$</tex> in the case that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex> are relatively prime and discriminants of maximal orders. To compute this formula, they first reduce the problem to counting the number of simultaneous embeddings of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_2}$</tex> into endomorphism rings of supersingular curves, and then solve this counting problem.Interestingly, this counting problem also appears when computing class polynomials for invariants of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> curves. However, in this application, one must consider orders <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal O}}_{d_2}$</tex> that are non-maximal. Motivated by the application to genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> curves, we generalize the methods of Gross and Zagier and give a computable formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v_{\ell }(J(d_1,d_2))$</tex> for any pair of discriminants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1\neq d_2$</tex> and any prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell \gt 2$</tex>. In the case that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1$</tex> is squarefree and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex> is the discriminant of any quadratic imaginary order, our formula can be stated in a simple closed form. We also give a conjectural closed formula when the conductors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_2$</tex> are relatively prime.

articleTitle: Local-to-Global Extensions of 𝒟-Modules in Positive Characteristic
abstract: In [14], Katz defines the notion of a special flat connection on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBP}}^1_{{{\BBC}}}\setminus {\{ }0,\infty {\} }$</tex>, and he shows that the functor which restricts a flat connection to the punctured disc around the point at infinity gives rise to an equivalence between the category of special flat connections on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBP}}^1_{{{\BBC}}}\setminus {\{ }0,\infty {\} }$</tex> and the category of differential modules on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBC}}{(\!(}t{)\!)}$</tex>. In this article, we prove the corresponding statement over an algebraically closed field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of positive characteristic. The role of flat connections is played by vector bundles carrying an action of the (full) ring of differential operators. Such objects are also called stratified bundles. The formal local variant on the field of Laurent series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k{(\!(}t{)\!)}$</tex> is called iterated differential module. We define the notion of a special stratified bundle on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBP}}^1_{k}\setminus {\{ }0,\infty {\} }$</tex>, and show that restriction to the punctured disk around the point at infinity induces an equivalence between the category of special stratified bundles and iterated differential modules on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k{(\!(}t{)\!)}$</tex>. This extends one of the main results of [13], and has several interesting consequences which extend well-known statements about étale fundamental groups to higher-dimensional fundamental groups.

articleTitle: Cohomology Theories with Supports
abstract: For E a presheaf of spectra on the category of smooth k-schemes satisfying Nisnevich excision, we prove that the canonical map from the algebraic singular complex of the theory E with quasi-finite supports to the theory E with supports intersecting all the faces properly is a weak equivalence on smooth k-schemes that are affine or projective. This establishes some cases of a conjecture of Marc Levine.

articleTitle: Generalized Monge–Ampère Capacities
abstract: We study various capacities on compact Kähler manifolds which generalize the Bedford–Taylor Monge–Ampère capacity. We then use these capacities to study the existence and the regularity of solutions of complex Monge–Ampère equations.

articleTitle: Secant Cumulants and Toric Geometry
abstract: We study the secant line variety of the Segre product of projective spaces using special cumulant coordinates adapted for secant varieties. We show that the secant variety is covered by open normal toric varieties. We prove that in cumulant coordinates its ideal is generated by binomial quadrics. We present new results on the local structure of the secant variety. In particular, we show that it has rational singularities and we give a description of the singular locus. We also classify all secant varieties that are Gorenstein. Moreover, generalizing [31], we obtain analogous results for the tangential variety.

articleTitle: The Average of the First Invariant Factor for Reductions of CM Elliptic Curves mod p
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E/{\BBQ}$</tex> be a fixed elliptic curve. For each prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> of good reduction, write <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E({\BBF}_p) \cong {\BBZ}/d_p {\BBZ} \oplus {\BBZ}/e_p {\BBZ}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_p \mid e_p$</tex>. Kowalski proposed investigating the average value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_p$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> runs over the rational primes. For CM curves, he showed that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\log \log {x}/\log {x} \ll \sum _{p \le x} d_p \ll x\sqrt {\log {x}}.$</tex> It was shown recently by Felix and Murty that in fact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{p \le x} d_p$</tex> exceeds any constant multiple of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\log \log {x}/\log {x}$</tex>, once <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> is sufficiently large. In the opposite direction, Kim has shown that the expression <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\sqrt {\log {x}}$</tex> in the upper bound can be replaced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\log \log {x}$</tex>. In this paper, we obtain the correct order of magnitude for the sum: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{p \le x} d_p \asymp x$</tex> for all large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>.

articleTitle: Every Symplectic Toric Orbifold is a Centered Reduction of a Cartesian Product of Weighted Projective Spaces
abstract: We prove that every symplectic toric orbifold is a centered reduction of a Cartesian product of weighted projective spaces. A theorem of Abreu and Macarini shows that if the level set of the reduction passes through a non-displaceable set then the image of this set in the reduced space is also non-displaceable. Using this result, we show that every symplectic toric orbifold contains a non-displaceable fiber and we identify this fiber.

articleTitle: Cell Decompositions of Double Bott–Samelson Varieties
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be a connected complex semisimple Lie group. Webster and Yakimov have constructed partitions of the double flag variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/B \times G/B_-$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(B, B_-)$</tex> is a pair of opposite Borel subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, generalizing the Deodhar decompositions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/B$</tex>. We show that these partitions can be better understood by constructing cell decompositions of a product of two Bott–Samelson varieties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{ {\bf u}, {\bf v} }$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\bf u}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\bf v}$</tex> are sequences of simple reflections. We construct coordinates on each cell of the decompositions and in the case of a positive subexpression, we relate these coordinates to regular functions on a particular open subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{ {\bf u}, {\bf v} }$</tex>. Our motivation for constructing cell decompositions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{ {\bf u}, {\bf v} }$</tex> was to study a certain natural Poisson structure on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{ {\bf u}, {\bf v} }$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Anti-Diagonal Filtration: Reduced Theory and Applications
abstract: Given a knot <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K \subset S^3$</tex>, Seidel and Smith described a graded cohomology group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Kh_{\rm symp,inv}(K)$</tex>, a variant of their symplectic Khovanov cohomology group [18]. They also constructed a spectral sequence converging to the Heegaard Floer homology group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\rm HF}(\Sigma ({K}) \#(S^{2}\times S^{1}))$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E^{1}$</tex>-page isomorphic to a summand of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Kh_{\rm symp,inv}(K)$</tex>. A previous paper [19] showed that the higher pages of this spectral sequence are knot invariants. Here we discuss a reduced version of the spectral sequence which directly computes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\rm HF}(\Sigma ({K}))$</tex>. Under some degeneration conditions, one obtains a new absolute Maslov grading on the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\rm HF}(\Sigma ({K}))$</tex>. This occurs when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is a two-bridge knot, and we compute the grading in this case. We also extract some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>-valued knot invariants from this construction.

articleTitle: Visibility and Directions in Quasicrystals
abstract: It is well known that a positive proportion of all points in a d-dimensional lattice is visible from the origin, and that these visible lattice points have constant density in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^d$</tex>. In the present paper, we prove an analogous result for a large class of quasicrystals, including the vertex set of a Penrose tiling. We furthermore establish that the statistical properties of the directions of visible points are described by certain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {SL}(d,{\BBR})$</tex>-invariant point processes. Our results imply in particular existence and continuity of the gap distribution for directions in certain 2D cut-and-project sets. This answers some of the questions raised by Baake et al. [1].

articleTitle: Simultaneous Dense and Nondense Orbits and the Space of Lattices
abstract: We show that the set of points nondense under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times n$</tex>-map on the circle and dense for the geodesic flow after we identify the circle with a periodic horospherical orbit of the modular surface has full Haudorff dimension. We also show the analogous result for toral automorphisms on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-torus and a diagonal flow. Our results can be interpreted in number-theoretic terms: the set of well-approximable numbers that are nondense under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times n$</tex>-map has full Hausdorff dimension. Similarly, the set of well-approximable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-vectors that are nondense under a hyperbolic toral automorphism has full Hausdorff dimension. Our result for numbers is the counterpart to a classical result of Kaufmann.

articleTitle: Shilov Boundaries of the Pluricomplex Green Function's Level Sets
abstract: In this paper, we study a relation between the Shilov boundaries of the pluricomplex Green function's level sets and the supports of Monge–Ampère-type currents. We also study the set which intersects the support of any nonzero closed positive current by applying our main result.

articleTitle: Cones of Hilbert Functions
abstract: We study the closed convex hull of various collections of Hilbert functions. Working over a standard graded polynomial ring with modules that are generated in degree 0, we describe the supporting hyperplanes and extreme rays for the cones generated by the Hilbert functions of all modules, all modules with bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>-invariant, and all modules with bounded Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity. The first of these cones is infinite-dimensional and simplicial, the second is finite-dimensional but neither simplicial nor polyhedral, and the third is finite-dimensional and simplicial.

articleTitle: a-Points of the Riemann Zeta-Function on the Critical Line
abstract: We investigate the proportion of the nontrivial roots of the equation ζ(s)=a, which lie on the line <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur {R}\,} s={1 \over 2}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a \in {\BBC}$</tex> not equal to zero. We show that at most one-half of these points lie on the line <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur {R}} s= {1 \over 2}$</tex>. Moreover, assuming a spacing condition on the ordinates of zeros of the Riemann zeta-function, we prove that zero percent of the nontrivial solutions to ζ(s)=a lie on the line <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur {R}} s= {1 \over 2}$</tex> for any nonzero complex number a.

articleTitle: Nodal Sets of Random Eigenfunctions for the Isotropic Harmonic Oscillator
abstract: The expected hypersurface measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {H}^{d-1}(Z_{E,h} \cap B(r, x))$</tex> of nodal sets of random eigenfunctions of eigenvalue E of the semiclassical isotropic harmonic oscillator in balls <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(r, x) \subset {\BBR}^d$</tex> is determined as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h{\rightarrow } 0.$</tex> In the allowed region the volumes are of order h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, while in the forbidden region they are of order h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Proof of the Kawamata–Morrison Cone Conjecture for Holomorphic Symplectic Varieties of K3[n] or Generalized Kummer Deformation Type
abstract: We prove a version of the Kawamata–Morrison ample cone conjecture for projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds deformation equivalent to either the Hilbert scheme of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> points on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K3$</tex> surface or a generalized Kummer variety. The finiteness of the set of birational models of such varieties follows.

articleTitle: Derived Kan Extension for Strict Polynomial Functors
abstract: We investigate fundamental properties of adjoint functors to the precomposition functor in the category of strict polynomial functors. In particular, we obtain the proof of Touzé's Collapsing Conjecture on Ext-groups between twisted functors and refinement of a general program of computing Ext-groups between strict polynomial functors important in representation theory.

articleTitle: Finding Linear Patterns of Complexity One
abstract: We study the following generalization of Roth’s theorem for 3-term arithmetic progressions. For s≥2, define a nontrivial s-configuration to be a set of s(s+1)/2 integers consisting of s distinct integers x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> as well as the averages (x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>+x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>)/2 (1≤i<j≤s). Our main result states that if a set A⊂[N] has density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta \gg (\log N)^{-c(s)}$</tex> for some positive constant c(s)>0 depending on s, then A contains a nontrivial s-configuration. This improves on the previous bound of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta \gg (\log \log N)^{-c(s)}$</tex> due to Dousse [3]. We also deduce, as a corollary, an improvement of a problem involving sum-free subsets.

articleTitle: Schmidt’s Subspace Theorem with Moving Hypersurfaces
abstract: One of the most important developments in recent years in Diophantine approximation is the work of Corvaja, Zannier, Evertse, and Ferretti on extending Schmidt’s Subspace Theorem from hyperplanes to hypersurfaces. In this paper, we further extend their result to moving hypersurfaces.

articleTitle: Applications of p-Adic Analysis for Bounding Periods of Subvarieties Under Étale Maps
abstract: Using methods of p-adic analysis, we obtain effective bounds for the length of the orbit of a preperiodic subvariety Y ⊂X under the action of an étale endomorphism of X. As a corollary of our result, we obtain effective bounds for the size of torsion of any semiabelian variety over a finitely generated field of characteristic 0. Our method allows us to show that any finitely generated torsion subgroup of Aut(X) is finite. This yields a different proof of Burnside's problem for automorphisms of quasiprojective varieties X defined over a field of characteristic 0.

articleTitle: Hypergeometric Solutions to the Symmetric q-Painlevé Equations
abstract: We consider the symmetric q-Painlevé equations derived from the birational representation of affine Weyl groups by applying the projective reduction and construct the hypergeometric solutions. Moreover, we discuss continuous limits of the symmetric q-Painlevé equations to Painlevé equations together with their hypergeometric solutions.

articleTitle: Affine Cellularity of Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier Algebras of Finite Types
abstract: We prove that the Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier algebras R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> of finite type are (graded) affine cellular in the sense of Koenig and Xi. In fact, we establish a stronger property, namely that the affine cell ideals in R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> are generated by idempotents. This, in particular, implies the (known) result that the global dimension of R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> is finite.

articleTitle: The Sup-Norm Problem for PGL(4)
abstract: Let F be an L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-normalized Hecke–Maaß cusp form for the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma = {\rm SL}_{4}({\BBZ})$</tex> with Laplace eigenvalue λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>. Assume that F satisfies the Ramanujan conjecture at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex> (this is satisfied by almost all cusp forms). If Ω is a compact subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \backslash \cal {H}_4$</tex>, we show the bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\| F|_{\Omega }\|_{\infty } \ll \lambda _F^{3/2 - \delta }$</tex> for some absolute constant δ>0.

articleTitle: On Distribution of Poles of Eisenstein Series and the Length Spectrum of Hyperbolic Manifolds
abstract: We extend results of Bhagwat and Rajan on a strong multiplicity one property for length spectrum to hyperbolic manifolds with cusps, showing that for two even dimensional hyperbolic manifolds of finite volume, if all but finitely many closed geodesics have the same length, then all closed geodesics have the same length. When the set of exceptional lengths is infinite, but sufficiently sparse, we can show that the two manifolds must have the same volume, and in low dimensions also the same number of cusps. A main ingredient in our proof is a generalization of a result of Selberg on the distribution of poles of Eisenstein series to hyperbolic manifolds.

articleTitle: Gerstenhaber and Batalin–Vilkovisky Structures on Modules over Operads
abstract: In this article, we show under what additional ingredients a comp (or opposite) module over an operad with multiplication can be given the structure of a cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-module and how the underlying simplicial homology gives rise to a Batalin–Vilkovisky module over the cohomology of the operad. In particular, one obtains a generalized Lie derivative and a generalized (cyclic) cap product that obey a Cartan–Rinehart homotopy formula, and hence yield the structure of a noncommutative differential calculus in the sense of Nest, Tamarkin, Tsygan, and others. Examples include the calculi known for the Hochschild theory of associative algebras, for Poisson structures, but above all the calculus for general left Hopf algebroids with respect to general coefficients (in which the classical calculus of vector fields and differential forms is contained).

articleTitle: Attaining Potentially Good Reduction in Arithmetic Dynamics
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a nonarchimedean field, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi \in K(z)$</tex> be a rational function of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 2$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> has potentially good reduction, we give an upper bound, depending only on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>, for the minimal degree of an extension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L/K$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> is conjugate over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> to a map of good reduction. In particular, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=2$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is less than the residue characteristic of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>, the bound is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d+1$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is discretely valued, we give examples to show that our bound is sharp.

articleTitle: On Isometric Embeddings into Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
abstract: We show that any metric on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^2$</tex> with Gauss curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K \geq -\kappa$</tex> admits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{1,a}$</tex>-isometric embedding into the hyperbolic space with sectional curvature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\kappa$</tex>. We also give a sufficient condition for a metric on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^2$</tex> to be isometrically embedded into anti-de Sitter spacetime with the prescribed cosmological time function.

articleTitle: On Integrable Generalizations of the Pentagram Map
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the generalization to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBRP}^n$</tex> of the pentagram map defined in [4] is invariant under certain scalings for any n. This property allows the definition of a Lax representation for the map and establishes its integrability.

articleTitle: The Arithmetic Tutte Polynomials of the Classical Root Systems
abstract: Many combinatorial and topological invariants of a hyperplane arrangement can be computed in terms of its Tutte polynomial. Similarly, many invariants of a toric arrangement can be computed in terms of its arithmetic Tutte polynomial. We compute the arithmetic Tutte polynomials of the classical root systems A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>,B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>,C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> with respect to their integer, root, and weight lattices. We do it in two ways: by introducing a finite field method for arithmetic Tutte polynomials and by enumerating signed graphs with respect to six parameters.

articleTitle: Stability Estimates for an Inverse Problem for the Magnetic Schrödinger Operator
abstract: In this paper, we prove stable determination of an inverse boundary value problem associated to a magnetic Schrödinger operator assuming that the magnetic and electric potentials are essentially bounded and the magnetic potentials admit a Hölder-type modulus of continuity in the sense of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Semi-Terminal Modifications of Demi-Normal Pairs
abstract: For a quasi-projective demi-normal pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X, \Delta )$</tex>, we prove that there exist a semi-canonical modification and a semi-terminal modification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X, \Delta )$</tex>.

articleTitle: An Inverse Problem for Self-adjoint Positive Hankel Operators
abstract: For a sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\alpha _n\}_{n=0}^\infty $</tex>, we consider the Hankel operator Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf>, realized as the infinite matrix in ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with the entries α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+m</inf>. We consider the subclass of bounded Hankel operators defined by the “double positivity” condition Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf>≥0, Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S*α</inf>≥0; here S*α is the shifted sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\alpha _{n+1}\}_{n=0}^\infty $</tex>. We prove that in this class, the sequence α is uniquely determined by the spectral shift function ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> for the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _{\alpha }^2$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma _{S^*\alpha }^2$</tex>. We also describe the class of all functions ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> arising in this way and prove that the map α↦ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> is a homeomorphism in appropriate topologies.

articleTitle: Variation of the Canonical Height for Polynomials in Several Variables
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a number field, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X/K$</tex> be a curve, let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_t:{\BBP}^N\to {\BBP}^N$</tex> be a family of morphisms over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P:X\to {\BBP}^N$</tex> be a morphism. Writing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat {h}_{f_t}$</tex> for the canonical height associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_t$</tex>, it follows from a result of Call and Silverman that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat {h}_{f_t}(P_t)/h_X(t)=\hat {h}_{f_\eta }(P_\eta )+o(1)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta $</tex> is the generic point of the curve. Assuming that there is a hyperplane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\eta ^*H=dH$</tex>, and such that the restriction of the family to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> is isotrivial, we improve this estimate to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\hat{h}_{f_t}(P_t)=\hat{h}_{f_\eta}(P_\eta)h_X(t)+O(1),$$</tex> for a particular Weil height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. In the one-variable case, this reduces to an earlier result of Ingram.

articleTitle: Noncollapsing of Curve-Shortening Flow in Surfaces
abstract: We prove that curve-shortening flow in a surface stays noncollapsed for finite time, in the sense of Huisken's distance comparison principle [3]. This gives an easier proof of [2] that any finite time singularity of curve-shortening flow in a compact surface will be a round point.

articleTitle: A Note on Riemann Hypothesis for Curves and Hypersurfaces Over Finite Fields
abstract: We give what is arguably a simple (though certainly not elementary, cf. [12]) proof of the Riemann Hypothesis for (projective, smooth, geometrically connected) curves and hypersurfaces over finite fields, by an argument which reduces us to checking a few examples.

articleTitle: Hochschild Cohomology with Support
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the functoriality properties of map-graded Hochschild complexes. We show that the category Map of map-graded categories is naturally a stack over the category of small categories endowed with a certain Grothendieck topology of 3-covers. For a related topology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\infty $</tex>-covers on the Cartesian morphisms in Map, we prove that taking map-graded Hochschild complexes defines a sheaf. From the functoriality related to “injections” between map-graded categories, we obtain Hochschild complexes “with support”. We revisit Keller's arrow category argument from this perspective, and introduce and investigate a general Grothendieck construction which encompasses both the map-graded categories associated to presheaves of algebras and certain generalized arrow categories, which together constitute a pair of complementary tools for deconstructing Hochschild complexes.

articleTitle: Degenerate Flag Varieties of Type A and C are Schubert Varieties
abstract: We show that any type A or C degenerate flag variety is, in fact, isomorphic to a Schubert variety in an appropriate partial flag manifold.

articleTitle: Weyl Modules for the Hyperspecial Current Algebra
abstract: We develop the theory of global and local Weyl modules for the hyperspecial current algebra of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{2n}^{(2)}$</tex>. We prove that the dimension of a local Weyl module depends only on its highest weight, thus establishing a freeness result for global Weyl modules. Furthermore, we show that the graded local Weyl modules are level one Demazure modules for the corresponding affine Lie algebra. In the last section, we derive the same results for the special current algebras of the twisted affine Lie algebras not of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{2n}^{(2)}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Algebraic Values of Certain Analytic Functions
abstract: Building on recent work of Masser concerning algebraic values of the Riemann zeta function, we prove two general results about the scarcity of algebraic points on the graphs of certain restrictions of certain analytic functions. For any of the graphs to which our results apply and any positive integer d, we show that there are at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C(\log H)^{3+\varepsilon}$</tex> algebraic points of degree at most d and multiplicative height at most H on that graph. In particular, we obtain this conclusion for any restriction of Γ(z) or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac {\zeta(z)}{\pi^2}$</tex> to a compact disk, answering questions from Masser's paper, the latter having been suggested by Pila. As in Masser's original work, the constant C may be effectively computed from certain data associated with the function in question.

articleTitle: Canonical Cohen Rings for Norm Fields
abstract: Fix K/Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> a finite extension and let L/K be an infinite, strictly arithmetically profinite extension in the sense of Fontaine–Wintenberger [24]. Let X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(L) denote its associated norm field. The goal of this paper is to associate to L/K, in a canonical and functorial way, a p-adically complete subring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf A}_{L/K}^+ \subset \widetilde {{\bf A}}^+$</tex> whose reduction modulo p is contained in the valuation ring of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(L). When the extension L/K is of a special form, which we call a φ-iterate extension, we prove that X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(L) is (at worst) a finite purely inseparable extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {Frac}} ({\bf A}_{L/K}^+/p{\bf A}_{L/K}^+)$</tex>. The class of φ-iterate extensions includes all Lubin–Tate extensions, as well as many other extensions such as the non-Galois “Kummer” extension occurring in the work of Faltings, Breuil, and Kisin. In particular, our work provides a canonical and functorial construction of every characteristic zero lift of the norm fields that have thus far played a foundational role in (integral) p-adic Hodge theory, as well as many other cases which have yet to be studied.

articleTitle: Logarithmic Time Decay for the Cubic Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations
abstract: We prove global existence of solutions to the Cauchy problem for the 1D cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${\rm i}u_{t}+{1 \over 2}u_{xx}=\lambda\,{\rm e}^{{\rm i} {\pi \over 2}}u^{3}+\vert u\vert^{2}u,\quad x\in {\bf R},\ t \gt 1, \qquad \quad {(0.1)}$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \in {\bf R},\ 0 \lt \vert \lambda \vert \lt \sqrt {3}$</tex>. We show that the time decay estimate of the solution in the far region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert x\vert \gt \sqrt {t}$</tex> coincides with that for the linear case, whereas in the short-range region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert x\vert \leq \sqrt {t}$</tex> the solution obtains an extra logarithmic time decay, which is less than that in the absence of the resonance term |u|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>u in Equation (0.1).

articleTitle: On the Number of Zeros of Linear Combinations of Independent Characteristic Polynomials of Random Unitary Matrices
abstract: We show that for any linear combination of characteristic polynomials of independent random unitary matrices with the same determinant, the expected proportion of zeros lying on the unit circle tends to 1 as the dimension of the matrices tends to infinity. This result is the random matrix analog of an earlier result by Bombieri and Hejhal on the distribution of zeros of linear combinations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions, and thus is consistent with the conjectured links between the value distribution of the characteristic polynomial of random unitary matrices and the value distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions on the critical line.

articleTitle: Sharp Global Regularity for the 2 + 1-Dimensional Equivariant Faddeev Model
abstract: The aim of this article is to prove that for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2+1$</tex>-dimensional equivariant Faddeev model, which is a quasilinear generalization of the corresponding nonlinear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> model, small initial data in critical Besov spaces evolve into global solutions which scatter.

articleTitle: Factorization of Anticanonical Maps of Fano Type Variety
abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to generalize Sakai's work on anticanonical models of rational surfaces to varieties of Fano type. We first prove a characterization of Fano Type Variety using the singularities of anticanonical models. Secondly, we study the decomposition of the anticanonical map using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_X$</tex>-minimal model program.

articleTitle: On the Galois Structure of Selmer Groups
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> be an abelian variety defined over a number field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> a finite Galois extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be a prime number. Then under certain not-too-stringent conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F,$</tex> we investigate the explicit Galois structure of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-primary Selmer group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. We also use the results so obtained to derive new bounds on the growth of the Selmer rank of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> over extensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>.

articleTitle: Artin L-Functions on Finite Quotients of PGL3
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{{\Gamma }}$</tex> be a finite 2D complex arising from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm PGL}}_3$</tex>. In this paper, we study Artin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions attached to finite-dimensional representations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex> of the fundamental group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{{\Gamma }}$</tex>. Some key properties, including rationality, functional equation, and invariance under induction, of these functions are proved. Moreover, using a cohomological argument, we establish a connection between the Artin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho$</tex>, generalizing the identity on zeta functions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_{{\Gamma }}$</tex> obtained in [9, 10].

articleTitle: Two-Parameter Quantum Algebras, Canonical Bases, and Categorifications
abstract: A theory of canonical basis for a two-parameter quantum algebra is developed in parallel with the one in one-parameter case. A geometric construction of the negative part of a two-parameter quantum algebra is given by using mixed perverse sheaves and Deligne's weight theory based on Lusztig's work [28]. A categorification of the negative part of a two-parameter quantum algebra is provided. A two-parameter quantum algebra is shown to be a two-cocycle deformation, depending only on the second parameter, of its one-parameter analog.

articleTitle: Jacquet Functor and De Concini–Procesi Compactification
abstract: We give a geometric realization of the Jacquet functor using a deformation of De Concini–Procesi compactification.

articleTitle: Reduction of τ-Tilting Modules and Torsion Pairs
abstract: The class of support <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-tilting modules was introduced recently by Adachi et al. These modules complete the class of tilting modules from the point of view of mutations. Given a finite-dimensional algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, we study all basic support <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-tilting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>-modules which have a given basic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-rigid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>-module as a direct summand. We show that there exist an algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> such that there exists an order-preserving bijection between these modules and all basic support <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-tilting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>-modules; we call this passage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-tilting reduction. An important step in our proof is the formation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-perpendicular categories which are analogs of ordinary perpendicular categories. Finally, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>-tilting reduction is compatible with silting reduction and 2-Calabi–Yau reduction in appropriate triangulated categories.

articleTitle: Beauville–Voisin Conjecture for Generalized Kummer Varieties
abstract: Inspired by their results on the Chow rings of projective K3 surfaces, Beauville and Voisin made the following conjecture: given a projective hyperkähler manifold, for any algebraic cycle that is a polynomial with rational coefficients of Chern classes of the tangent bundle and line bundles, it is rationally equivalent to zero if and only if it is numerically equivalent to zero. In this paper, we prove the Beauville–Voisin conjecture for generalized Kummer varieties.

articleTitle: On Hodge Numbers of Complete Intersections and Landau–Ginzburg Models
abstract: We prove that the Hodge number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{1,N-1}(X)$</tex> of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-dimensional (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\geqslant 3$</tex>) Fano complete intersection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is less by one then the number of irreducible components of the central fiber of (any) Calabi–Yau compactification of Givental's Landau–Ginzburg model for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: Stable CMC and Index One Minimal Surfaces in Conformally Flat Manifolds
abstract: Let M be a Riemannian three-manifold of nonnegative Ricci curvature, Ric ≥0. Suppose that M is conformally flat and simply connected or more generally that it admits a conformal immersion into the standard 3-sphere. Let Σ be a compact connected and orientable surface immersed in M which is a stable constant mean curvature (CMC) surface or an index one minimal surface. We prove that Σ is homeomorphic either to a sphere or to a torus. Moreover, in case Σ is homeomorphic to a torus, then it is embedded, minimal, conformal to a flat square torus and Ric(N)=0, where N is a unit field normal to Σ. The result is sharp, we can perturb the standard metric on the 3-sphere in its conformal class to obtain metrics of nonnegative Ricci curvature admitting minimal tori of index one and which are stable as CMC surfaces.As a consequence, in any 3-sphere of positive Ricci curvature which is conformally flat, the isoperimetric domains are topologically 3-balls. This proves a special case of a conjecture of Ros [11, 12].

articleTitle: Local Brunella's Alternative I. RICH Foliations
