abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the structure of codimension 1 singular holomorphic foliations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^3,0$</tex> without invariant germs of analytic surface. We focus on the so-called CH-foliations, that is, foliations without saddle nodes in 2D sections. Considering a reduction of singularities, we detect the possible existence of “nodal components”, which are a higher-dimensional version of the nodal separators in dimension 2. If the foliation is without nodal components, we prove that all the leaves in a neighborhood of the origin contain at least one germ of analytic curve at the origin. We also study the structure of nodal components for the case of “Relatively Isolated CH-foliations” and we show that they cut the dicritical components or they exit the origin through a noncompact invariant curve. This allows us to give a precise statement of a local version of Brunella's alternative: if we do not have an invariant surface, all the leaves contain a germ of analytic curve or it is possible to detect the nodal components in the generic points of the singular curves before doing the reduction of singularities.

articleTitle: A Mean Curvature Type Flow in Space Forms
abstract: In this article, we introduce a new type of mean curvature flow (1.3) for bounded star-shaped domains in space forms and prove its longtime existence, exponential convergence without any curvature assumption. Along this flow, the enclosed volume is a constant and the surface area evolves monotonically. Moreover, for a bounded convex domain in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^{n+1}$</tex>, the quermassintegrals evolve monotonically along the flow which allows us to prove a class of Alexandrov–Fenchel inequalities of quermassintegrals.

articleTitle: Rigidity in the Invariant Theory of Compact Lie Groups
abstract: A compact Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> and a faithful complex representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> determine the Sato–Tate measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu _{G,V}$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}$</tex>, defined as the direct image of Haar measure with respect to the character map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\mapsto {\rm tr}(g\mid V)$</tex>. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for a Sato–Tate measure to be an isolated point in the set of all Sato–Tate measures, endowed with the topology defined by moments. In particular, we prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is connected and semisimple and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> is irreducible, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu _{G,V}$</tex> is an isolated point.

articleTitle: On the Knot Floer Homology of Twisted Torus Knots
abstract: In this paper, we study the knot Floer homology of a subfamily of twisted (p,q) torus knots where q≡±1 (mod p). Specifically, we classify the knots in this subfamily that admit L-space surgeries. To do calculations, we use the fact that these knots are (1,1) knots and, therefore, admit a genus one Heegaard diagram.

articleTitle: Rational Homology Spheres as Universal Abelian Covers
abstract: Rational homology sphere graph manifolds play an important role in singularity theory. They occur as the links, and hence determine the topology, of many interesting types of surface singularities. These include all rational and splice quotient singularities. It is known that the splice diagram of a rational homology sphere graph manifold determines the universal abelian cover of the manifold. In this article, we give a condition on the splice diagram to determine when the universal abelian cover itself is a rational homology sphere.

articleTitle: Building Meromorphic Solutions of q-Difference Equations Using a Borel–Laplace Summation
abstract: After introducing q-analogs of the Borel and Laplace transformations, we prove that to every formal power series solution of a linear q-difference equation with rational coefficients, we may apply several q-Borel and Laplace transformations of convenient orders and convenient direction in order to construct a solution of the same equation that is meromorphic on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^{*}$</tex>. We use this theorem to construct explicitly an invertible matrix solution of a linear q-difference system with rational coefficients, of which entries are meromorphic on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^{*}$</tex>. Moreover, when the system has two slopes and is put in the Birkhoff–Guenther normal form, we show how the solutions we compute are related to the one constructed by Ramis et al. [27].

articleTitle: H∞ Functional Calculus and Maximal Inequalities for Semigroups of Contractions on Vector-Valued Lp-Spaces
abstract: Let {T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t>0</inf> be a strongly continuous semigroup of positive contractions on L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(X,μ) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \lt p \lt \infty $</tex>. Let E be a unconditional martingale differences (UMD) Banach lattice of measurable functions on another measure space (Ω,ν). For f∈L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(X;E), define <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\cal{M}(f)(x, \omega)=\sup_{t \gt 0} {1 \over t}\left|\int_0^tT_s(f(\cdot,\omega))(x)\,{\rm d}s\right|,\quad (x,\omega)\in X\times\Omega.$$</tex> Then the following maximal ergodic inequality holds: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\|\cal{M}(f)\|_{L_p(X; E)}\lesssim \|f\|_{L_p(X; E)},\quad f\in L_p(X; E).$$</tex> If the semigroup {T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t>0</inf> is additionally assumed to be analytic, then {T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t>0</inf> extends to an analytic semigroup on L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(X;E) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {M}(f)$</tex> in the above inequality can be replaced by the following sectorial maximal function. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\cal{T}_\theta(f)(x, \omega)=\sup_{|{\rm arg}(z)| \lt \theta}|T_z(f(\cdot,\omega))(x)|$$</tex> for some θ>0.Under the latter analyticity assumption and if E is a complex interpolation space between a Hilbert space and a UMD Banach space, then {T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>}<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t>0</inf> extends to an analytic semigroup on L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>(X;E) and its negative generator has a bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^\infty (\Sigma _\sigma)$</tex> calculus for some σ<π/2.

articleTitle: Logarithmic Bounds for Translation-Invariant Equations in Squares
abstract: We show that the equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _1 n_1^2 + \cdots + \lambda _s n_s^2 = 0$</tex> admits nontrivial solutions in any subset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[N]$</tex> of density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\log N)^{-c_s}$</tex>, provided that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \geq 7$</tex> and the coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda _i \in {\BBZ} \smallsetminus \{0\}$</tex> sum to zero and satisfy certain sign conditions. This improves upon previous known density bounds of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\log \log N)^{-c}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Quasiprojective Three-Manifold Groups and Complexification of Three-Manifolds
abstract: We characterize the quasiprojective groups that appear as fundamental groups of compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifolds (with or without boundary). We also characterize all closed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>-manifolds that admit good complexifications. These answer questions of Friedl and Suciu [18] and Totaro [34].

articleTitle: DT-Invariants of Quivers and the Steinberg Character of GLn
abstract: In this paper, we give a simple description of Donaldson-Thomas (DT)-invariants of double quivers without potential as the multiplicity of the Steinberg character in some representation associated with the quiver. When the dimension vector is indivisible, we use this description to express these DT-invariants as the Poincaré polynomial of some singular quiver varieties. Finally, we explain the connections with [6] where DT-invariants are expressed as the graded multiplicities of the trivial representation of some Weyl group in the cohomology of some nonsingular quiver varieties attached to an extended quiver.

articleTitle: On Complexified Analytic Hamiltonian Flows and Geodesics on the Space of Kähler Metrics
abstract: For a compact real analytic symplectic manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,\omega ),$</tex> we describe an approach to the complexification of Hamiltonian flows [5, 30, 33] and corresponding geodesics on the space of Kähler metrics. In this approach, motivated by recent work on quantization, the complexified Hamiltonian flows act, through the Gröbner theory of Lie series, on the sheaf of complex-valued real analytic functions, changing the sheaves of holomorphic functions. This defines an action on the space of (equivalent) complex structures on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and also a direct action on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. This description is related to the approach of [3] where one has an action on a complexification <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{{\BBC}}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> followed by projection to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. Our approach allows for the study of some Hamiltonian functions which are not real analytic. It also leads naturally to the consideration of continuous degenerations of diffeomorphisms and of Kähler structures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>. Hence, one can link continuously (geometric quantization) real, and more general non-Kähler, polarizations with Kähler polarizations. This corresponds to the extension of the geodesics to the boundary of the space of Kähler metrics. Three illustrative examples are considered. We find an explicit formula for the complex time evolution of the Kähler potential under the flow. For integral symplectic forms, this formula corresponds to the complexification of the prequantization of Hamiltonian symplectomorphisms. We verify that certain families of Kähler structures, which have been studied in geometric quantization, are geodesic families.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Gradient Ricci Solitons Revisited
abstract: In this note, we complete the classification of the geometry of noncompact 2D gradient Ricci solitons. As a consequence, we obtain two corollaries: First, a complete 2D gradient Ricci soliton has bounded curvature. Secondly, we give examples of complete 2D expanding Ricci solitons with negative curvature that are topologically disks and are not isometric to hyperbolic space.

articleTitle: The Affine Sieve Beyond Expansion I: Thin Hypotenuses
abstract: We study an instance of the Affine Sieve, producing a level of distribution beyond that which can be obtained from current techniques, even assuming a Selberg/Ramanujan-type spectral gap. In particular, we consider the set of hypotenuses in a thin orbit of Pythagorean triples. Previous work [13, 14, 16] gave an exponent of distribution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \lt {1 \over 12}$</tex> coming from Gamburd's [10] gap <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta ={5 \over 6}$</tex>, thereby producing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=13$</tex> almost primes in this linear sieve problem (see Section 1 for definitions). If conditioned on a best possible gap <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta ={1 \over 2}$</tex>, the known method would give an exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \lt {1 \over 4}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=5$</tex> almost primes. The exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over 4}$</tex> is the natural analog of the “Bombieri–Vinogradov” range of distribution for this problem, see Remark 1.19.In this paper, we unconditionally prove the exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \lt 7/24$</tex> (in the “beyond-Bombieri–Vinogradov” range), thereby producing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=4$</tex> almost primes. The main tools involve developing bilinear forms and the dispersion method in the range of incomplete sums for this Affine Sieve problem.

articleTitle: Lyapunov Exponent and Harmonic Measure on the Boundary of the Connectedness Locus
abstract: For almost all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c\in \partial {\cal M}_{d}$</tex> in the sense of the harmonic measure the Lyapunov exponent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> under iterates of the unicritical polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^{d}+c$</tex> is equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log d$</tex>. The result quantifies the lower estimates of [4, 7]. Even though the theorem originates from ergodic theory, a short proof is based on quasiconformal and geometric analysis.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily Long Factorizations in Mapping Class Groups
abstract: On a compact oriented surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 1$</tex> boundary components, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta _1, \delta _2,\ldots , \delta _n$</tex>, we consider positive factorizations of the boundary multitwist <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\delta _1} t_{\delta _2} \cdots t_{\delta _n}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\delta _i}$</tex> is the positive Dehn twist about the boundary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta _i$</tex>. We prove that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\geq 3$</tex>, the boundary multitwist <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\delta _1} t_{\delta _2}$</tex> can be written as a product of arbitrarily large number of positive Dehn twists about nonseparating simple closed curves, extending a recent result of Baykur and Van Horn-Morris, who proved this result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\geq 8$</tex>. This fact has immediate corollaries on the Euler characteristics of the Stein fillings of contact three manifolds.

articleTitle: Presenting Queer Schur Superalgebras
abstract: Associated to the two types of finite-dimensional simple superalgebras, there are the general linear Lie superalgebra and the queer Lie superalgebra. The universal enveloping algebras of these Lie superalgebras act on the tensor spaces of the natural representations and, thus, define certain finite-dimensional quotients, the Schur superalgebras, and the queer Schur superalgebra. In this paper, we introduce the quantum analog of the queer Schur superalgebra and investigate the presentation problem for both the queer Schur superalgebra and its quantum analog.

articleTitle: On Algebraic Equivalences Among the Twenty-Seven Abel-Prym Curves on a Generic Abelian Five-Fold
abstract: This article shows that on a generic principally polarized abelian variety of dimension 5 the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}$</tex>-vector space spanned by the classes of the twenty-seven Abel-Prym curves modulo algebraic equivalence has dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7$</tex>.

articleTitle: Riemannian Curl in Contact Geometry
abstract: We consider a contact manifold with a pseudo-Riemannian metric and define a contact vector field associated with this pair of structures. We call this new differential invariant the contact Riemannian curl. We show that the contact Riemannian curl vanishes if the metric is of constant curvature and the contact structure is defined by a Killing 1-form. We also show that the contact Riemannian curl has a strong similarity with the Schwarzian derivative, since it depends only on the projective equivalence class of the metric. The subsymbol of the Laplace–Beltrami operator corresponding to a metric on a contact manifold is proportional to the contact Riemannian curl. We also show that the contact Riemannian curl vanishes on the spherical (co)tangent bundle over a Riemannian manifold.

articleTitle: Equidistribution of Frobenius Eigenvalues
abstract: We study the problem of variation of Frobenius eigenvalues on the cohomology of families of local systems of algebraic curves over finite fields.

articleTitle: Poisson Reduction of the Space of Polygons
abstract:
A Poisson structure is defined on the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {W}}$</tex> of twisted polygons in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}^{
u }$</tex>. Poisson reductions with respect to two Poisson group actions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {W}}$</tex> are described. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u =2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u =3$</tex> cases are discussed in detail. Amongst the Poisson structures arising in examples are to be found the lattice Virasoro structure, the second Toda lattice structure, and some extended Toda lattice structures. It is shown that, in general, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u$</tex>, the reduction procedure gives rise to a family of bi-Hamiltonian structures on the reduced space.

articleTitle: Anti De Sitter Deformation of Quaternionic Analysis and the Second-Order Pole
abstract: This is a continuation of a series of papers [2–4], where we develop quaternionic analysis from the point of view of representation theory of the conformal Lie group and its Lie algebra. In this paper, we continue to study the quaternionic analogs of Cauchy's formula for the second-order pole. These quaternionic analogs are closely related to regularization of infinities of vacuum polarization diagrams in 4D quantum field theory. To add some flexibility, especially when dealing with Cauchy's formula for the second-order pole, we introduce a one-parameter deformation of quaternionic analysis. This deformation of quaternions preserves conformal invariance and has a geometric realization as anti de Sitter space sitting inside the 5D Euclidean space. We show that many results of quaternionic analysis—including the Cauchy–Fueter formula—admit a simple and canonical deformation. We conclude this paper with a deformation of the quaternionic analogs of Cauchy's formula for the second-order pole.

articleTitle: Vanishing of Certain Equivariant Distributions on p-Adic Spherical Spaces, and Nonvanishing of Spherical Bessel Functions
abstract: We prove vanishing of distribution on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic spherical spaces that are equivariant with respect to a generic character of the nilradical of a Borel subgroup and satisfy a certain condition on the wave-front set. We deduce from this nonvanishing of spherical Bessel functions for Galois symmetric pairs.

articleTitle: Nonexistence of Shrinkers for the Harmonic Map Flow in Higher Dimensions
abstract: We prove that the harmonic map flow from the Euclidean space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^d$</tex> into the sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^d$</tex> has no equivariant self-similar shrinking solutions in dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 7$</tex>.

articleTitle: On Brendle’s Estimate for the Inscribed Radius Under Mean Curvature Flow
abstract: In a recent paper [3], Brendle proved that the inscribed radius of closed embedded mean convex hypersurfaces moving by mean curvature flow is at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over (1+\delta)H}$</tex> at all points with H≥C(δ,M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). In this note, we give a shorter proof of Brendle’s estimate, and of a more general result for α-Andrews flows, based on our recent estimates from Haslhofer and Kleiner [4].

articleTitle: Hua-Type Beta-Integrals and Projective Systems of Measures on Flag Spaces
abstract: We construct a family of measures on flag spaces (or, equivalently, on the spaces of upper-triangular matrices) compatible with respect to natural projections. We obtain an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n(n-1)/2$</tex>-parametric family of beta-integrals over space of upper-triangular matrices of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>.

articleTitle: ᵶ-Stability and Finite-Dimensional Tracial Boundaries
abstract: We show that a simple separable unital nuclear nonelementary C*-algebra whose tracial state space has a compact extreme boundary with finite covering dimension admits uniformly tracially large order zero maps from matrix algebras into its central sequence algebra. As a consequence, strict comparison implies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {Z}$</tex>-stability for these algebras.

articleTitle: Quasi-Ordinary Singularities: Tree Model, Discriminant, and Irreducibility
abstract: Let f(Y)∈K[[X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>]][Y ] be a quasi-ordinary Weierstrass polynomial with coefficients in the ring of formal power series over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. In this paper, we study the discriminant D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> of f(Y)−V, where V is a new variable. We show that the Newton polytope of D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> depends only on contacts between the roots of f(Y). Then, we prove that f(Y) is irreducible if and only if the Newton polytope of D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> satisfies some arithmetic conditions. Finally, we generalize these results to quasi-ordinary power series.

articleTitle: Uniqueness of Rankin–Selberg Periods
abstract: Let k be a local field of characteristic zero. Rankin–Selberg’s local zeta integrals produce linear functionals on generic irreducible admissible smooth representations of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(k)×GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>(k), with certain invariance properties. We show that up to scalar multiplication, these linear functionals are determined by the invariance properties.

articleTitle: Radial Part Calculations for $\widehat {\Fraktur {sl}}_2$ and the Heun-KZB Heat Equation
abstract: In the present paper, we determine the radial part of the Casimir element for the affine Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat {\Fraktur {sl}}_2$</tex> with respect to the Chevalley involution. The resulting operator is identified with a blend of the Inozemtsev Hamiltonian and the KZB heat equation in dimension one. Moreover, it is shown how the corresponding zonal spherical functions give rise to symmetric theta functions and convergence is discussed. The paper takes guidance from previous work by Etingof and Kirillov on the diagonal case. Communicated by Prof. Eric Opdam

articleTitle: Moment-Angle Manifolds and Panov's Problem
abstract: We answer a problem posed by Panov, which is to describe the relationship between the wedge summands in a homotopy decomposition of the moment-angle complex corresponding to a disjoint union of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> points and the connected sum factors in a diffeomorphism decomposition of the moment-angle manifold corresponding to the simple polytope obtained by making <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> vertex cuts on a standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-simplex. This establishes a bridge between two very different approaches to moment-angle manifolds.

articleTitle: Logarithmic-Scale Quasimodes that do not Equidistribute
abstract: Given any compact hyperbolic surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, and a closed geodesic on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, we construct of a sequence of quasimodes on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> whose microlocal lifts concentrate positive mass on the geodesic. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) property does not hold for these quasimodes. This is analogous to a construction of Faure-Nonnenmacher-De Bièvre in the context of quantized cat maps and lends credence to the suggestion that large multiplicities play a role in the known failure of QUE for certain “toy models” of quantum chaos. We moreover conjecture a precise threshold for the order of quasimodes needed for QUE to hold— the result of the present paper shows that this conjecture, if true, is sharp.

articleTitle: On Dual F-Signature
abstract: We define the dual F-signature of modules, which is equivalent to the F-signature if the module is the base ring. By using this invariant, we give characterizations of regular, F-regular, F-rational, and Gorenstein singularities.

articleTitle: Small Points and Free Abelian Groups
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> be an algebraic extension of the rational numbers and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> an elliptic curve defined over some number field contained in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. The absolute logarithmic Weil height, respectively, the Néron–Tate height, induces a norm on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F^\ast $</tex> modulo torsion, respectively, on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E(F)$</tex> modulo torsion. The groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F^\ast $</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E(F)$</tex> are free abelian modulo torsion if the height function does not attain arbitrarily small positive values. In this paper, we prove the failure of the converse to this statement by explicitly constructing counterexamples.

articleTitle: Genera of Curves on a Very General Surface in ℙ3
abstract: In this paper, we consider the question of determining the geometric genera of irreducible curves lying on a very general surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geqslant 5$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^3$</tex> (the cases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\leqslant 4$</tex> are well known). For any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geqslant 4,$</tex> we introduce the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}(d)$</tex> of all non-negative integers which are not realized as geometric genera of irreducible curves on a very general surface of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^3$</tex>. We prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}(d)$</tex> is finite and, in particular, that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}(5)= \{0,1,2\}$</tex>. The set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}(d)$</tex> is the union of finitely many disjoint and separated integer intervals. The first of them, according to a theorem of Xu, is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}_0(d) := [0,{d(d-3) \over 2} - 3]$</tex>. We show that the next one is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Gaps}_1(d) := [{d^2-3d+4 \over 2}, d^2 - 2d - 9]$</tex> for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geqslant 6$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Generalized Frankel Conjecture in Sasaki Geometry
abstract: We prove some structure results for transversely reducible Sasaki manifolds. In particular, we show a Sasaki manifold with positive Ricci curvature is transversely irreducible, and so join (product) construction cannot be generalized to irregular Sasaki–Einstein manifolds, as opposed to the quasi-regular case done by Wang–Ziller and Boyer–Galicki. As an application, we classify compact Sasaki manifolds with nonnegative transverse bisectional curvature, which can be viewed as the generalized Frankel conjecture in Sasaki geometry.

articleTitle: Generic Representations of Wild Quivers
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex> be a wild connected directed quiver. We show that any generic representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is the union of its subrepresentations of finite length that are regular. As a consequence, we see that the direct limit closure of the preprojective component does not contain any generic module.

articleTitle: Double Total Ramifications for Curves of Genus 2
abstract: Inside the moduli space of curves of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> with two marked points, we consider the loci of curves admitting a map to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^1$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> totally ramified over the two marked points, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d\geq 2$</tex>. Such loci have codimension two. We compute the class of their closures in the moduli space of stable curves. Several results will be deduced from this computation.

articleTitle: Nilpotent Completions of Groups, Grothendieck Pairs, and Four Problems of Baumslag
abstract: Two groups are said to have the same nilpotent genus if they have the same nilpotent quotients. We answer four questions of Baumslag concerning nilpotent completions. (i) There exists a pair of finitely generated, residually torsion-free nilpotent groups of the same nilpotent genus such that one is finitely presented and the other is not. (ii) There exists a pair of finitely presented, residually torsion-free nilpotent groups of the same nilpotent genus such that one has a solvable conjugacy problem and the other does not. (iii) There exists a pair of finitely generated, residually torsion-free nilpotent groups of the same nilpotent genus such that one has finitely generated second homology <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_2(-,{\BBZ})$</tex> and the other does not. (iv) A nontrivial normal subgroup of infinite index in a finitely generated parafree group cannot be finitely generated. In proving this last result, we establish that the first L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-Betti number of a finitely generated parafree group in the same nilpotent genus as a free group of rank r is r−1. It follows that the reduced C*-algebra of the group is simple if r≥2, and that a version of the Freiheitssatz holds for parafree groups.

articleTitle: Nonembeddability into a Fixed Sphere for a Family of Compact Real Algebraic Hypersurfaces
abstract: We construct a family of compact real algebraic strongly pseudoconvex hypersurfaces which cannot be embedded into any fixed sphere.

articleTitle: The Class of the Bielliptic Locus in Genus 3
abstract: Let the bielliptic locus be the closure in the moduli space of stable curves of the locus of smooth curves that are double covers of genus 1 curves. In this paper, we compute the class of the bielliptic locus in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {{\cal M}}_{3}$</tex> in terms of a standard basis of the rational Chow group of codimension-2 classes in the moduli space. Our method is to test the class on the hyperelliptic locus: this gives the desired result up to two free parameters, which are then determined by intersecting the locus with two surfaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {{\cal M}}_{3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Families of Lattice Polarized K3 Surfaces with Monodromy
abstract: We extend the notion of lattice polarization for K3 surfaces to families over a (not necessarily simply connected) base, in a way that gives control over the action of monodromy on the algebraic cycles, and discuss the uses of this new theory in the study of families of K3 surfaces admitting fibrewise symplectic automorphisms. We then give an application of these ideas to the study of Calabi-Yau three-folds admitting fibrations by lattice polarized K3 surfaces.

articleTitle: Disk Complexes and Genus Two Heegaard Splittings for NonPrime 3-Manifolds
abstract: Given a genus two Heegaard splitting for a nonprime 3-manifold, we define a special subcomplex of the disk complex for one of the handlebodies of the splitting, and then show that it is contractible. As applications, first we show that the complex of Haken spheres for the splitting is contractible, which refines the results of Lei and Lei-Zhang. Secondly, we classify all the genus two Heegaard splittings for nonprime 3-manifolds, which is a generalization of the result of Montesinos–Safont. Finally, we show that the mapping class group of the splitting, called the Goeritz group, is finitely presented by giving its explicit presentation.

articleTitle: On Ideals in the Enveloping Algebra of a Locally Simple Lie Algebra
abstract: We study (two-sided) ideals I in the enveloping algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {g}_{\infty }$</tex> obtained as the union (equivalently, direct limit) of an arbitrary chain of embeddings of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\Fraktur{g}_1 \rightarrow \Fraktur{g}_2 \rightarrow \cdots\rightarrow \Fraktur{g}_n \rightarrow \cdots $$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty } \dim \Fraktur {g}_n=\infty $</tex>. Our main result is an explicit description of the zero-sets of the corresponding graded ideals grI. We use this description and results of Zhilinskii to prove Baranov’s conjecture that, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {g}_{\infty }$</tex> is not diagonal in the sense of Baranov and Zhilinskii, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> has a single nonzero proper ideal: the augmentation ideal. Our study is based on a complete description of the radical Poisson ideals in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf S}^\cdot (\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> and their zero-sets. We then discuss in detail integrable ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex>. These are certain ideals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I\subset {U} (\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I\cap {U} (\Fraktur {g}_n)$</tex> is an intersection of ideals of finite codimension in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_n)$</tex> for any n≥1. We present a classification of prime integrable ideals based on work of Zhilinskii. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {g}_{\infty } \cong \Fraktur {sl}_{\infty }, \Fraktur {so}_{\infty }$</tex>, all zero-sets of radical Poisson ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf S}^\cdot (\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> arise from prime integrable ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {g}_{\infty } \cong \Fraktur {sp}_{\infty }$</tex> only “half” of the zero-sets of Poisson ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf S}^\cdot (\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex> arise from integrable ideals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${U}(\Fraktur {g}_{\infty })$</tex>.

articleTitle: Degrees of Self-Maps of Simply Connected Manifolds
abstract: An oriented compact closed manifold is called inflexible, if the set of mapping degrees ranging over all continuous self-maps is finite. Inflexible manifolds have gained importance in the theory of functorial semi-norms on homology. Although inflexibility is expected to be a generic property in large dimensions, not many simply connected examples are known. We show that from a certain dimension on there are infinitely many rational homotopy types of inflexible manifolds in each dimension. Besides, we prove flexibility for large classes of manifolds and, in particular, as a spin-off, for homogeneous spaces. This is an outcome of a lifting result which also permits to generalize a conjecture of Copeland–Shar to the “real world”. Moreover, we then provide examples of simply connected smooth compact closed manifolds in each dimension from dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$70$</tex> on which have the following properties: they do not admit any self-map that reverses orientation. (For this we consider the lack of orientation reversal in the strongest sense possible, i.e., we prove the nonexistence of any self-map of arbitrary negative mapping degree.) Moreover, the manifolds neither split as nontrivial Cartesian products nor as nontrivial connected sums.

articleTitle: Drinfeld Modules, Frobenius Endomorphisms, and CM-Liftings
abstract: We give a global description of the Frobenius elements in the division fields of Drinfeld modules of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>. We apply this description to derive a criterion for the splitting modulo primes of a class of nonsolvable polynomials, and to study the frequency with which the reductions of Drinfeld modules have small endomorphism rings. We also generalize some of these results to higher rank Drinfeld modules and prove CM-lifting theorems for Drinfeld modules.

articleTitle: Geodesic and Billiard Flows on Quadrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces: L–A Pairs and Chasles Theorem
abstract: In this article, we construct L–A representations of geodesic flows on quadrics and of billiard problems within ellipsoids in the pseudo-Euclidean spaces. A geometric interpretation of the integrability analogous to the classical Chasles theorem for symmetric ellipsoids is given. We also consider a generalization of the billiard within arbitrary quadric allowing virtual billiard reflections.

articleTitle: Strictly Amenable Representations of Reduced Group C* -Algebras
abstract: We show that a locally compact group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is amenable if and only if its reduced group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^* $</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*_r(G)$</tex> is nuclear and has a tracial state, which is also equivalent to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*_r(G)$</tex> having a special kind of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^* $</tex>-representation that we propose to call “strictly amenable representation”. Consequently, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is separable and connected, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is amenable if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*_r(G)$</tex> has a tracial state.

articleTitle: ADE Subalgebras of the Triplet Vertex Algebra W(p): E6, E7
abstract: It is the forth paper in a series devoted to the investigation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ADE$</tex> subalgebras of the triplet vertex algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)$</tex>. In this paper, we prove <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{2}$</tex>-cofiniteness of the invariant subalgebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)^{\Gamma }$</tex> and study their representations when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> is the tetrahedral group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> (of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_6$</tex>-type), or the octahedral group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O$</tex> (of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_7$</tex>-type). We give a list of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21p$</tex> irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)^{T}$</tex>-modules and a list of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$28p$</tex> irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)^{O}$</tex>-modules. The completeness of these two lists can be reduced to some conjectures about constant term identities which have been verified in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p=1$</tex>. For the proof of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{2}$</tex>-cofiniteness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)^{\Gamma }$</tex>, and the calculations of the Zhu's algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\cal {W}(p)^{\Gamma })$</tex>, we develop several quite universal formulas (Theorem 4.3 and its corollaries). In Appendix, we further apply them to derive a useful tool of structure coefficients for the triplet vertex algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)$</tex> and its irreducible modules, which unifies almost all the calculations in this paper; as an unexpected byproduct, we give a new proof of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur {sl}_{2}$</tex>-action on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal {W}(p)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Combinatorial Results on (1, 2, 1, 2)-Avoiding GL(p, ℂ) × GL(q, ℂ)-Orbit Closures on GL(p+q, ℂ)/B
abstract: Using recent results of the second author which explicitly identify the “<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,2,1,2)$</tex>-avoiding” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}(p,{{ \BBC}}) \times {\rm GL}(q,{{ \BBC}})$</tex>-orbit closures on the flag manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}(p+q,{{ \BBC}})/B$</tex> as certain Richardson varieties, we give combinatorial criteria for determining smoothness, lci-ness, and Gorensteinness of such orbit closures. (In the case of smoothness, this gives a new proof of a theorem of W.M. McGovern.) Going a step further, we also describe a straightforward way to compute the singular locus, the non-lci locus, and the non-Gorenstein locus of any such orbit closure. We then describe a manifestly positive combinatorial formula for the Kazhdan–Lusztig–Vogan polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\tau ,\gamma }(q)$</tex> in the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> corresponds to the trivial local system on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,2,1,2)$</tex>-avoiding orbit closure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex> corresponds to the trivial local system on any orbit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q'$</tex> contained in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {Q}$</tex>. This combines the aforementioned result of the second author, results of Knutson et al., and a formula of Lascoux and Schützenberger which computes the ordinary (type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>) Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{x,w}(q)$</tex> whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w \in S_n$</tex> is cograssmannian.

articleTitle: On the Distribution of a Cotangent Sum
abstract: Maier and Rassias computed the moments and proved a distribution result for the cotangent sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${c}_0(a/q):=-\sum _{m \lt q} {m \over q}\cot ({\pi ma}/{q})$</tex> on average over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over 2} \lt A_0\leq a/q \lt A_1 \lt 1$</tex>, as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\rightarrow \infty$</tex>. We give a simple argument that recovers their results (with stronger error terms) and extends them to the full range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\leq a \lt q$</tex>. Moreover, we give a density result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${c}_0$</tex> and answer a question posed by Maier and Rassias on the growth of the moments of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${c}_0$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Polar Complex for Locally Free Sheaves
abstract: We construct the so-called polar complex for an arbitrary locally free sheaf on a smooth variety over a field of characteristic zero. This complex is built from logarithmic forms on all irreducible subvarieties with values in a locally free sheaf. We prove that cohomology groups of the polar complex are canonically isomorphic to the cohomology groups of the locally free sheaf. Relations of the polar complex with Rost's cycle modules, algebraic cycles, Cousin complex, and adelic complex are discussed. In particular, the polar complex is a subcomplex in the Cousin complex. One can say that the polar complex is a first-order pole part of the Cousin complex, providing a much smaller, but, in fact, quasiisomorphic subcomplex.

articleTitle: Toric Actions on b-Symplectic Manifolds
abstract: We study Hamiltonian actions on b-symplectic manifolds with a focus on the effective case of half the dimension of the manifold. In particular, we prove a Delzant-type theorem that classifies these manifolds using polytopes that reside in a certain enlarged and decorated version of the dual of the Lie algebra of the torus.

articleTitle: A Note on Logarithmic Growth Newton Polygons of p-Adic Differential Equations
abstract: In this paper, we answer a question due to Y. André related to B. Dwork's conjecture on a specialization of the logarithmic growth of solutions of p-adic linear differential equations. Precisely speaking, we explicitly construct a ∇-module M over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBQ}_p[\![X]\!]_0$</tex> of rank 2 such that the left endpoint of the special log-growth Newton polygon of M is strictly above the left endpoint of the generic log-growth Newton polygon of M.

articleTitle: Euclidean Minimal Tori with Planar Ends and Elliptic Solitons
abstract: A Euclidean minimal torus with planar ends gives rise to an immersed Willmore torus in the conformal 3-sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^3={\BBR}^3\cup \{\infty \}$</tex>. The class of Willmore tori obtained this way is given a spectral theoretic characterization as the class of Willmore tori with reducible spectral curve. A spectral curve of this type is necessarily the double of the spectral curve of an elliptic Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) soliton. The simplest possible examples of minimal tori with planar ends are related to 1-gap Lamé potentials, the simplest nontrivial algebro geometric Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) potentials. If one allows for translational periods, Riemann's “staircase” minimal surfaces appear as other examples related to 1-gap Lamé potentials.

articleTitle: Two Triangularity Results and Invariants of 𝔰𝔭((p + q), C), Sp(p, C) × Sp(q, C)) and (𝔰𝔬(2n, C), GL(n, C)) Modules
abstract: Fix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal O$</tex> a special nilpotent co-adjoint orbit and write <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\cal O)$</tex> for the group of components of the centralizer of an element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal O$</tex>. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bf 1$</tex> denotes the trivial representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(\cal O)$</tex>. The Springer correspondence attaches to the pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\cal O, \bf 1)$</tex> an irreducible representation of the Weyl group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> which we denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Sp}(\cal O)$</tex>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Sp}(\cal O)$</tex> admits two natural bases consisting of homogeneous polynomials on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Fraktur {h}}^*$</tex>. One of the bases is parametrized by a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {Prim}}_{\rho }(\cal O)$</tex>, consisting of certain primitive ideals of the universal enveloping algebra. The second basis consists of character polynomials, parametrized by a set of geometric objects. The relation between these bases encodes significant representation theoretical information. We study the change-of-basis matrix and derive consequences relevant to the computation of invariants of Harish-Chandra modules.

articleTitle: Q-Systems, Factorization Dynamics, and the Twist Automorphism
abstract: We provide a concrete realization of the cluster algebras associated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-systems as amalgamations of cluster structures on double Bruhat cells in simple algebraic groups. For nonsimply laced groups, this provides a cluster-algebraic formulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-systems of twisted type. It also yields a uniform proof of the discrete integrability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>-systems of different types by identifying them with the dynamics of factorization mappings on quotients of double Bruhat cells. On the double Bruhat cell itself, we find these dynamics are closely related to those of the Fomin–Zelevinsky twist map. This leads to an explicit formula expressing twisted cluster variables as Laurent monomials in the untwisted cluster variables obtained from the corresponding mutation sequence. This holds for Coxeter double Bruhat cells in any symmetrizable Kac–Moody group, and in affine type the factorization mapping is again an integrable mutation sequence.

articleTitle: Positive Representations of Split Real Quantum Groups: The Universal R Operator
abstract: The universal R operator for the positive representations of split real quantum groups is computed, generalizing the formula of compact quantum groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal U_q(\mathfrak g)$</tex> by Kirillov–Reshetikhin and Levendorskiĭ–Soibelman, and the formula in the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal U_{q\tilde q}(\mathfrak {sl}(2,\ \mathbb R))$</tex> by Faddeev, Kashaev, and Bytsko-Teschner. Several new functional relations of the quantum dilogarithm are obtained, generalizing the quantum exponential relations and the pentagon relations. The quantum Weyl element and Lusztig's isomorphism in the positive setting are also studied in detail. Finally, we introduce a C*-algebraic version of the split real quantum group in the language of multiplier Hopf algebras, and consequently the definition of R is made rigorous as the canonical element of the Drinfeld's double U of certain multiplier Hopf algebra Ub. Moreover, a ribbon structure is introduced for an extension of U.

articleTitle: Flow Monotonicity and Strichartz Inequalities
abstract: We identify complete monotonicity properties underlying a variety of well-known sharp Strichartz inequalities in euclidean space.
